title: Reflections on Thiele, Schur, and Continued Fractions
abstract: We survey several classical continued-fraction constructions from a common point of view centered on linear-fractional transformations, interpolation, and the recurrence relations they generate. Beginning with Thiele's interpolation algorithm, we trace how similar mechanisms reappear in the Schur algorithm, Wall's continued fractions, and multipoint Nevanlinna--Pick interpolation. Particular attention is paid to the emergence of $R_{II}$-type continued fractions, which arise naturally as even parts of Thiele continued fractions, and to the associated pencils of tridiagonal matrices. A detour through Euler's continued-fraction formula illustrates how rational Nevanlinna functions lead naturally to finite $R_{II}$-pencils, while the Schur algorithm is related to Wall pencils and, through a different reorganization, to CMV matrices. We also discuss a modified Schur transformation that removes an interpolation condition at a pair of symmetric points, which leads to a linear pencil of two Hermitian tridiagonal matrices. Finally, we indicate how periodically occurring interpolation nodes at infinity convert $R_{II}$-pencils into ordinary banded matrices, suggesting a connection with GMP matrices.

title: Archimedes' Angle Measure and The Fundamental Theorem of Trigonometry
abstract: We aim to understand a distant conversation about a trigonometric principle. Although foundational to calculus, this principle and the basic concept of angle measure are often treated tacitly in both elementary and advanced accounts. The primordial idea of counting rotations makes one aware of the integers. In the same vein, Archimedes' measure of partial rotations hints at the completeness of the real numbers. By a less well-known implication, these ideas also lead to the complex numbers and to the Fundamental Theorem of Trigonometry. What does it all mean? And is it true?

title: Condorcet's nontransitive dice: A minimal realization of a complete ranking profile
abstract: We construct three independent finite-support random variables whose six strict ordering probabilities reproduce the complete ranking-frequency profile in a classical example of Condorcet's paradox. The construction has total support size seven, and we prove that no realization of this profile has smaller total support size. Here dice are allowed to be weighted: different outcomes need not have equal probabilities. We then formulate the realization problem for an arbitrary vector of six ordering probabilities. We distinguish constraints on the pairwise comparison probabilities from constraints on the full ranking distribution and give an example showing that pairwise feasibility is not sufficient. For the fixed interlaced supports $\{1,4,7\}$, $\{2,5,8\}$, and $\{3,6,9\}$, we derive the polynomial realization system. On the branch where the smallest outcome of the second variable has probability zero, we give a compact polynomial characterization for profiles with their first two ordering probabilities positive. This yields an explicit semialgebraic sufficient condition for the general realization problem and a rational construction, both with elementary proofs.

title: Modeling fluid--solid interaction in three-dimensional granular systems: Two-way coupling of SPH and LS-DEM
abstract: This paper presents a two-way coupled fluid--solid interaction framework for granular systems based on the level-set discrete element method (LS-DEM) and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH). The proposed method is mesh-free, fully Lagrangian, and equipped with a seamless description of arbitrary solid shapes. In particular, a level-set representation of grain geometry is used for both contact detection and fluid--solid coupling, allowing for realistic, highly irregular grains to be handled within a unified computational framework. Moreover, the method incorporates a convenient treatment of moving boundaries and admits a simple computational implementation. The capabilities of the proposed SPH--LS-DEM framework are demonstrated through several numerical benchmarks involving dam-break flow, flow through porous media, granular collapse, and cyclic loading of a saturated granular specimen. The study sets the stage for several extensions to multiphysics problems across disciplines.

title: Compactifying the $G_2'$-Hitchin component via almost-complex curves
abstract: By studying limits of induced metrics of equivariant almost-complex curves in the pseudosphere $\mathbb{S}^{2,4}$, we compactify the $G_{2}'$-Hitchin component.

title: Protection Group of Colored Links
abstract: Colored links provide a mathematical framework for studying the topological stability and classification of three-dimensional topological vortex configurations. Earlier classifications in settings of physical interest relied on system-specific invariants. Here, we introduce a universal invariant of colored links, the \textit{protection group}, interpret earlier classification results as computations of this group, and compute it in new examples.

title: Narrower arithmetic progressions in the primes
abstract: For each fixed $k\geq 3$ and $δ> 0$, we prove that every subset of the primes up to $X$ of relative density at least $δ$ contains a non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression with common difference $O_{k,δ,\varepsilon}((\log X)^{k\cdot 2^{k-3}+\varepsilon})$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This improves the previous exponent $(k-1)2^{k-2}$. The main ingredient is a relative Szemerédi theorem for narrow progressions under weaker linear forms conditions.

title: On the local boundedness of weak solutions to doubly nonlinear equations with variable exponents
abstract: We establish local boundedness, together with quantitative estimates, for non-negative weak sub-solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear parabolic equations whose prototype is \[ (u^q)_t-\operatorname{div} \Big(|Du|^{p(x,t)-2}Du\Big)=0, \qquad p(x,t)>1,\quad q>0. \] The results are obtained under a logarithmic continuity condition on the variable exponent $p(x,t)$ and suitable relations between $q$ and the local bounds of $p(x,t)$. In certain ranges of the exponents, an additional local integrability assumption is required.

title: Symmetries of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology
abstract: We study the behavior of Manolescu's construction of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology under symmetries. Specifically, for k<n we construct a localization spectral sequence from the symplectic sl(n) homology of a knot to the direct sum of the symplectic sl(k) and sl(n-k) homologies of the same knot, giving a geometric analog of rank-reducing spectral sequences arising from deformations on the non-symplectic theory. We also prove the existence of a localization spectral sequence relating the symplectic Khovanov--Rozansky homology of a two-periodic link to the symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the quotient link, in analogy to a theorem of Seidel and Smith for symplectic Khovanov homology. The proofs rely on a generalization of the localization theorem of Seidel-Smith and Large for equivariant Lagrangian Floer cohomology with respect to order two actions; in particular, we extend the theory to the case that the fixed set of the action carries a stable normal real polarization.

title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
abstract: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.

title: Schatten and weak Schatten classes of composition operator differences on Bergman spaces
abstract: We investigate Schatten and weak Schatten class membership of differences of composition operators on the standard weighted Bergman spaces over the unit disk. We prove that the known sufficient condition for Schatten p-class membership is also necessary for 0<p<2, thereby completing the characterization for all p>0. We also characterize when differences of composition operators belong to weak Schatten classes for every p>0. Both results are expressed in terms of local-mass conditions involving the pseudohyperbolic distance between the inducing maps, and yield two-sided (quasi-)norm estimates.

title: Optimal Production Scheduling for Multi-Product Mineral Manufacturing
abstract: Short-term scheduling in multi-product mineral manufacturing requires coordinating material movement and production across interconnected processing stages while addressing confirmed customer orders and longer-term production requirements. This work develops a generalized network-based, lexicographic multi-objective optimization (MOO) scheduling framework for these systems. The formulation represents the progression of material from raw-material supply through production and inventory to customer fulfillment. A sequential objective hierarchy first prioritizes fulfillment of confirmed customer orders and then progressively directs feasible production capacity toward cumulative targets supplied by the facility's demand-planning process. This approach ensures that the performance achieved for each higher-priority objective is preserved before subsequent targets are considered. Selected product-line activation decisions are represented using generalized disjunctive programming (GDP). An industrial mineral-manufacturing case study demonstrates the proposed framework's ability to generate feasible shift-level schedules and preserve the intended operational priorities with practical computational performance.

title: Gumbel Fluctuations of the Maximum of the Airy$_1$ Process
abstract: We establish the Gumbel limit for the maximum of the Airy$_1$ process over $[0,N]$ as $N\to\infty$, with explicit centering of order $(\log N)^{2/3}$ and scale $(\log N)^{-1/3}$. The proof starts with a two-term expansion for the tail of the maximum over a fixed interval. Its leading term determines the centering, while the second term gives the joint-exceedance asymptotic for touching intervals. We then bound joint exceedances in separated unit intervals, uniformly over gaps up to a fixed multiple of the square root of the threshold. Covariance and mixing estimates control the larger gaps and complete the blocking argument.

title: Almost all vertex-transitive graphs and digraphs are Cayley
abstract: We prove that almost all vertex-transitive digraphs are Cayley digraphs, and that almost all vertex-transitive graphs are Cayley graphs, as the number of vertices tends to infinity through all positive integers. The proportions of Cayley objects are at least $1-2^{-n/4+o(n)}$ for digraphs and $1-2^{-n/24+o(n)}$ for graphs. This proves the McKay--Praeger conjecture and its digraph analogue.

title: Theta-Eta Mellin Transforms, Shifted Reflections, and Rigorous Approximation Theory for a Variant Theta Construction
abstract: We develop a rigorous analytic framework for investigating a proposed functional equation associated with a variant theta construction. We prove the classical Mellin identity connecting the Jacobi kernel $1-θ_4(0\mid ix^2)$ to the completed Dirichlet eta function, and extend its Mellin transform meromorphically to the whole plane with a single simple pole at the origin. Mellin uniqueness identifies $x^{3/8}(1-θ_4(0\mid ix^2))$ as the unique kernel in a natural weighted $L^1$ class whose Mellin transform is the shifted completed eta function. We distinguish this Gaussian kernel from the weighted exponential series $Θ^B(s)=\sum_{n\geq1}ne^{-ns}$, whose Mellin transform is $Γ(s)ζ(s-1)$ and obeys a different, explicitly derived reflection relation. We show that every affine reflection $s\mapsto c-s$ can be generated for a shifted completed eta or zeta function by choosing the shift appropriately; consequently, the occurrence of $\tfrac14-s$ alone cannot identify the original variant with a shifted eta function. The corrected analytic product defined here is an elementary meromorphic multiplier of the completed zeta function and therefore has a precise $1-s$ functional equation. We prove an explicit eta-tail bound, a sharper alternating-tail asymptotic, a uniformly convergent Euler-transformed eta series with a geometric error bound, a uniform zeta-approximation bound away from the line $\Re s=1$, and a combined truncation estimate when both the zeta and weighted-exponential factors are truncated. We also determine the principal Laurent data and the cancellation of the gamma poles at the trivial zeta zeros for the corrected product. Reproducible high-precision experiments verify the stated error scales. The exact identification of the original variant with a shifted completed eta function remains open.

title: Cohomology Rings of Fiber Products of Lefschetz Fibrations
abstract: We prove a Lefschetz-type theorem for the cohomology rings of fiber products of two Lefschetz fibrations with disjoint critical loci. As an application, we compute the Hodge numbers of several examples of higher-dimensional Schoen's Calabi-Yau manifolds.

title: Octahedrally and Icosahedrally Symmetric Solutions of the N-Vortex Problem on the Sphere
abstract: We investigate the octahedrally and icosahedrally symmetric solutions of the N-vortex problem on the sphere, for N = 24 and N = 60 respectively, in the case of equal vorticities. Exploiting the symmetries arising from rotations and permutations of the vortices, the problem is reduced to the analysis of a one-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian system on the sphere. The original contributions of this article concern the analysis of this reduced system yielding in particular a classification of the equilibrium and collision configurations with the prescribed symmetries. The computational complexity of the analysis is overcome by exploiting the associated discrete symmetries through the invariant theory of reflection groups and Palais' principle of symmetric criticality, and, in some cases, by resorting to numerical approximations.

title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders
abstract: We study extreme-value phenomena for random samples in partially ordered sets through their meets and joins, the order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. In this paper we consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. We analyse these extrema both at fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, identifying almost-sure collapse to the bottom or top elements and critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.

title: On regularity-free characterization of bisymmetric means
abstract: We prove that every reflexive, bisymmetric binary operation on a non-degenerate real interval that is strictly increasing in each variable is automatically continuous and is a weighted quasi-arithmetic mean. This settles the reflexive, strictly increasing case of the automatic-continuity problem without assuming symmetry. The proof constructs a symmetric mean as the unique fixed point of a natural increasing operation and then applies the known symmetric automatic-continuity theorem. Maksa's method, combined with an interpolation argument on a countable dense set, yields an exact characterization of operations of arbitrary finite arity, with uniquely determined positive weights.

title: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
abstract: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $π$. We show that $π^2 = p\,α_*$ for a unique automorphism $α$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius. For $p \ge 7$ this gives the list of Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points: eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on $p$, and its number 15, 3, 3, 7, 1, 1, 3 or 1 of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational $(2,2)$-kernels; when all Weierstrass points are rational, the 2-Tate pairing on $J[2]$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$. We then prove closed formulas, in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders and of $ζ_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt p)}(-1)$, for the mass of the curves of each type and for the mass of the rational kernels whose quotient is a product of elliptic curves. For $π^2 = \pm p$ the total masses are due to Ibukiyama and to Xue and Yu; our proofs use the 2-adic Tate modules, the symmetry of the Richelot correspondence and Eichler's mass formula, and, for the other curves, modules over orders of a quartic CM field. The kernels are counted through gluings of supersingular elliptic curves. As a consequence, the proportion of rational kernels with decomposed quotient is of order $p^{-1/2}(1+L(1,χ))$, where $χ$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$. All formulas agree with an exact enumeration for the 37 primes $7 \le p \le 173$. Finally we describe the graph of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational Richelot isogenies, which is far from connected in the range computed, and discuss what these results say about its use in isogeny-based cryptography.

title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
abstract: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to compute the coefficients. To illustrate the method, we compute the terms for the Virasoro extremal projector up to order 6. Furthermore, we formulate a conjecture for the denominators of the truncated extremal projector of the Virasoro algebra. We provide symbolic computational evidence up to order 6 and prove a weaker version of the conjecture.

title: Connectivity of Matroids with Breadth-Critical Tangles
abstract: We construct an explicit infinite sequence of nonnegative integers $(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ such that, for every $k\ge2$, every finite matroid with a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. The constants $s_i$ depend only on $i$. This proves a conjecture of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle.

title: Circular decompositions for hyperbolic genus one knots
abstract: We consider hyperbolic genus one knots having two or more non-isotopic, disjoint, genus one Seifert surfaces, with the property that the complementary regiones are handlebody pairs. We determine whether or not these knots have circular width equal to $(3)$. Moreover we give bounds on their circular widths. We also give explicit examples of such knots having three or five non-isotopic genus one Seifert surfaces and compute their circular widths. In particular this shows that many of these knots are non-almost fibered.

title: Conditional limit theorems in dynamical systems
abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems. We study the statistical properties of the dynamics within transient regimes by establishing a suite of limit theorems describing the behavior of trajectories under the condition that they remain outside a ``hole'', or region of no return. Under a spectral gap assumption for the associated open transfer operator, we first establish conditioning and Yaglom limits and identify the corresponding conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures. We then establish conditional exponential decay of correlations and the Strong Law of Large Numbers for both deterministic and quenched random systems. We also obtain a conditional Central Limit Theorem, Large Deviation Principle, and Berry--Esseen theorem, with additional assumptions in the quenched random case. We also derive standard (non-conditional) limit theorems on the surviving set of points that never enter the hole.

title: Theorems of the Alternative and Nonnegativity Certificates for Systems of Jensen-type Polynomials with Universal Quantifiers
abstract: We introduce Jensen-type polynomials, a class of possibly nonconvex polynomials that extends the Jensen inequality for SOS-convex polynomials while retaining natural sums of squares (SOS) certificates for nonnegativity. We show that polynomials with essentially nonpositive coefficients belong to this class and establish a composition principle that yields further examples, including componentwise univariate compositions and compositions with structured quadratic maps motivated by source-localization loss functions. We then derive theorems of the alternative that provide SOS certificates for infeasibility of systems of strict inequalities involving Jensen-type polynomials and universally quantified variables. We illustrate our results through two applications, with numerical examples. First, we show that source-localization problems admit an exact SOS reformulation under a simple dimension condition, and that an optimal solution can be recovered by solving a semidefinite program (SDP) and applying the explicit Jensen map. Second, our SOS certificates yield two {\it convergent} SDP hierarchies for semi-infinite optimization with Jensen-type polynomials, providing upper and lower bounds on the optimal value. We also establish finite-convergence and solution-extraction results, under flat truncation rank condition and the associated Jensen maps.

title: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
abstract: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jordán: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

title: Statistical robustness and time consistency in risk averse optimization
abstract: The aim of this manuscript is to investigate risk measures which are not necessarily convex. We show that law invariant coherent risk measures are not robust with respect to contamination of the probability measure, in the sense that an arbitrarily small contamination can change their values by an arbitrary amount. This contrasts with the Value-at-Risk, which is robust against such contamination. In addition, we show that for a given law invariant risk measure and a given policy, one can construct, under mild conditions, conditional risk measures with respect to which this policy is time consistent, in the frameworks of both Markov Decision Processes and Stochastic Optimal Control.

title: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
abstract: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

title: Quadratically Regularized Medians in Metric and Wasserstein Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of robust aggregators in Wasserstein spaces. After proving that all the commonly used Wasserstein barycenters are manipulable by one single corrupted input through a novel first-order optimality condition, we generalize both to the metric setting and to fractional exponents the concept of Lipschitz resilience introduced recently by Allouah, Guerraoui, Hoang and Villemaud. We proceed to show that adding a quadratic regularization to Wasserstein medians defined either in terms of the $W_1$-metric or linearized $W_2$-metric are resilient in that sense, by leveraging fine convexity estimates along generalized geodesics and flat interpolations. We finally show that iteratively solving the latter problem amounts to performing a Majorization-Minimization approximation of $W_2$-medians.

title: An explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations
abstract: We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval. Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions. Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Ait-Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler-Maruyama scheme.

title: Periodicity of Entire Solutions of $ff''=H^2$
abstract:
Let $f$ denote a transcendental entire function. The so called Yang's conjecture asserts that if for some integer $k$ ($\geq1$) the product $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic, then $f$ must be also periodic. In this paper, we prove that when $k=2$ for a given periodic transcendental entire function $H$, and $f$ is an entire solution of the equation $$ff''=H^2,$$
  then \(f\) must be periodic.

title: Unique-maximum colourings of planar graphs with respect to neighbourhoods
abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph by positive integers is a unique-maximum colouring with respect to open (resp. closed) neighbourhoods if the maximum colour appears exactly once in the open (resp. closed) neighbourhood of every vertex. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták (Discrete Appl. Math. 324 (2023) 80-92) conjectured that four colours suffice for closed neighbourhoods in planar graphs. We prove this conjecture by colouring a suitable independent dominating set with the three largest colours. They further conjectured that six colours suffice if the colouring is also proper. We disprove this conjecture by a planar graph which needs seven colours, and we show that seven colours always suffice. For open neighbourhoods, we show that eight colours suffice, even for proper colourings, which improves the previous bound of ten. In the proper case, our graph again needs seven colours. If the colouring need not be proper and the graph has no vertices of degree 2, then six colours suffice.

title: A Graph-Theoretic Framework for Identifying Mathematical Programming Decompositions
abstract: We develop a framework for identifying combinations of complicating variables and/or constraints that can be used to formulate mathematical programming decompositions. A mathematical program is represented by a graph which accounts for the structural and functional relationship between variables and constraints. Graph projections are used to focus on variable- or constraint-based decompositions. A series of coarsening operations is used to generate a reduced graph based on the original or projected graph. On the reduced graph, we use integer programming to identify different combinations of complicating variables and/or constraints. Specifically, variables and constraints are identified as complicating based on their structural role and/or their functionality (contribution to nonlinearity) in the mathematical program. The framework allows us to assess the viability of different decomposition types (variable, constraint, cross) and identify multiple potential decomposition formulations of the same type (e.g. different combinations of complicating variables for Benders decomposition). The systematic nature of our framework facilitates broader studies into the efficacy of different decompositions across a range of problems including energy markets, process design, and machine learning.

title: On counting integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in families of slant boxes
abstract: In this article, we develop an upper bound for the number of integral symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in a slant box with coefficients bounded by some given power of the volume of the slant box. We develop a counting method that expands on Shankar-Siad-Swaminathan's work on rank-3 integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant to higher-rank matrices using geometry-of-numbers methods and invariant theory on the splitting of quadratic forms associated with the determinant formula into corresponding linear forms. We expect this generalization will allow us to apply the counting results to arithmetic statistics frameworks. In forthcoming work, we will apply the counting results to study the distribution of 2-torsion subgroups of class groups of unit-monogenised number fields.

title: The Spectral Distribution of Matrix Least Squares Solutions, and the Ellipsoid Fitting Problem
abstract: We study the spectral distribution of the least squares solution to a random linear system whose unknown is a symmetric matrix. In the normalized and isotropic setting, we derive a closed-form description of the support of the spectral distribution. As an application, we consider the ellipsoid fitting problem: given $n$ standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$, does there exist a centered ellipsoid passing through all of them? It was recently shown that this problem has a sharp phase transition at $n \approx d^2/4$. On the satisfiability side, unlike earlier results, these sharp results do not rely on least squares candidates. We show that the least squares candidates considered in earlier works have a threshold of positive semi-definiteness at $n \approx d^2/10$, which was previously observed numerically and predicted non-rigorously using statistical physics methods. Moreover, we show that the corresponding least squares dual certificates have a threshold of positive definiteness at $n \approx 2d^2/5$. Our approach combines several matrix concentration tools. A key technical ingredient, which may be of independent interest, is showing that a certain kernel matrix is well-conditioned with high probability until $n \approx d^2/2$.

title: Joint extreme-value asymptotics for the radius and centre of smallest enclosing balls
abstract: We study the joint extreme-value behaviour of the radius and centre of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ spherically symmetric sample. In the Gumbel and Weibull regimes, we obtain joint limit theorems and show that the enclosing ball is asymptotically supported by exactly $d+1$ sample points, thereby resolving an open support problem in the Gumbel case. In the Fréchet regime, the limit is given by the smallest enclosing ball of an extremal Poisson cloud. For planar Gaussian samples, we derive an explicit joint limit law from Daniels' finite-sample formula and show that this law is universal throughout the planar Gumbel domain. In the bounded-support Weibull regime, we additionally obtain uniform tail bounds, moment convergence and an explicit limiting density, while the uniform-ball case admits an interpretation in terms of a Poisson zero cell.

title: Kernel Design in Particle Mesh Ewald Methods: Splitting, Interpolation, and Upsampling
abstract: For more than thirty years, particle mesh Ewald (PME) methods have dominated the computation of electrostatic interactions in molecular dynamics. A PME method uses a splitting kernel to divide the interaction into a local part, summed within a cutoff, and a smooth part, computed on a grid with a spreading and interpolation (SI) kernel. The established methods use Ewald's Gaussian split with B-spline SI kernels, and the recent Ewald summation with prolates accelerates them severalfold by using a prolate spheroidal wave function (PSWF) for both kernels. Neither choice meets two needs of molecular dynamics: a smooth energy, which long simulations need in order to conserve it, and a low-order SI kernel that stays accurate on coarse grids and gains accuracy as the grid is refined. We present a framework for designing both kernels to meet these needs. For inverse powers from the Coulomb to the dispersion interaction, our splits make the local part smooth at the cutoff to any order while keeping the Fourier concentration of the smooth part close to optimal. We show that with analytic differentiation, the force error of a continuous SI kernel of fixed shape vanishes under grid refinement only if every particle, wherever it lies, gives the grid its exact charge and dipole moment. Our SI kernel for the Coulomb interaction ensures this by construction and is twice continuously differentiable. Compared with the B-spline of the same order, it needs fewer grid points by a factor of up to nearly five; on coarse grids, it mostly needs a lower order than the PSWF kernel. In simulations of liquid water over 100 million time steps, the new kernels reduce the energy drift of both the established and the PSWF kernels by about three orders of magnitude, with a smaller force error than either. Existing PME codes can adopt them by replacing only the two kernels and the Fourier multiplier.

title: A Complete Classification of the One-Dimensional Nonlocal Eigenvalue Problem
abstract: We give a complete classification of the spectral stability of the following one-dimensional nonlocal eigenvalue problem (NLEP) $$ \partial_x^2φ-φ+pw^{p-1}φ-γ(p-1)\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^{r-1}φdx}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^r dx}w^p=λφ, $$ where $w$ is the unique positive even solution of $w''-w+w^p=0$ decaying at infinity, $p,r>1$, and $γ\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\Reγ\ge0$. This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. When $r<(p+3)/2$, the arcs open to the right, and the strictly stable region lies between them. Their common endpoint is $γ=1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ=γ_H>1$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$. In each case, the two arcs approach a common vertical asymptote. As an application, for real $γ\ge0$, the condition for strict spectral stability is $γ>1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ>γ_H$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$, where $γ_H>1$ is the value at which a conjugate pair of eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis. The key ingredient in determining how the number of eigenvalues in the open right half-plane changes at imaginary-axis crossings is a cumulative estimate for the mixed-sign spectral weights that arise for certain $p$ and $r$ with $1<p<3$ and $1<r<2$.

title: Drift-Aware Adaptive Semantic Codec Update Strategy for Dynamic Semantic Communications
abstract: Semantic communication reduces transmission overhead by conveying task-relevant semantic features, but its performance depends on the consistency between training and target-domain data distributions. In dynamic environments, distribution drift can make offline-trained semantic codec models stale and degrade transmission performance. Frequent updates alleviate this degradation but increase communication, computation, and queueing costs, whereas infrequent updates delay model adaptation. To address this tradeoff, we propose a drift-aware adaptive update strategy for dynamic semantic communication systems. Drift intensity is quantified in the semantic feature space, and Drift-Aware Age of Model (DA-AoM) is introduced to jointly capture drift-induced performance degradation, drift-dependent update service delay, and conventional update latency. Closed-form average DA-AoM expressions are derived for edge-layer M/M/1 and cloud-layer D/M/1 update scenarios, based on which the update frequency is optimized under the queueing-stability constraint. Simulations show that DA-AoM captures the joint effects of drift intensity, computing rate, bandwidth, and update frequency on model freshness beyond conventional Age of Information (AoI). The proposed strategy reduces average DA-AoM by 9.2\%--42.4\% compared with representative baselines under the same resource constraints.

title: Geography of Klein bottle Luttinger surgery
abstract: We propose and study a modification of Auroux's uniqueness question on Luttinger surgery by replacing Lagrangian tori with Klein bottles. In Kodaira dimension $-\infty$, we introduce two simple graphs whose connected components give bounds and, in several cases, exact counts of Klein bottle Luttinger equivalence classes. In Kodaira dimension zero, we provide examples of numerical invariants supporting infinitely many equivalence classes and prove a homological non-triviality theorem for Lagrangian Klein bottles in all symplectic Calabi--Yau surfaces with positive Euler characteristic. In positive Kodaira dimensions, we construct examples in which Klein bottle Luttinger surgery changes the symplectic Kodaira dimension.

title: The Kazdan-Warner equation on a finite graph with a Neumann boundary condition
abstract: We study the Kazdan-Warner equation $Δu = c - h \mathrm{e}^u$ on a finite connected domain $Ω$ of a locally finite graph, with Neumann boundary data $\partial u / \partialν= g$. We reduce the boundary condition to homogeneous form and use variational methods and upper and lower solutions to study solvability. Let $c_g \mathrel{:=} |Ω|^{-1}\int_{\partialΩ} g\, \mathrm{d}μ$, and let $ψ$ solve $Δψ= c_g$ with boundary data $\partialψ/ \partialν= g$ and zero mean on $Ω$. When $c = c_g$ and $h \not\equiv 0$, a solution exists if and only if $h$ changes sign and $\int_Ωh \mathrm{e}^ψ\, \mathrm{d}μ< 0$. When $c > c_g$, a solution exists if and only if $h$ is positive somewhere in $Ω$. When $c < c_g$, solvability requires $\int_Ωh \mathrm{e}^ψ\, \mathrm{d}μ< 0$. Under this condition there is a threshold $-\infty \le c_-(h) < c_g$ such that a solution exists for $c_-(h) < c < c_g$ and no solution exists for $c < c_-(h)$. If $h \le 0$ and $h \not\equiv 0$, a solution exists for every $c < c_g$.

title: Averting `Gravity': Launch Control and the Limits of Collision Avoidance in Low Earth Orbit Operations
abstract: As large constellations fill low Earth orbit, the risk of a runaway collision cascade has become a central concern of space operations. Debris population models treat collision avoidance as a fixed input, although the capacity to screen potential collisions and plan maneuvers degrades as debris accumulates. Using a stylized multi-layer queueing network model, we show that collision avoidance capabilities that saturate as the in-custody fragment count increases, can make the orbital shell bistable, with a low-debris and a high-debris equilibrium, and hysteretic. This has two major operational consequences. First, leaving the high-debris equilibrium requires a large cut in launch rates. Second, in the low-debris equilibrium, fragment counts respond with a delay as the launch rate rises past a tipping point. Removing bistability is desirable, and we show that fragment count-indexed admission control can achieve this. The least restrictive such policy lengthens the lag, whereas an exponential tilt of this policy makes the fragment count track its equilibrium with a bounded lag. Furthermore, admitting more launches can reduce the rate of completed missions, and under a unimodality condition a threshold rule on the debris fragment count maximizes this rate at equilibrium.

title: Irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on projective $k$-lattices and Frobenius numbers
abstract:
The irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ induces an action on the space $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of projective classes of rank $k$-discrete subgroups in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and every starting point in $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $2\leq k<n$, we prove convergence of the orbit averages over expanding norm balls and give a complete, explicit description of their limits.
  In an overview, every limit is supported on the subbundle over the unique compact $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit in the Grassmannian. The conditional measures on the fibers are either uniform on finite sets or convex combinations of at most two homogeneous measures associated with split simple subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}_k(\mathbb{R})$ containing the principal $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$.
  Another objective of our work is to relate weak-$*$ limits of probability measures on $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ supported on the projective classes of lattices orthogonal to integer vectors with limiting distributions of the corresponding normalized Frobenius numbers. This correspondence gives limit laws for vectors sampled from certain proper subvarieties, extending J. Marklof's work on sampling from full-dimensional domains. Specifically, together with our results for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ orbits in $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, this correspondence gives limit laws for primitive integer vectors sampled from $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbits. Using an earlier result of the first author and Shapira, we obtain analogous laws for integer vectors sampled on level sets of certain quadratic forms, as the level tends to infinity.

title: 3-Cube-Free Sets in Cyclic Groups
abstract: A set is called $3$-cube-free if it contains no configuration of the following form: $\{x,y,z,x+y,x+z,y+z,x+y+z\}$. We study the maximum density of $3$-cube-free sets in finite cyclic groups. As observed by Meng, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_m$ has size at most $2m/3$, and this bound is sharp whenever $3\mid m$. Our main result shows that there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every $m$ not divisible by $3$, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ has size at most $\left(2/3-\varepsilon\right)m$. Thus, in this setting, the natural $2/3$ barrier can be uniformly improved. Long and Wagner conjectured that every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_{2^n}$ has size at most $5\cdot 2^n/8$. We also establish this conjecture for 3-cube-free sets whose density in the layer of odd residues is at least $2/3$. Together with induction, this reduces the conjecture to the case where this density lies in $(5/8,2/3)$.

title: The Gini Index of an Integer Composition
abstract: We extend the discrete Gini statistic on integer partitions to integer compositions by rearranging the parts in decreasing order. Under the uniform distribution on the $2^{n-1}$ compositions of $n$, the resulting statistic has a rational ordinary generating function for its aggregate values, as well as a rational generating function for its second moments. More generally, the generating function of every fixed raw moment is rational, although the bivariate generating function encoding the entire distribution is not. We obtain an exact formula for the mean and prove that the variance of the unnormalized statistic is asymptotic to $10n^3/189$. The normalization used for partitions has mean tending to $2/3$, in contrast to the limit $1$ under uniform random partitions. Using the separator representation of a random composition and a renewal-reward argument, we prove a central limit theorem: its centered, normalized Gini statistic has asymptotic Gaussian fluctuations with variance constant $40/189$. We also prove that the ordinary classical Gini coefficient of the composition parts tends to $1/3$ and satisfies a central limit theorem with variance constant $20/189$.

title: Binomially Weighted Partition Statistics: Generating Functions, Asymptotics, and Dominance
abstract: For an integer partition $λ=(λ_1,λ_2,\ldots)$, we consider $M_m(λ)=\sum_{i\geq1}\binom{i+m}{m+1}λ_i$, where $m\geq0$. We prove conjugation and Frobenius-coordinate identities for this family and obtain its ordinary and bivariate generating functions. Differentiating the bivariate product gives exact formulas for the mean and variance under uniform sampling of partitions of $n$. For fixed $m$, we show that $\mathbb E[M_m]\simζ(m+3)(\sqrt{6n}/π)^{m+3}$ and determine an explicit positive constant multiplying $(\sqrt{6n}/π)^{2m+5}$ in the variance asymptotic. The family encompasses the row sum underlying the discrete Gini statistic and, after conjugation, a linear combination giving the Wiener index of starlike trees; the associated normalized statistics have contrasting limits under uniform random sampling. We also prove that every $M_m$ is strictly decreasing along the dominance order. Consequently its level sets are antichains, providing coefficient-based lower bounds for the width of the dominance lattice.

title: Optimal Control of RKHS Diffeomorphic Flows for Classification and Generative Modeling
abstract: We develop a unified optimal-control framework that solves supervised classification and likelihood-based density estimation with a single diffeomorphic flow whose velocity lives in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS); the two tasks share all structure except the objective. Variable projection eliminates the terminal model (a classifier, or a Gaussian-mixture (GMM) reference), leaving a reduced control problem whose gradient comes from an analytic discrete adjoint. The RKHS parameterization makes the flow's divergence exact and deterministic at the cost of one kernel matrix-vector product, avoiding the stochastic trace estimators and potential-flow restrictions of existing continuous normalizing flows. Because the objective and gradient are deterministic, matrix-free reduced Gauss-Newton (GN) and related second-order solvers are practical for both tasks, which we benchmark against a range of first- and second-order optimizers; the learned map is a diffeomorphism with explicitly controlled regularity. In experiments from dimension 2 to 256, the reduced GN solvers use the fewest iterations of any optimizer tested and, together with joint L-BFGS, the least work; a multiscale kernel improves the density fit, and a trainable GMM reference reduces the deformation needed for multimodal transport at comparable likelihood while lowering the likelihood on real data. The full-model solve is quadratic in the particle count and sub-linear in dimension; a control-point reduction makes the particle-count scaling linear at near-lossless accuracy.

title: Large entropy implies Hölder regularity on large sets
abstract: Let $F$ be a holomorphic endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}^k(\mathbb C)$ of algebraic degree $d\ge2$, with $k\ge1$. We prove that every ergodic $F$-invariant probability measure $μ$ of entropy strictly greater than $(k-1)\log d$ admits compact sets of $μ$-measure arbitrarily close to one on which the restrictions of $μ$ have Hölder continuous super-potentials. Consequently, $μ$ gives zero mass to every Borel pluripolar set.

title: Ramsey Theory for Edge Ideals
abstract: We initiate the study of Ramsey theory for edge ideals. The edge ideal I_G is generated by the monomials x_ux_v for all edges uv of G. A central invariant measuring structure in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra are the betti number beta_{i,j}(S/I) for some ideal I in a ring S. We prove the Ramsey Theorem for Edge Ideals: For any betti number indices i,j, and any number of colors m, there is a graph F such that for every m-coloring of the edges of F, there is a color l such that beta_{i,j}(S/I_{F_l}) >0, where F_l is the subgraph of F whose edges are in color l. Moreover, the number of vertices of F is at most jm^2.

title: Formalizing local gauge freedom via bi-equivariant groupoid algebras
abstract: Gauge degrees of freedom appear in many different contexts. Here, we describe their emergence in the context of architected metamaterials built from self-coupling blocks with internal symmetries. Quantifying the dynamics requires choices of local frames and the many available options constitute the local gauge degrees of freedom of the problem. In the absence of internal symmetries, the dynamical matrices generating the dynamics are all built from the left regular representation of a groupoid C*-algebra canonically associated to the architecture. If the resonators display internal symmetries, we show that the mentioned groupoid C*-algebra accepts a natural 2-action by the group of internal symmetries and that the local gauge freedom can be encoded in a bi-equivariant sub-groupoid algebra generated from the mentioned 2-action. The latter is shown to be the smallest C*-algebra containing all dynamical matrices that can be engineered in a laboratory, for a given architecture and discrete group of internal symmetries.

title: Minimal super dominating sets of maximum cardinality
abstract: Let $G = (V,E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ of vertices is a super dominating set if every vertex $v \in V - S$ has a neighbour $u \in S$, whose only neighbour in $V - S$ is $v$. A set $S \subseteq V$ is called open irredundant if every vertex $u \in S$ has at least one neighbour $v \in V - S$ whose only neighbour in $S$ is $u$. In this paper we establish connections between super dominating sets and open irredundant sets, similar to the connections that exist between dominating sets and irredundant sets. In particular, we define the new parameter $Γ_{sp}(G)$ as the maximum cardinality of a minimal super dominating set of $G$ and calculate $Γ_{sp}(G)$ for some families of graphs $G$. Finally we present some properties of open irredundant sets and we will develop Gallai theorems involving domination, super domination and open irredundance parameters of graphs.

title: Beyond Area: Perimeter Optimization in the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Problem
abstract:
The planar Skorokhod embedding problem asks for a simply connected planar domain whose Brownian exit distribution has a prescribed real marginal $μ$. We investigate the minimization of conformal perimeter over the class of all such embeddings.
  We first establish the main existence theorem showing that whenever a finite-perimeter embedding exists, the infimum is attained (and vice versa). We derive necessary conditions for finiteness and sufficient conditions based on logarithmic integrability of the density. In particular, we demonstrate that finite area does not guarantee the existence of an embedding with finite perimeter.
  Although Gross's canonical embedding minimizes area, we construct an explicit family of domains for which Brownian symmetrization strictly increases perimeter, disproving its universal perimeter minimality. On the positive side, using Pruss's containment theorem and inequalities from convex geometry, we establish a general lower bound in terms of the convex hull of the Gross domain. Consequently, whenever the Gross embedding is bounded and convex, it is the unique perimeter minimizer.
  Finally, we formulate an open problem concerning the relationship between the existence of finite-perimeter embeddings and the regularity of Gross's canonical embedding.

title: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
abstract: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

title: Classification of Forbidden 0-1 Patterns by Their Extremal Function
abstract: This paper concerns the maximum weight of $n\times n$ 0-1 matrices that avoid some pattern $P$, denoted $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)$. Furedi and Hajnal initiated a research program of classifying all patterns according to their extremal function, but to date, only the weight-4 patterns are completely understood. In this paper we make progress on several fronts of the classification problem. A pattern is light if its columns have weight 1 and linear if $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)=O(n)$. We characterize the set of weight-5 linear light patterns, and the set of weight-5 linear patterns more generally. Along the way we identify several new infinite classes of linear patterns, which support the Pettie-Tardos conjecture on characterizing all linear light patterns. It was known that there exist infinitely many minimally nonlinear patterns. We identify a specific infinite set of minimally nonlinear patterns. We also prove that there are $2^{Ω(r)}$ weight-$r$ minimally nonlinear patterns, and that every minimally nonlinear pattern has extremal function $O(n\log n)$, with the exception of the 4-cycle. We classify many of the outstanding weight-5 patterns according to their extremal function, leaving only a small set remaining. The newly classified weight-5 patterns have extremal function $Θ(n)$ or $Θ(nα(n))$. We also exhibit a large number of weight-6 patterns with extremal function $Θ(n\log n/\log\log n)$, which is notable in that this function had not been encountered before for any single pattern $P$, though it was known to be the correct extremal function for a pair of forbidden patterns.

title: Gram's law for moving targets of the Riemann zeta-function
abstract: We study the solutions of $ζ(s)=f(s)$ for targets $f$ that grow with $|s|$, and Gram's law for them: the statement that each shifted Gram interval contains exactly one solution. The deviation from Gram's law is an integer phase-slip counter, equal up to rounding to $-\frac{1}{2}S(t;x_c)$, where $S(t;x)=π^{-1}\argζ(x+it)$ and $x_c\approx 1/2+\log|f(it)|/\log t$ is a balance abscissa determined by the target. If $|f|\asymp t^κ$ with $κ>κ_1=0.5339\ldots$, where $\sum_p\arcsin(p^{-1/2-κ_1})=π$, and $\arg f$ converges, then every sufficiently high shifted Gram interval contains exactly one solution, which is simple; this localises the fixed points of $ζ$. The threshold is sharp: for $f=c(-s)^κ$ with $1/2<κ<κ_1$, Gram's law fails in $\asymp T$ intervals up to height $T$, and for $0<κ\le 1/2$ it fails infinitely often but with density zero. In both ranges the counter has an explicit limiting distribution. For targets growing more slowly than any power, such as $\log(-s)$, the solutions lie on average $(1+o(1))\log|f(iT)|/\log T$ to the left of the critical line. If $\log|f(iT)|/\sqrt{\log\log T}\to\infty$, the proportion of solutions to the right of the line tends to $0$, whereas for fixed targets Selberg conjectured a quarter, and the counting error at the shifted Gram points is asymptotically Gaussian with variance $(8π^2)^{-1}\log(\log T/\log|f(iT)|)+O(1)$. For $\log(-s)$ the solutions follow neither $θ(T)/π$ nor the zeros of $ζ$. All results are unconditional; numerical computations for $\log(-s)$ illustrate how slowly they take effect.

title: Error Analysis of Deep Learning
abstract: This review examines deep learning theory through the lens of error decomposition, systematically addressing approximation, statistical, and optimization errors. We trace the development of error analyses from bounds on individual error components to frameworks that account for all three. Using nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz Method as dual running examples, we demonstrate how these analyses apply across fundamentally different loss structures. We then review representative analyses in scientific machine learning, generative learning, reinforcement learning, representation learning, and large language models, showing how learning errors affect solutions, distributions, and predictions through problem-specific arguments. Throughout, we clarify which error components are controlled, how they are combined, and what assumptions are needed to obtain guarantees for trained networks.

title: Taylor coefficients and duality for finite multiple T-values
abstract: We express every normalized finite multiple $T$-value of positive even depth as the coefficient of $u^{p-1}$ in an explicit iterated integral built from $du$ and $du/\sinh u$. An analogous formula for odd-depth $S$-values, combined with reversal, gives a coefficient representation of $T_p(\mathbf{s})$ for every nonempty index $\mathbf{s}$. The coefficients involved are $p$-integral without a restriction on the weight. For indices $(\{1\}^{\ell},3,\{1\}^{m})$ with $\ell+m$ odd, we obtain an explicit Bernoulli convolution. It yields a prime-by-prime proof of $T_p(\{1\}^{\ell},3,\{1\}^{m})=T_p(\ell+1,1,m+1)$ for odd $\ell$, and the corresponding identity with an $S$-value for even $\ell$, whenever $p\ge5$ and $p>\ell+m+1$. This proves the finite assertion of the first family in Cheng and Zhao's duality conjecture. We also establish uniform depth-two identities, evaluate the boundary cases, and explain the obstruction to the same termwise argument for $(\{1\}^{\ell},4,\{1\}^{m})$.

title: Log-concavity for alternating Eulerian polynomials
abstract: Alternating Eulerian polynomials enumerate permutations by the alternating descent statistic introduced by Chebikin. We prove that their coefficient sequences are log-concave, verifying a conjecture of Lin, Ma, Wang and Wang. Our proof combines a factorization involving reciprocal quadratic factors, estimates for ordinary Eulerian zeros, and a log-concavity criterion for products of such factors. The required finite verifications use exact integer arithmetic. As applications, we obtain log-concavity for the distribution of $3$-descents, a local limit theorem for alternating descents, and bounds for the largest coefficient. We also give a Lorentzian reformulation of the main theorem.

title: Strong Structural Stability of Scalar-Plus-Compact Operators on Banach Spaces
abstract: We prove that every strongly structurally stable operator of the form \(λI+K\) on a real or complex Banach space, where \(λ\) is a scalar and \(K\) is compact, is hyperbolic. Applying this result to the real Banach space constructed by Argyros and Haydon and its complexification, both of which are infinite-dimensional separable Banach spaces with the scalar-plus-compact property, we show that neither space supports a nonhyperbolic and strongly structurally stable operator, thereby giving a negative answer to the part of the open problem of Bernardes and Messaoudi concerning strong structural stability.

title: Existence of SRB measures for some Rössler systems
abstract: We prove that for the Rössler system $\dot x=-(y+z)$, $\dot y=x+ay$, $\dot z=b+z(x-c)$ with $a=b=0.2$, the set of parameters $c$ within $6\cdot10^{-5}$ of the classical value $c=5.7$ for which the flow has a Hénon-like strange attractor supporting a Sinai--Ruelle--Bowen (SRB) measure has positive Lebesgue measure. The key step, proved with computer assistance, is that at a parameter localised in an explicit interval within $5.5\cdot10^{-5}$ of $5.7$ the period-one saddle of the Poincaré map has a quadratic homoclinic tangency that unfolds generically; the conclusion then follows from the theorems of Mora--Viana, Benedicks--Young and Benedicks--Viana. The same method gives two further such tangencies near $5.7$ and one at the band-merging parameter $c\approx4.507$. The proof reduces the generic-tangency conditions to finitely many inequalities, through explicit $C^2$ graph-transform bounds for the local invariant manifolds of a Poincaré map whose area contraction is of order $10^{-11}$--$10^{-14}$, and a scalar tangency function. The inequalities are checked with interval arithmetic in CAPD and re-checked with an independent implementation based on the Kv library; the analytic tangency criterion is formalised in Lean~4. Whether an SRB measure exists at $c=5.7$ itself remains open.

title: Riesz and Lusin type theorems in Choquet integral spaces: quasicontinuity and density of continuous functions for monotone measures
abstract: We study the approximation of measurable functions by continuous functions, in measure and with respect to the Choquet, Sugeno and Shilkret integrals, for monotone measures on metric spaces. For every monotone measure, quasicontinuous functions are limits of continuous functions in measure and in the Sugeno integral; for unbounded Choquet integrable functions this remains true under a small-set subadditivity condition or under null-additivity. Conversely, under property [S1] and an outer smallness condition, every such limit is quasicontinuous, and examples show that neither condition can be omitted. This extends to monotone measures a classical description of the closure of continuous functions in capacitary $L^1$-spaces. We characterize the indicator functions in this closure by a symmetric approximation property of sets, and we give criteria, involving regularity and order continuity, for the density of bounded continuous functions. As applications, we show that two approximation theorems of Cao with compactly supported functions fail on spaces which are not locally compact, we prove that, for a given finite, continuous, weakly null-additive measure on a separable metric space, their conclusions for convergence in measure, for the Sugeno integral and for the Choquet integral of bounded functions hold if and only if the measure is concentrated on the set of points having a compact neighbourhood (and, under null-additivity, also for unbounded Choquet integrable functions), and we prove corrected versions on locally compact spaces; we describe the closure explicitly for possibility measures; and we give a Lebesgue-null Cantor dust which shows, for all $n\ge1$ and $0<δ<n$, that continuous functions are not dense in the Choquet space of the dyadic Hausdorff content.

title: A counterexample to the Harper-norm silver-mean conjecture
abstract: The silver-mean conjecture formulated in Gerhold and Shalit 2022 states that the norm $E(α)$ of the Harper operator attains its minimum at the silver mean $α= \sqrt{2}-1$. We show that this conjecture is wrong by constructing an explicit rational point with a smaller Harper-norm value: $E(181/437)<2.591046794<E(\sqrt2-1)$. The separating decimal is an exact rational number. All acceptance checks use exact integer arithmetic with rigorously proved coefficient enclosures. No floating-point eigenvalue estimates or external witness data enter the certificate.

title: Spectral dimension reduction of dynamical systems on graphons
abstract: Spectral dimension reduction approximates a dynamical system on a large network by a low-dimensional system whose variables are weighted averages of the node states, with weights given by dominant eigenvectors of the network. Its effectiveness is closely related to the low-rank structure of the interaction matrix. We develop a graphon analogue of this reduction for dynamical systems on dense graph limits. For graphon dynamical systems, we formulate the reduction in terms of the compact self-adjoint integral operator associated with the graphon. This operator-theoretic setting gives a continuum analogue of the spectral/SVD-based framework used for finite networks: the eigenfunctions provide the reduction basis, and the decay of the corresponding singular values quantifies the effect of discarded modes. For finite-rank graphons, we prove exact reduction results for two classes of graphon dynamical systems. We also show that, for finite-rank graphons, the reduced system preserves equilibria, linear stability, and local bifurcations. For infinite-rank graphons, we derive error bounds for the spectral reduction. Numerical examples using finite-rank and infinite-rank graphons illustrate the exact and approximate regimes of the theory.

title: Spectral Stability and Convergence of the Unnormalized Graph Laplacian on Noisy Point Clouds
abstract: The first eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the unnormalized graph Laplacian of clean samples from a manifold, suitably scaled, approximate those of a weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator. However, the samples are usually observed with noise and therefore need not lie on the manifold. We build the clean and noisy graph Laplacians, with bandwidth $\varepsilon$, on the clean samples and on the noisy observations, where the noise is arbitrary but bounded by $δ$. We show that, with high probability, the first eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the noisy graph Laplacian are close to those of the clean one: the eigenvalues within $O(δ/\varepsilon)$, and the subspaces spanned by the first eigenvectors within $O(\sqrt{δ/\varepsilon})$, whether or not the eigenvalues are simple. Consequently, if $δ$ is small enough relative to $\varepsilon$, the noisy graph Laplacian approximates the weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator at the same rate as the clean one. We also show that, for large noise, we can get the same rate as the clean graph Laplacian by first using a denoiser, and then building the graph Laplacian on the denoised observations.

title: The Double Entropy Fit Index (DEFI): An Information-Theoretic Approach to Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering
abstract: We introduce the Double-Entropy Fit Index (DEFI), a regularized information-theoretic criterion for selecting among candidate graph partitions and reduced representations. DEFI couples entropy-based compression with relevance preservation and penalizes model dimensionality, cluster imbalance, and partition fragmentation. An exact Rényi-2 entropy identity shows that partitioning alters both spectral concentration and graph-volume normalization, explaining why unregularized entropy minimization can favor degenerate solutions. Across a 243-condition population-analytic factor recovery benchmark, DEFI achieved an overall exact recovery rate of 97.2\% (versus 75.0\% for EGA-TMFG, 45.8\% for TEFI on von Neumann entropy). In controlled local candidate batteries (distinguishing the true model from adjacent $K \pm 1$ and factor-split alternatives), DEFI identified the correct partition in 99.2\% of replications. Across ten clustering benchmarks, DEFI-guided Gaussian mixtures achieved a mean ARI of 0.929, exceeding HDBSCAN (0.809), Ward clustering (0.700), and conventional GMM criteria (0.501-0.580), with gains concentrating where standard criteria over-extract components.

title: Twisting and foam inequalities for the upsilon invariant
abstract: We describe two families of bounds on the Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó invariant $Υ_K(t)$, one controlling its behavior under inserting full twists into a knot and one controlling a limited class of foams, or singular cobordisms between knots. By constructing certain explicit foams, we show that these two formal properties of $Υ$ together exactly determine $Υ_K(t)$ for all torus knots. This generalizes previously observed behavior at $t = 0$, Livingston's slice-torus invariants, and at $t=1$, Sato's unoriented analogue. Our foam bounds on $Υ$ make significant use of Alishahi's generalization of $Υ$ to knotted graphs. Along the way we compute Alishahi's invariant for all theta-graphs lying on the Heegaard torus in $S^3$. We also relate the evaluations of $Υ$ for torus theta-graphs to a distinguished family of properly embedded 2-complexes in the 4-ball sharing many properties with Batson's surfaces.

title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $λ$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $Δ^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.

title: Minimax estimation for simultaneous deconvolution model in random design using wavelets
abstract: Simultaneous deconvolution model is investigated when the design points are random and follow bounded densities and errors are either $i.i.d.$ or long-memory dependent. We propose wavelet hard-thresholding estimators, and show that they achieve asymptotically near-optimal convergence rates for the $L^2$-risk when the response function belongs to Besov space under both $i.i.d.$ errors and homoskedastic, long-memory errors. However, under heteroskedastic, long-memory errors the estimator is not optimal. For the $i.i.d.$ errors, the convergence rates are {identical} to those found in simultaneous deconvolution under regular design {and $i.i.d.$ errors}. However, for long-memory dependent errors, the convergence rates are new {and completely different from those in simultaneous deconvolution under regular design and long-memory errors}.

title: Evergreen leaves and universal lifetime laws in preferential-attachment trees
abstract: We study leaf lifetimes in general preferential-attachment trees. First we characterize the existence of evergreen leaves, that is, vertices that remain leaves forever. When no evergreen leaves exist, we establish, for a broad class of attachment functions, a remarkable one-parameter universality: the normalizations and limiting laws for various characteristics of leaf lifetimes depend on the attachment function only through a single numerical parameter. In particular, we obtain a shifted Pareto limit law for individual lifetimes and a joint functional limit theorem for the lifetime and label of the longest-lasting leaf. The limiting two-dimensional process, which we call the beta-decorated Fréchet extremal process, admits an elegant representation in terms of the Stoev--Taqqu extremal integral and the sets of optimal choices considered by Molchanov and Strokorb. We also establish a Poisson point-process limit for rescaled leaf lifetimes and corresponding labels, a finiteness criterion for long-lasting leaves, and a functional central limit theorem for their number at the critical threshold.

title: A Study of Fixed versus Adaptive Step Sizes for Phasor Dynamics Simulations
abstract: Transient phasor dynamics simulations model the response of power systems to disturbances using differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). Fixed-step integration is widely used to solve these DAEs numerically, but a step size suitable for resolving a fault transient may be unnecessarily small during the rest of a simulation. In this work, we provide a quantitative comparison of fixed and adaptive backward differentiation formulas on a suite of seven grid test cases ranging from 200 to 70,000 buses. Adaptive step sizes automatically shrink near faults, perturbations, and controller limits, and grow during less active portions of the simulation. At the global error achieved by a fixed quarter-cycle step size, adaptive results give 1.8 to 2.6 times speedups. Local error distributions, step size profiles, and work-precision plots show how accuracy, nonlinear solver, and step selection contribute to these differences. The results establish adaptive integration as the preferred approach for these simulations.

title: Non-principality of forbidden subposet problems
abstract: We show pairs of posets such that the largest families not containing any of them is substantially smaller than the largest families avoiding only one of them.

title: Numerical approximation of Benjamin-Ono type models for two-dimensional internal waves
abstract: In this paper we analyze the numerical approximation with spectral methods of two asymptotic models for the two-dimensional propagation of internal waves in a two-layer system of fluids with rigid-lid condition. The semidiscretization in space of the periodic initial-value problem with the spectral Fourier-Galerkin method is introduced and some error estimates are derived. Then the semidiscrete system is integrated in time with the Implicit Midpoint Rule and several numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the corresponding full discretization.

title: Conjugate Power Series of Ultralogarithm Branches
abstract: We investigate multivalued solutions of the transcendental ultralogarithm equation $e^{aw} = 1 + a x e^{bw}$ for arbitrary real parameters $a > b > 0$. A sector-based conjugation criterion is formulated and rigorously proved, reducing the technical two-dimensional indexing of conjugate master-series expansions inside ($|x| < R$) and outside ($|x| > R$) the disk of convergence to a unified one-dimensional branch index $n \in Z$. For integer exponents, a logarithmic analog of Vieta's theorem is established. Using multi-channel phase hodographs, we analyze branch evolution across integer, fractional, and transcendental incommensurable ($a = π$, $b = e$) exponents. It is demonstrated that logarithmic stratification eliminates branch cuts of fractional powers, ensuring global stability of iterative root refinement near branch points without auxiliary sheet-selection parameters. Finally, using the Sagdeev pseudopotential method in plasma physics, we confirm the continuous preservation of branch numbering in the Lambert $W$ limit and the physical invariance of the indices $n = 0$ (subsonic regime) and $n = -1$ (supersonic regime).

title: How random are affine maps over finite cyclic groups and generalized cyclotomic permutations over finite fields?
abstract: We analyze the dynamical behavior of affine permutations over the ring $\mathbb{Z}_{p^e}$ and generalized cyclotomic permutations (GCPs) over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We use the description of their functional graphs to determine two statistical parameters: the expected number of cycles and the expected length of a cycle that contains a random element. We obtain explicit closed-form expressions for both expectations and an exact reduction from GCPs to affine permutations. We compare these parameters with the corresponding expectations for random permutations, to determine how closely the cycle statistics of each family resemble those of random permutations.

title: Longitudinal Subdivision Invariance of Periodic Directed Strips and Its Application to Elongated Octagonal Strips
abstract: We prove that longitudinal refinements of finite-width periodic directed strips preserve subdivision containment. The refinement lengths may be arbitrary positive integers, without a uniform upper bound, and no matching condition is imposed on the horizontal arcs. We construct subdivision models in both directions that preserve each designated rail as a whole. The equivalence also holds when the designated rail images are required to lie in a prescribed end. A nonperiodic example shows that reverse containment may fail without periodicity. As an application, we obtain an elongated octagonal strip $O_n$ by subdividing selected longitudinal arcs of the directed hexagonal strip $H_n$. We show that every bounded face of $O_n$ is an octagon for $n\geq 2$ and that $O_n$ and $H_n$ are subdivision-equivalent. Consequently, the known exact end in-degree thresholds and forced-width formula for $H_n$ also hold for $O_n$.

title: Local connectivity of friends-and-strangers graphs with a star
abstract: Given two finite simple graphs $X$ and $Y$ with the same number of vertices, the vertex set of the friends-and-strangers graph $\FS(X,Y)$ consists of all bijections from the vertices of $X$ to the vertices of $Y$. Two bijections are adjacent exactly when one is obtained from the other by swapping the images of two adjacent vertices of $X$, while leaving all other images unchanged, and the two swapped images are adjacent in $Y$. For $n\ge2$, let $\Star_n$ be the star on $n$ vertices. Krishnan and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 33 (2026), no. 3, Paper P3.41] conjectured that, for $n\ge3$, whenever $\FS(X,\Star_n)$ is connected, the maximum number of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths between any two distinct vertices is equal to the smaller of their degrees. We prove this conjecture. More precisely, if $\FS(X,\Star_n)$ is connected, then $X$ must be $2$-connected, and the conjectured equality holds for every pair of distinct vertices. We further prove the stronger result that, whenever $X$ is $2$-connected, the same equality holds in every connected component of $\FS(X,\Star_n)$.

title: Structure-Preserving Universal Differential Equations for Epidemic Dynamics
abstract: Universal differential equations (UDEs) combine mechanistic epidemic models with learned neural closures, but generic additive corrections may violate essential epidemiological properties. We introduce a class of structure-preserving epidemic UDEs in which learned closures parameterize intercompartmental fluxes and the force of infection factorizes through infected compartments. This architecture guarantees positivity, population boundedness, and invariance of the disease-free set. We derive a rank-one next-generation matrix and a closed-form basic reproduction number determined by the learned rates at the disease-free equilibrium. Under explicit conditions, we establish results on threshold dynamics, disease-free and endemic equilibria, stability, and uniform persistence. For a neural SEIR model, center manifold analysis characterizes the direction of bifurcation through derivatives of the learned transmission rate. We further establish fundamental identifiability limitations: closures that agree on observed epidemic trajectories can yield different reproduction numbers and bifurcation types. Quantitative bounds relate uncertainty in the reproduction number to closure regularity and the distance of observations from the disease-free equilibrium, while monotonicity provides one-sided bounds. A numerical example involving three closures illustrates these results.
