Our findings provide a rigorous framework for epidemiologically consistent scientific machine learning and clarify which dynamical properties can be recovered from epidemic data.

title: A Topologist's Proof of Krasnosel'skii's Bifurcation Theorem
abstract: This note offers a proof of Krasnosel'skii's bifurcation theorem that bypasses the traditional machinery of nonlinear analysis: neither the Leray-Schauder degree nor the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction is used. The argument rests only on elementary operator theory and straightforward vector-bundle topology, providing a topologist's perspective on a classical result in nonlinear functional analysis.

title: Hessian--Maslov Geometry of Oja--Brockett Flows
abstract: This paper is organized in three parts. Part I develops the theoretical foundations of the Maslov index for caustics of the Legendre map, covering its semiclassical origin, geometric formulation as an intersection number in the Lagrangian Grassmannian, Hormander's local formula, and the dynamical viewpoint of bifurcating fixed points of a gradient flow. The theory is illustrated on the two-dimensional vector-valued quartic potential, whose caustic is a cusp and whose minima and saddles exchange stability when the eigenvalue ratio crosses 1. Part II lifts the setting to tall n x k matrices and introduces the potential f(X) = -1/2 tr(A^2 X B^2 X^T) + 1/4 tr[(A X B X^T)^2]. Numerical evidence confirms that fixed points of the associated negative gradient flow realize Brockett's sorting theorem. When eigenvalues of A or B degenerate, the fixed-point set expands into a flag manifold; crossing a Weyl wall produces Hessian degeneracy and an exchange of sort order. These phenomena are identified with the Maslov cycle, showing that combinatorial inversion numbers (Coxeter length) and the differential-geometric Maslov index are two faces of the same wall-crossing. Part III supplies the rigorous analysis underlying Part II. The ambient Hessian of the general Oja-Brockett flow dot{X} = A X B - X B X^T A X is completely decomposed into normal, vertical and horizontal sectors, and closed spectral formulas depending on both SPD matrices A and B are derived. In particular, the formula mu^V_{ij} = (lambda_i - lambda_j)(b_i - b_j) reveals a second, dual wall system (the B-wall) that is independent of the classical Weyl wall of A. Under this double-wall structure a genuine eigenvalue crossing becomes an avoided crossing; the associated horizontal and vertical coupling constants are given in closed form.

title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
abstract:
We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces.
  As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

title: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
abstract: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.

title: Convergence of the big J-function of a GKM manifold
abstract: The genus-$0$ equivariant Gromov--Witten (GW) invariants of a GKM manifold can be computed recursively by a recursion discovered by Brown and studied further by Coates--Corti--Iritani--Tseng. In this paper, we prove a slightly modified version of this result by realizing the J-function as a solution to a fixed-point problem. As an application, we prove that both the equivariant and the non-equivariant quantum cohomologies of a GKM manifold are convergent. We also show that the equivariant central charges have no poles in the spectral parameter, compute their monodromy and their asymptotics at $z=0$, and formulate an equivariant mirror symmetry conjecture for GKM manifolds.

title: Multiple transition points for an epidemic model
abstract: This paper is concerned with a spatial epidemic model on the $d$-dimensional square lattice that extends the contact process in two ways by assuming that each site is occupied by a social cluster of $N$ individuals rather than a single individual, and that infected individuals can be either asymptomatic or symptomatic. Newly infected individuals begin as asymptomatic and develop the symptoms at a spontaneous mutation rate $γ$, and all infected individuals recover at rate one. The model also distinguishes between external (between adjacent clusters) and internal (within clusters) infection rates for each state. Our analysis shows that, when either asymptomatic or symptomatic individuals only spread the disease externally and at a subcritical rate, while the other class only transmits the disease internally and at a large rate, the system exhibits at least two phase transitions with respect to the mutation rate $γ$ when social clusters are large. Specifically, the epidemic dies out for extreme values but survives for intermediate values of the mutation rate.

title: Federated Differential Privacy with Batch Contamination
abstract: We study mean estimation under federated differential privacy (FDP) constraints and batch contamination, considering both Gaussian and heavy-tailed distributions. In the homogeneous setting, where sample sizes and privacy budgets are constant across servers, we show that the costs of privacy and contamination disentangle. Under a bounded $v$th moment condition, with $v \in (1, \infty)$, the cost of batch contamination is of order $(\varepsilon/n)^{2-2/v}\vee \varepsilon^2/n$, where $\varepsilon$ is the contamination level and $n$ is the per-batch sample size. This reveals a phase transition at $\varepsilon\asymp n^{1-v/2}$, for $v > 2$, which is the first of its kind in the literature. We develop a two-stage procedure that achieves the minimax rate up to poly-logarithmic factors. A key component is a private smoothed voting procedure tailored to the FDP setting that provides optimal sensitivity control. For heterogeneous batch sample sizes and privacy budgets, we introduce a batch partitioning framework that groups batches with comparable per-batch sample sizes and privacy budgets. Surprisingly, the minimax rate is determined, up to poly-logarithmic factors, by the most informative group of batches. Consequently, in some regimes, it is minimax optimal to use only an arbitrarily small proportion of the data set. Heterogeneity also introduces interactions between the costs of privacy and contamination, in contrast to their disentanglement in the homogeneous setting. For unknown contamination level, we propose an adaptive, near-minimax optimal Lepski-type extension for the heterogeneous Gaussian setting, designed specifically to prevent privacy leakage by ensuring no repeated use of data points.

title: A Feasible-Domain Reduction Approach with Objective-Loss Guarantees for Multilevel Multiobjective Linear Programming
abstract: In some approaches to decentralized multilevel multiobjective programming, each decision-maker selects a compromise and restricts the feasible region before passing the decision to the next level. However, these restrictions do not necessarily limit the deterioration of objective values at preceding levels. This paper studies how to choose variable bounds that keep such losses within prescribed tolerances. We establish exact conditions using linear programming duality and derive simpler bounds based on objective coefficients. We also examine the choice of restriction widths and establish guarantees for successive reductions. A two-level numerical example illustrates the results and the influence of tolerances on the final compromise.

title: Norm Approximation with Linear Growth of Error for Bosonic Dynamics in the Mean-Field Regime
abstract: We consider the quantum many-body dynamics of a homogeneous confined Bose gas in three dimensions in the mean-field scaling regime. We study the Cauchy problem for a class of initial data describing finitely many excitations over a Bose-Einstein condensate. Using a rigorous version of Bogolyubov's theory, we prove that the many-body evolution can be approximated in Fock space norm by a quasifree evolution of the excitations with an error which grows linearly in time. In distinction from earlier results, the slow growth in time holds even though the effective equation is not dispersive.

title: Antidirected paths on five vertices in 5-chromatic digraphs
abstract: We prove that every 5-chromatic digraph containing no copy of the regular tournament on five vertices contains both antidirected paths on five vertices. This answers a question posed by El Sahili in 2004. The proof uses an edge bound for 5-critical graphs to constrain the out-degrees in a counterexample and obtain a contradiction by constructing a proper 4-colouring.

title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
abstract: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erdős (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $Ω(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstraëte (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erdős in a stronger form. It is natural to consider the size of the circuit spectra of binary matroids. Murty (1971) characterized all connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size one. Lemos et al. (2011) characterized the connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size two, where the largest size is odd. For general binary matroids, it is still an open question to find a lower bound for the size of the circuit spectra. In this paper, we give best-possible such lower bounds for connected binary matroids that do not contain both the Fano matroid and its dual as minors. Let $M$ be a simple connected binary matroid that does not have both the Fano matroid and its dual as a minor, and $d\geq 3$ be the minimum cocircuit size of $M$. We prove that (1) for each element $e$ of $M$, the circuit $e$-spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-2$. This bound is best possible. (2) The circuit spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-1$, unless $M\cong F_7,F_7^*,R_{10}$. In exceptional cases, the spectrum of $M$ has size equal to $d-2$.

title: Fibrations and nilpotent collapsing structure
abstract:
We construct fiber bundles, singular fibrations, and nilpotent collapsing structures for Riemannian manifolds with lower Ricci curvature bounds under additional geometric assumptions.
  For every $n$ and $D>0$, there exists $ε(n,D)>0$ such that a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold $M$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{diam}(M)\le D,\qquad \operatorname{sec}_M\ge-1,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_M\ge-ε(n,D) \] admits a finite cover of degree at most $C(n)$ that is a smooth fiber bundle over a nilmanifold. The fibers have finite fundamental group, and the base dimension equals the Hirsch rank of $π_1(M)$. If $π_1(M)$ is torsion-free, then $M$ itself fibers smoothly over an infranilmanifold with simply connected fibers.
  We next consider a Gromov--Hausdorff convergent sequence $M_i\to X$ of closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds with uniformly bounded diameter, $\operatorname{Ric}_{M_i}\ge -(n-1)$, and the $(ρ,δ)$ local rewinding Reifenberg condition, where $ρ>0$ is fixed and $δ$ is sufficiently small. For all sufficiently large $i$, we construct singular fibrations $\bar{F}_i:M_i\to X$ that are $ε_i$-Gromov--Hausdorff approximations, with $ε_i\to0$, and whose fibers are homeomorphic to infranilmanifolds. Under the same local hypotheses, complete, possibly noncompact manifolds admit nilpotent collapsing structures on their $ε(n,ρ)$-collapsed regions.

title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
abstract: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$. It controls, in a range of degrees, the restriction of natural transformations $\mathrm{id}\to F$ to the orthogonal complement of the collection, and it is computed from the collection by a finite complex. For collections of line bundles on surfaces whose Hom divisors have nonnegative canonical degree, the tensor product with a skyscraper sheaf has height exactly two, and the projections of skyscraper sheaves form a two-dimensional family of point-like objects in the orthogonal complement. We apply these tools to Orlov's rationality conjecture. A smooth projective complex surface is rational if its derived category has a full exceptional collection in which all members except possibly one are line bundles, or one that consists of at most three completely orthogonal blocks of arbitrary objects; we also obtain rationality in several cases with four blocks or with a hereditary component. If $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of the form $(M_i\boxtimes\mathcal O(a_i))$, then the $M_i$ with relative degrees of a fixed parity form a full exceptional collection on $S$; consequently $S$ is rational whenever $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. Finally, we show that the general case of the conjecture for surfaces is equivalent to the surjectivity and injectivity of two maps in Hochschild cohomology.

title: Degree-three Euclidean spanning trees within a factor of 1.514 of the minimum
abstract: For every finite point set $X$ in a Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, we prove that there is a spanning tree of maximum degree three and total length at most $(757/500)\MST(X)=1.514\MST(X)$, where $\MST(X)$ denotes the unrestricted minimum spanning-tree length. More strongly, for any root and any finite list of other points, there is a Hamiltonian path starting at the root whose length is at most $1.514$ times the sum of the root-to-point distances. The proof follows the rooted-path and variable-block framework used in earlier work, and applies Young's weighted-distance inequality to explicit rational mixtures of paths. Eight ordered radius regions cover the normalized domain. Their local estimates require only 29 vertex comparisons, all certified by rational arithmetic. The cover uses the three thresholds $1/4$, $3/8$, and $1/2$; its largest block has nine vertices. We give complete proofs of the normalization transfer, the global induction, and the terminal cases with zero or one actual tail point. We also give a fixed-dimensional cross-polytope lower bound, present Zbarsky's orthogonal simplex-cluster construction in explicit coordinates, and compare their finite-dimension bounds. The base cases complete the upper-bound argument before the lower-bound constructions are presented.

title: 2-Walk-regular graphs with $k_2$ at most twice the valency
abstract: In this paper, we characterize $2$-walk-regular graphs with valency $k$, diameter at least four and $k_2\leq 2k$, generalizing a result of Koolen and Park, and classify the distance-regular graphs satisfying these conditions. We also classify $2$-walk-regular graphs with valency $k$, diameter at least four and at most $4k+4$ vertices.

title: Linear Connectivity of Boundaries of Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
abstract:
To every right-angled Coxeter group one can canonically associate a hyperbolic metric space, called its maximized hyperbolic space. This space is Morse recognizing and is obtained from the Davis complex by coning off its standard product regions. We characterize, purely in terms of the defining graph, when the Gromov boundary of a maximized hyperbolic space is nonempty and linearly connected.
  As an application, we prove that among one-ended right-angled Coxeter groups, splitting over a subgroup of an unbounded product subgroup is a quasi-isometry invariant. We also establish several features shared by maximized hyperbolic spaces and curve graphs, including the existence of dead ends and visibility of boundaries. Moreover, when the boundary is nonempty, it is non-compact if and only if the defining graph contains an induced 4-cycle.

title: Wei-Norman Factorization of Frenet-Serret equations and the Cardan Lock
abstract: Frenet-Serret equations for particles moving along differentiable curves, in the case of non-constant curvature and torsion, are considered in the framework of the Wei-Norman factorization of the propagator using the Lie algebra of the rotation group. It leads to a system of coupled linear equations that are highly coupled if Euler or Cardan angles are used, but that can be uncoupled if the Cartan basis in the Lie algebra is used, resulting essentially in a Ricatti equation. However, since the rotations algebra is not a solvable algebra, the global Wei-Norman Theorem does not apply and singularities in the solutions of the system of equations appear at certain points, related to the \text{gimbal o Cardan lock}. Notwidthstanding, a detailed study of the limit at these points shows that in most of the cases the propagator is well defined and gimbal lock is avoided.

title: From Persistent Cohomology to Maps into Arbitrary Eilenberg-MacLane Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we address the construction of Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates (functions from datasets to Eilenberg-MacLane spaces $K(G,n)$) that encode nontrivial persistent cohomology classes in arbitrary dimensions $n$ and coefficient group $G$. The construction leverages the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence in Čech cohomology, from the short exact sequence of sheaves of continuous maps with values in $G$, $EG$ and $BG$. Crucially, the derivation is constructive: we give an explicit, recursive formula for preimages under the connecting homomorphism, which yields a constructive version of a classical cohomology vanishing theorem and, in turn, an algorithm for general Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates. We validate our approach through experiments on synthetic datasets, and present novel examples of $K(\mathbb{Z}/2, 2)$-coordinates not addressed in prior work.

title: An Explicit Construction of Large Families of MSTD Sets
abstract: A finite set $S\subset\mathbb Z$ is more sums than differences (MSTD) if $|S+S|>|S-S|$. Yufei Zhao's bidirectional-ballot construction gives $Θ(2^N/N)$ MSTD subsets of $[0,N-1]$, the best previously known size bound for an explicit family, to the author's knowledge. We improve this bound: for every fixed integer $T\geq1$, we construct a family of $Θ_T(2^N/(\log_2^{\circ T} N)^{2^T})$ MSTD subsets, where $\log_2^{\circ T}$ denotes the $T$-fold iterated logarithm. This family is asymptotically larger than Zhao's for every fixed $T\geq1$. A subfamily of the same order of magnitude can be numbered so that any chosen member can be generated deterministically in time polynomial in $N$, without listing preceding members. As a supplementary comparison, replacing the terminal ballot rule by exhaustive fringe search gives a positive-proportion family with the same polynomial-time generation property.

title: Computing with Orientation-Dependent Vector Fields in Crystallographic Texture Analysis
abstract:
We present a computational framework for representing orientation-dependent vector fields. Building on (arXiv:2608.21235), we translate the differential-geometric formulation into crystallographic notation and focus on its computational use in crystallographic texture analysis.
  In crystallographic applications, small orientation changes are commonly described by rotation vectors, spin tensors, or infinitesimal misorientations. By contrast, vector fields in harmonic computations are usually represented by components with respect to Euler-angle derivatives, following the classical formulation of generalized spherical harmonics. This representation is convenient but numerically unfavorable. We instead use rotation-vector components, extending a familiar description of individual orientation changes to orientation-dependent vector fields.
  In this representation, vector fields are described by three scalar component functions, which can be expanded into generalized spherical harmonics. We derive frequency-domain formulas for gradient, divergence, and curl, enabling their evaluation directly on harmonic coefficients. In particular, the gradient of a band-limited scalar function remains band-limited with the same bandwidth.

title: Sharp error estimates for Lagrange interpolation and Kantorovich-type operators in weighted $L_p$-spaces
abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp direct and inverse approximation estimates for algebraic Lagrange interpolation polynomials and Kantorovich-type operators in weighted $L_p$ spaces on $[-1,1]$. A well-known limitation in the theory of approximation by interpolation polynomials states that for small rates of convergence $α\le 1/p$, classical moduli of smoothness fail to provide matching direct and inverse estimates due to the insufficiency of integral metrics to determine pointwise values at the interpolation nodes. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce new special semi-discrete measures of smoothness based on Steklov averaging operators, which combine global $L_p$-smoothness with discrete deviations from Steklov averages at the interpolation nodes. By using these measures, we establish fully matching direct and inverse approximation theorems for Lagrange interpolation polynomials, thereby providing complete two-sided characterizations of the rate of convergence for an arbitrary rate $α> 0$. As a natural application of the developed approach, we also obtain corresponding direct and inverse estimates, as well as strong converse inequalities, for Kantorovich-type operators constructed via Lagrange polynomials.

title: Affine extensions and central compression for product-one-free sequences
abstract: Let $H_s=H_{27}\times C_3^s$, where $H_{27}$ is the nonabelian group of order $27$ and exponent three. We study the elements which can be adjoined to a product-one-free sequence $L$ of length $2s+5$. Let $Q$ be its central subsequence and let $h$ be the dimension of the subgroup generated by $Q$. If $2h-|Q|\le1$, all admissible individual extensions lie in one affine hyperplane of the full additive group coordinates, avoiding the identity. The proof combines coefficient identities with finite, explicitly verified configurations and a transfer valid in every dimension. We also prove an exact central compression theorem: a central zero-sum-free block of length $2h-1$ can be replaced by one term after quotienting by an $(h-1)$-dimensional central subgroup, with a forward implication for product-one-freeness and admissible extensions. For the extraspecial group $E_2$ of order $3^5$ and exponent three, a finite stress obstruction and central compression yield a further uniform restriction: in any product-one-free sequence of length $2r+11$ over $E_2\times C_3^r$, the central subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $2h-2$, where $h$ is its full central rank.

title: Digital Twin Models for Malaria Transmission: A Classical and Stieltjes Derivative Approach
abstract: We propose two mathematical models for malaria transmission grounded in mosquito--human interactions and the digital twin framework. The first model is formulated using classical derivatives, whereas the second employs Stieltjes derivatives to represent abrupt biological events such as egg hatching and adult-emergence pulses in \emph{Anopheles} mosquito populations. The Stieltjes formulation unifies, in a single equation with two derivators, the continuous transmission dynamics, the biological impulses and the data-assimilation corrections of the digital twin; we prove its well-posedness, specify the order of biological and assimilation atoms when they coincide, and give quantitative conditions under which additive emergence pulses preserve biological admissibility. The numerical study uses 132 monthly confirmed-malaria observations from Kebbi State (January 2015--December 2025) and a synthetic entomological series generated in a controlled recovery experiment, because no measured mosquito time series is available. Parameters are updated incrementally on rolling windows, and one-step-ahead forecasts combine the mechanistic ensemble with a past-only seasonal-persistence component. In the recovery experiment, the model endowed with seasonal recruitment and emergence pulses, which the Stieltjes derivator represents exactly, recovers the synthetic vector dynamics far better than the unforced classical model; this gain is attributable to the seasonal and impulsive mechanisms rather than to the derivative calculus itself, and the phase and pulse schedule of the generator were known to the model. The human-case results are comparable between both formulations; the one-step forecasts improve on a seasonal-naive predictor but not on last-month persistence, so they must be interpreted as a proof of concept rather than as an independent epidemiological validation.

title: Zero-sum subsequences of cross number $1$ over cyclic groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathsf{T}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that every sequence of length $t$ over $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of cross number $1$. We determine the exact value of $\mathsf{T}(C_n)$ for every positive integer $n$, showing that $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=2n-1$ when $n$ is odd and $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=3n/2-1$ when $n$ is even. In particular, $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=\mathsf{s}(C_n)$ for odd $n$.

title: From Powers--Stormer to Loewner Inertia: Weighted Trace Functionals and Orthogonal Perturbations
abstract: We study the weighted trace functional $\TT_{f,h}(A,B)=\Tr h^\circ(A-B)[f(A)-f(B)]$, where $h^\circ(H)=h(H_+)-h(H_-)$. The Jordan decomposition of $A-B$ yields exact common-roof decompositions for operator monotone and operator convex functions, including the Powers--Størmer and Ricard trace comparisons. The orthogonal cross term gives a finite rank-one realization of the classical conditional Löwner-matrix criterion for operator convexity. For powers, resolvent squares yield a coupling-dependent Mellin strip, endpoint identities, and quantitative bounds on off-sector spectral interactions. Linearization produces positive and inverse moment subspaces of power Löwner matrices. A confluent determinant calculation provides the remaining sign data in the known inertia classification. We give explicit equality conditions and a finite-copy application of the Powers--Størmer equality case.

title: Fixed and periodic points of bi-dual intersection operators
abstract: We classify the fixed and periodic points, up to positive dilation, of the operators $\mathbb I_m=\mathbb I_{m,m+1}$ in the indexed bi-dual intersection family associated with centro-section integrals. For $n\ge3$ and $1\le m\le n-2$, a star body satisfies $\mathbb I_m^{\,r}K=cK$ for some $c>0$ and an integer $r\ge1$ if and only if it is an origin-centered Euclidean ball. No convexity, origin symmetry, or initial differentiability is assumed. An exact Grassmannian graph representation gives a decreasing weight and yields a strictly positive linear increment under continuous Steiner symmetrization unless the body is already symmetric. At a fixed point, a uniform radial Taylor estimate makes the same volume-preserving increment quadratic. Sobolev estimates for the spherical Radon transform and its adjoint supply the required regularity. Independently, a strict Lyapunov inequality reduces every periodic point up to dilation to a fixed point. We also prove automatic positivity and smoothness for bounded nonnegative solutions and local geometric convergence of normalized iterates near the ball.

title: On pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian metrics
abstract: In our previous work, we studied the squared $L^2$-norm functionals $\mathcal G$ of Gauduchon's torsion $1$-form and $\mathcal F$ of the Chern torsion over the space of all Hermitian metrics with unit volume on a compact complex manifold. We introduced torsion-critical metrics as critical points of $\mathcal F$. In this paper, We prove that a pluriclosed and astheno-Kähler metric is torsion-critical if and only if it is Kähler. In particular, every compact pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian threefold is Kähler. We also give explicit examples and derive geometric consequences under additional curvature assumptions.

title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
abstract: We study nef line bundles on polarized fibrations $(X/C,\bar{H})$, with a fixed nef metrized ample polarization satisfying $H^d=1$, where $d=\dim X$. We prove a quantitative arithmetic height inequality under relative metric positivity, allowing singular arithmetic models and relatively nef adelic bundles. The height deficit defines a local energy. For nef, relatively ample line bundles over finitely generated fields, this energy is bounded below for almost every complex or nonarchimedean local-field realization of fixed polarized global model data, outside one null set common to the entire relative metric class. The results include big non-semiample examples. For ample $L$ and smooth positively curved $\bar{H}$, the complex critical equation is the Calabi--Yau equation; at zero volume, projective bundles recover Donaldson's functional. We also study critical metrics and conjectural canonical heights defined by energy envelopes.

title: Iterated socles and closure operations
abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a $d$-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local ring, $d\geq2$ containing a field, and let $J\subseteq\mathfrak m^s$ be a parameter ideal with $s\geq2$, also, in the mixed case via some mild assumptions. We prove for that $J:\mathfrak m^{(d-1)(s-1)}\subseteq\overline{J}$, and that $J:\mathfrak m^{(d-1)(s-1)+1}\subseteq\overline{J}$ when $R$ is not regular. We show that Cohen--Macaulayness cannot be removed. We also prove the characteristic-free exact formula $g(J)=(d-1)(s-1)+r$ for parameter ideals of order $s$ with a level tangent cone, giving singular mixed-characteristic Gorenstein and non-Gorenstein examples in which the singular bound is attained.

title: Two-Scale Calculus for Riesz Fractional Gradients: Compactness, Realization, and Periodic Homogenization
abstract: We develop a two-scale calculus for the Riesz fractional gradient $\grads$, $0<s<1$, acting on functions that vanish outside a bounded open set $Ω\subset\R^N$. For bounded families in $H_0^s(Ω)$ we characterize the interior two-scale limits of the fractional gradients and prove, by a Fourier-multiplier estimate, that every limit of this form is generated by such a family; a periodic fractional Helmholtz decomposition identifies the microscopic potentials, and $\eps^s$ is the natural amplitude of the oscillations. For periodic fractional divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, uniformly elliptic, not necessarily symmetric coefficients, we identify the two-scale limit of the fractional gradients and the homogenized problem, whose coefficient is the classical homogenized matrix in $Ω$ and the cell average outside $Ω$, and we construct correctors in $H_0^s(Ω)$ that give strong convergence in $H^s(\R^N)$. The identification extends to parabolic problems with dual-space forcing.

title: Linear Duality and Its Nonlinear Extension via Topological Covering Theorems
abstract:
Linear programming duality and core existence theorems in cooperative game theory are closely related. For example, in the 1960s, Bondareva used linear duality to characterize when the core of a game with transferable utility is nonempty. Scarf later established a core existence theorem for balanced games with non-transferable utility. Shapley derived this result from his KKMS covering theorem, demonstrating how topological covering theorems yield core existence results.
  In this note we give a new KKM-type covering proof of linear duality. We then extend the argument to inequalities with continuous perturbations. Under some asymptotic growth assumptions on perturbations, we obtain a feasible point and balancing coefficients satisfying complementary slackness, a Lagrangian lower bound, and a Scarf-type feasibility criterion. The latter yields Scarf's theorem for normalized cooperative games with non-transferable utility.
  Using Musin's 2017 KKM-type theorems with boundary conditions and the author's 2026 results on cover degrees relative to point configurations, we also obtain a complementary slackness theorem for continuous functions on compact connected oriented manifolds with nonempty boundary.

title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

title: Efficient Implementation of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta Methods for Model Predictive Control
abstract: In direct shooting methods for nonlinear optimal control, one of the major computational costs is simulation of the system and calculation of sensitivities. These costs are particularly steep when the stiffness of the controlled system prescribes the use of implicit integrators, amongst which, implicit Runge-Kutta schemes are most popular. These methods require the use of Newton's method to solve a moderately sized system of nonlinear equations with a dense Jacobian, the computation of which grows cubically with the number of stages, that is, the number of abscissa. To mitigate this we investigate the use of the family of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta (DIRK) methods whose Butcher tableaux are lower triangular. We describe the structure exploiting linear algebra required to make the DIRK methods competitive with fully implicit methods, including efficient sensitivity calculations. Finally, we evaluate the performance of DIRK methods on several example systems, and show that the efficient implementation yields Pareto optimal integration schemes. The fixed step size integrators are provided as part of the acados package and use high-performance linear algebra provided by BLASFEO.

title: Covering dense $r$-graphs by perfect matchings
abstract:
For a matching-covered graph $G$, let $τ(G)$ denote the minimum number of perfect matchings needed to cover all edges of $G$. An $r$-regular graph $G$ is said to be an $r$-graph if $|\partial(X)|\geq r$ for each odd set $X\subseteq V(G)$, where $\partial(X)$ denotes the set of edges with precisely one end in $X$. The generalized Berge conjecture, which was proposed by Mazzuoccolo (J. Graph Theory, 73 (2013) 377-385) and equivalent to the generalized Berge-Fulkerson Conjecture posed by Seymour (Proc. London Math. Soc., 38 (1979) 423-460), states that $τ(G)\leq 2r-1$ for every $r$-graph $G$, while the 1-factorization conjecture, first explicitly formulated by Chetwynd and Hilton (Proc. London Math. Soc., 50 (1985) 193-206), states that $τ(G)=r$ for every $r$-graph $G$ of order $2n$ with $r\ge n$. These conjectures are still open. In this paper, we obtain the following two main results:
  1. Let $G$ be an $r$-graph of order $2n$. If $r\ge n$, then $τ(G)\leq 2r-1$, which implies that the generalized Berge conjecture holds for $r\ge n$, and a linear upper bound of $τ(G)$ in the 1-factorization conjecture is obtained.
  2. Let $G$ be an $r$-graph of order $2n$. If $r\ge 2n/3$, then $τ(G)\leq 4r$, which implies that a linear upper bound of $τ(G)$ in the generalized Berge conjecture is obtained if $r\geq 2n/3$.
  Our main approach combines equitable proper edge-colorings, matching extension techniques, and applications of Edmonds's perfect matching polytope theorem.

title: Local energy decay for small radial solutions of the two-dimensional Hamiltonian $abcd$ Boussinesq system
abstract: We consider the $abcd$ Boussinesq system in two space dimensions, a four-parameter family of models for the two-way propagation of small-amplitude long surface waves, in the generic regime $a,c<0$, $b,d>0$. We first revisit the local well-posedness theory in Sobolev spaces in dimensions $2\le n\le4$ and show that for the Hamiltonian case $b=d$ the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed for small data in the energy space $\mathbb{H}^1(\mathbb R^n)$. Then we consider the asymptotic behavior of these global solutions in the $n=2$ case. Under the condition $-a,-c>b/9$, we prove that every small solution with radial symmetry exhibits local energy decay. As a consequence, there are no small radial time-periodic (in particular, stationary) solutions. Decay also holds, along sequences of times, on balls whose radius grows almost linearly in time. The proof is based on new virial identities adapted to the radial structure of the system. In the proof we introduce two correction functionals such that the resulting quadratic form is coercive precisely when $-a,-c>b/9$, a threshold which is sharp for the functional. To our knowledge this is the first result describing the long-time dynamics of $abcd$ systems in dimension two.

title: Berry Esseen bounds for fractional Vasicek type processes: continuous and high-frequency regimes
abstract: We study the estimation of the drift parameters $(a,b)$ of the fractional Vasicek process $dX_t=a(b-X_t)\,dt+dB^H_t$, driven by a fractional Brownian motion of Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. The estimators are of moment type, built from the empirical mean and variance of the path, and are analysed in two regimes: continuous observation on $[0,T]$, and high-frequency observation at times $t_i=iΔ_n$ with $Δ_n\to0$ and $T_n=nΔ_n\to\infty$. Using the Malliavin--Stein method on the second Wiener chaos, we prove consistency of both estimators for every $H$, and quantitative central limit theorems in the Wasserstein distance: for $H<\frac34$ for the estimator of $a$, with explicit rates depending on $H$, and for every $H\in(0,1)$ for the estimator of $b$, at the rate $T^{-H}$. In the discrete regime the bounds contain an additional discretization term of order $Δ_n^{\min\{H+1/2,\,1\}}$, and for $H<\frac12$ the central limit theorem for the estimator of $b$ requires in addition $T_n^{1-2H}Δ_n^{1+2H}\to0$. A short Monte Carlo study illustrates the results.

title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $λ$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

title: Hydrodynamic limit of the Toda lattice
abstract: In this paper we consider the Toda lattice under random, spatially inhomogeneous initial data, meaning that its initial momenta and interparticle spacings are independent and their laws may slowly vary in space. When the density is strictly positive (but sufficiently small), we identify the model's hydrodynamic limit under Euler scaling. More precisely, we prove that spatial averages of each of the model's local conserved quantities converge to moments of a density $m_τ(λ,q)$ solving the generalized hydrodynamic equation predicted by Doyon arXiv:1902.07624 and Spohn arXiv:1902.07751. To do so, we justify the notion that the Toda lattice can be thought of as a dense collection of many "quasiparticles" that interact through scattering. As in Aggarwal arXiv:2503.08018, we define these quasiparticles through spectral properties of the Toda Lax matrix, but in our inhomogeneous setting we must now show that the eigenvectors of this Lax matrix remain localized throughout the dynamics. The core of our work is to show that, with high probability, the quasiparticle trajectories converge to the characteristic curves of the generalized hydrodynamic equation.

title: Semi-Implicit and Convex Splitting Schemes for the Surface Cahn--Hilliard Equation on Curved Closed Surfaces
abstract: The surface Cahn--Hilliard equation describes phase separation and coarsening of a conserved composition field on fixed curved surfaces. We study a mixed $hp$-surface finite element discretization with curvilinear high-order elements, primarily on the sphere, with the stabilized semi-implicit BDF2 integrator and a stabilized convex-splitting variant solved with the same factorization. For the semi-implicit scheme with a quadratic-growth potential and a truncated nonlinear bulk chemical-potential term, we prove exact discrete mass conservation, energy decay for the start-up steps, an exact per-step energy balance for the BDF2 phase, and a conditional monotone law for a modified Lyapunov functional. A manufactured solution with analytic forcing verifies second order in time and the expected $h$- and $p$-convergence. Torus tests include controlled equal-area bands, whose diffuse energies reproduce sharp-interface perimeters within $1\%$, deterministic coarsening, and a viscous R{ä}tz--Voigt model. Genus-two and genus-three calculations on implicit surfaces conserve mass to roundoff, and their unstable-mode counts agree with area-based Weyl estimates within $1\%$.

title: Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
abstract:
We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(Ω\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(Ω\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partialΩ\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(Ω\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partialΩ\setminusΣ\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminusΣ\), where \(Σ=\{κ=0\}\) is the zero set of the curvature of \(\partialΩ\). Also, at each point \(p\inΣ\cap\{h\neq g\}\), the two one-sided branches extend real analytically across \(p\).
  The proof recasts the vertical part near a contact point as a scalar obstacle problem with a possibly degenerate right-hand side, whose model case is \(Δv=H\,\id_{\{v>0\}}\) with \(H\ge0\) a polynomial. These results are optimal: for merely smooth data the trace may be discontinuous, while in the real-analytic case there are examples where corners do occur.

title: Asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic SPDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
abstract: We study the strong convergence and asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic stochastic partial differential equations driven by additive cylindrical fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(\frac12,1)$. The drift is globally Lipschitz and Gâteaux differentiable, with a second directional derivative taking values in a negative-order space. Under a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt condition on the noise and suitable derivative bounds, we establish strong error estimates that reflect the interaction between noise regularity and drift regularity. In a regime where the strong order is one, the normalized error $m(X^m-X)$ converges in probability in $C([0,T];\V)$ to the unique continuous solution of a random linear integral equation. Its stochastic forcing is a divergence integral plus an explicit covariance correction. The proof combines a Gâteaux chain rule for Malliavin derivatives, uniform spectral approximations, and time increment estimates. Localization gives the result for independent random initial values with finite moments, together with lower-moment convergence at each fixed time.

title: Functional Principal Component Analysis: Minimax Optimality from Sparse to Dense Designs and Beyond
abstract: Functional principal component analysis (FPCA) plays a central role as a dimension-reduction and representation tool in functional data analysis, but its minimax theory for diverging spectral indices under noisy discrete observation has remained open for over two decades. To fill this gap, we consider a sieve-based FPCA framework that pools discrete measurements across subjects and accommodates sampling frequencies ranging from sparse to dense under random designs. We begin by establishing new minimax rates for covariance estimation over general bivariate function classes beyond tensor-product low-complexity structures, thereby identifying the intrinsically two-dimensional optimal rate. Our central theoretical contribution is to establish minimax optimal rates for both individually labelled eigenfunctions with diverging indices and leading principal subspaces of increasing dimensions, under explicit growth and regularity conditions. To establish these results, we develop a general framework for sharp minimax analysis of FPCA under discrete observation, separating spectral approximation from stochastic perturbations and exploiting their distinct structures, thereby offering a new approach to a broad class of nonparametric spectral estimation problems. For both spectral targets, the optimal rates reveal two distinct statistical mechanisms, spectral identification and nonparametric reconstruction, whose interplay gives rise to either four or two sampling regimes. This yields, for the first time, a precise characterization of the impact of discrete sampling across the full range from sparse to dense designs. Finally, as a downstream application, we analyze FPCA-based functional linear regression and show that the FPCA-based estimator attains the minimax-optimal rates.

title: Large-Scale Tensor Trace-Ratio Problem: Randomized Algorithm and Sparse Multilinear Discriminant Analysis via Closed-Form Solution
abstract: Trace-ratio optimization problems from high-dimensional tensor data appear across numerous research domains including machine learning, signal processing, as well as pattern recognition. Up to now, analytical closed-form expressions remain unavailable for tensor trace-ratio tasks; prevailing techniques mostly adopt inner-outer iterative schemes to tackle such optimization tasks. However, when dealing with high-dimensional tensor data sets, existing multilinear discriminant analysis methods often encounter limitations such as heavy computational costs, insufficient memory space, and interference from redundant features. This paper yields two core contributions.First, we present a closed-form solution under the full row rank condition, and construct a randomized solver targeting large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization. In contrast to prior approaches, the devised algorithm achieves substantial computational speedup.Its core mechanism is to reformulate the original large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization into a tensor least-squares formulation, instead of the much more complicated (generalized) tensor eigenproblems. We derive theoretical error-bound results which verify the reliability of the newly developed algorithm. Second, we build a sparse multilinear discriminant analysis model leveraging the above closed-form result combined with tensor \ell_{2,0}-norm regularization, and propose a sparse multilinear discriminant method for tensor feature selection. The sparse method can identify key discriminative features from high-dimensional data and suppress redundant information. Comprehensive numerical evaluations are conducted over multiple publicly available real-world benchmarks.The proposed methods demonstrate significant advantages in computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale problems, while achieving competitive classification accuracy on some datasets.

title: Variational Estimates for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs
abstract: We study edge variation estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on finite connected graphs. For $0<α<1$, we determine the optimal coefficient in the uniform estimate of the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge $p$-variation of the original function. We also obtain two-sided variation bounds involving the number of vertices and the diameter. On complete graphs, we prove that the sharp $(p,q)$ constant is $(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{1/q-1/p}$ for all $0<p\leq q\leq\infty$. On star graphs with $n\geq4$, we determine the sharp infinite-exponent constant and show that the sharp constant for $p=2$ equals $1-n^{α-1}$ if and only if $n^{α-1}\geq1/2$. Combining this with the known estimate for $p=1$, we also obtain sharp mixed estimates. Extremizers and counterexamples are given.

title: On the slope stability of vector bundles on Sasakian manifolds
abstract: We study the variation problem of slope stability of $T$-linearized sheaves on a compact Sasakian manifold, or more generally, on an affine variety with a good $T$-action. In particular, we establish the wall-and-chamber structure for the slope stability of $T$-linearized torsion-free sheaves.

title: 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer as orbits under the group of interval shifts
abstract: We generate a splitting of the 924 monotonically ascending twelve tone half series H=(H_1,..,H_6) in [0,..,11]^6 in 80 orbits H^G under the additive cyclic group G=Z/12Z of transpositions (interval shifts). By classification according to cardinality and forming the union of the orbits H^G and K^G of a half series H and its complement K, we obtain exactly the 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer, completely independent of symmetry properties, however, fundamentally due to so-called wider-gleiche orbits. This was not clear in previous literature.

title: $L^p$-isometries on idempotents
abstract: We study surjective $L^p$-isometries on spaces of bounded idempotents in an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. On each fixed positive finite-rank stratum, every surjective $L^p$-isometry, $1\leq p<\infty$, is implemented by a unitary or antiunitary operator, possibly composed with adjunction; no separability is required. The same conclusion holds for the operator norm, viewed as the $L^\infty$-norm. On a separable space, operator-norm isometries of the infinite-rank, infinite-corank sector admit the additional complement operation, as do surjective $L^p$-isometries between individual $L^p$-perturbation classes for $1\leq p<\infty$. For the extended $L^p$-metric on all idempotents, implementations may be chosen independently on finite-distance classes, subject to an explicit compatibility condition for matching infinite-rank classes. The proofs use similarity coordinates and metric blow-ups, followed by tangent-space splittings, nearest projections at the $L^1$ endpoint, or sharp Fredholm-index distance estimates. We also establish uniqueness of standard implementations and use essential-spectral invariants to obtain continuum many perturbation-class isometry types.

title: A Godunov-type in-cell discontinuous reconstruction shock-capturing method for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
abstract: The present paper is devoted to show the correct convergence of a numerical method based on Godunov and the in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic but never recasts in a conservation form. With ambiguous nonconservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. In a previous work the authors determine the simple waves of the nonconservative system studied here and they are able to construct the solutions of the Riemann problem of interest. These solutions are used to obtain a Godunov-type scheme and it is combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique to obtain the correct convergence to the exact solution even in the presence of shocks.

title: Second-Order Steady-State Approximation of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models
abstract: Mean-field models provide tractable approximations for large stochastic systems, but second-order steady-state results are largely limited to homogeneous or fixed-dimensional population processes. This paper develops a second-order steady-state approximation for fully heterogeneous mean-field models. Conditioning on the realized agent parameters, we study fixed-dimensional weighted occupancies even though the dimension of the full heterogeneous mean-field system grows linearly with the number of agents $M$. We first establish an $O(M^{-1})$ bound on the mean-field approximation error for stationary expectations of twice continuously differentiable functions of these occupancies. We then characterize the leading term in this error in terms of the stationary mean bias and covariance of the weighted occupancies. A Lyapunov equation for the linearized dynamics yields an approximation to the stationary covariance of the unscaled weighted occupancy with error $O(M^{-3/2})$. Its solution, together with the drift derivatives at equilibrium, also gives an explicit $1/M$ correction to the mean-field prediction of the stationary mean. The corrected mean has error $o(M^{-1})$, which improves to $O(M^{-3/2})$ under a stronger bound on the drift remainder. The resulting covariance and mean-refinement equations have the same structure as the finite-time heterogeneous refined mean-field equations, but our results directly provide steady-state guarantees for weighted occupancies rather than marginal state probabilities of individual agents. The results are illustrated through a heterogeneous power-of-two load-balancing model with buffer size two.

title: On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums
abstract: Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $σ$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.

title: An Isogeometric Collocation Solver Based on the Quantized Tensor Train Representation
abstract: We introduce an isogeometric collocation framework based on the quan tized tensor train (QTT) representation to solve partial differential equa tions. The proposed method constructs isogeometric collocation operators directly in the QTT format using only a few sampled entries, enabling ef ficient compression and computation. The vectors of the geometry-derived coefficients at the collocation points are represented in the QTT format using the TT-cross approximation. We conduct numerical experiments using the proposed QTT-based isogeometric collocation framework for the convection diffusion-reaction problems in different spatial dimensions and for the Poisson problems on three-dimensional nontrivial geometries, showing significant re ductions in memory usage and computational cost while preserving solution accuracy.

title: A Geometric Characteristic Long Exact Sequence for Codimension-Two Spin and Pin-plus/minus Bordism
abstract: Following Botvinnik--Rosenberg \cite{BotvinnikRosenberg2023}, we define fibered-boundary bordism, introduce sphere-bundle bordism, and prove an exact sequence relating them to ordinary bordism. The sequence also holds when all sphere fibers are required to be non-$D^r$-bounding. Following Debray--Ye--Yu \cite{DebrayYeYu2026}, we define characteristic cycles with a chosen complement structure trivializing a characteristic class. For the GM and $\mathrm{KT}^{\pm}$ cases, deleting tubular neighborhoods and identifying sphere-bundle structures with determinant-twisted base structures give a characteristic exact sequence. This proves the bordism-group consequence of the DYY conjecture for our definitions, without constructing the conjectured map of spectra.

title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
abstract: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and $n\to0$ with $nL^{1/2}$ fixed, we derive a universal scaling function which characterizes the large-deviation statistics of the two-polymer free energy and is expected to be universal within the one-dimensional two-layer periodic SHE/KPZ class. The two tails of the large-deviation function are obtained analytically, revealing different roles of the non-crossing constraint in favorable and unfavorable fluctuations of the common disorder.

title: The $S$ and Double-Exponential Transformations with a Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals
abstract: Three-centre two-electron Coulomb and hybrid integrals over exponential-type functions involve semi-infinite radial integrals containing oscillatory spherical Bessel functions. We investigate the combination of the $S$ transformation with Fourier-type double-exponential (DE) quadrature for their accurate and efficient numerical evaluation. The $S$ transformation transfers derivatives from the spherical-Bessel factor to the radial amplitude, converting the integral into a sine representation particularly well suited to Fourier-type DE quadrature. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the combined $S+\mathrm{DE}$ approach can substantially reduce the number of quadrature nodes required to achieve high accuracy compared with direct DE. We further identify a geometry-dependent oscillation-to-damping ratio and establish a convergent moment expansion in the weakly oscillatory regime. Exploiting this complementary representation markedly enhances the numerical reliability of the algorithm in regimes where direct oscillatory quadrature becomes inefficient. The method is examined through semi-infinite radial integrals and complete H$_2$O and C$_2$H$_4$ molecular integrals over Slater-type functions, with comparisons against complete $S$-series evaluations and values reported in the literature.

title: Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
abstract: We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. For a fixed weak nonzero shock, sufficiently weak rarefaction and contact waves, and small H^2(R) initial perturbations, we establish asymptotic stability with a time-dependent shift on the viscous shock. The L^4 time average of the uniform perturbation and the shift velocity over [t,2t] is bounded by C_S(1+t)^(-1/4). We prove pointwise-in-time bounds of order (1+t)^(-1/12) on the whole line, (1+t)^(-1/4) near the shifted shock, and (1+t)^(-1/6) on |x| >= ηt for each fixed η>0. The proof uses energy estimates and comparison on finite time interval

title: Pseudocompact MAD families under $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak c$
abstract: We prove that if the bounding number $\mathfrak b$ equals the cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$, then every infinite almost disjoint family of size less than $\mathfrak c$ can be extended to a maximal almost disjoint family whose Isbell--Mrówka space has a pseudocompact Vietoris hyperspace.

title: Near-optimal convergence of Widlund's method and numerical exploration of different implementations
abstract: For linear systems arising from the discretization of certain classes of mathematical models, the splitting of the linear system into its Hermitian and skew-Hermitian parts has a physical meaning. If, in addition, the Hermitian part is positive definite, there exist Krylov subspace methods based on three-term recurrences where the Hermitian part is used as a preconditioner. Two such Krylov subspace methods are Widlund's method and Rapoport's method. In this paper we establish a ``near-optimal'' guarantee for the convergence of Widlund's method, showing that the overall convergence of Widlund's method is nearly as good as that of Rapoport's method. Specifically, we show that for every iteration $k$, there exists an iteration $j\leq k$ where the residual norm of Widlund's method is less than $\sqrt{k+1} $ times the residual norm of Rapoport's method at iteration $k$. This bound is sharp. We also provide a computational study on various implementations of Widlund's method in the exact and inexact cases, and show that certain implementations may stagnate while others do not, i.e., we look at the robustness of the different implementations. We recommend two implementations.

title: Benchmarking Traditional and Learning-Based Reference-Free Compressors for Long-Read Sequencing Data
abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies generate large volumes of data, creating substantial storage and transmission demands. Although reference-based compressors can achieve high compression, their reliance on an appropriate reference genome limits their use. We present LRCBench, a benchmark and survey of reference-free lossless compressors for long-read sequencing data. We review traditional and learning-based general-purpose and sequencing-specific methods, then evaluate 35 compressors on 16 real-world datasets from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio platforms. We compare compression ratio, storage savings, runtime, peak memory use, and robustness across datasets. Learning-based compressors are evaluated on six MinION datasets because of their high computational costs. CoLoRd achieves the best overall compression ratios in our experiments, while other methods offer trade-offs in speed, memory use, and robustness. We also examine multithreaded speedup and discuss future directions in parallel acceleration, privacy protection, adaptive parameter tuning, and hardware-algorithm co-design.

title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
abstract: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension.

title: Weak Hilbert's Nullstellensatz for skew polynomials over division rings
abstract: We establish a weak Nullstellensatz for skew polynomial rings $R_n=D[x_1,\ldots,x_n;σ]$, where $D$ is a division ring and the commuting variables induce the same automorphism $σ$ of $D$. For $n\ge2$, we characterize the pairs $(D,σ)$ for which every maximal left ideal is generated by $x_1-a_1,\ldots,x_n-a_n$, with $σ(a_j)a_i=σ(a_i)a_j$. The criterion consists of right $σ$-algebraic closure of $D$ and right algebraic closure of the centralizers of all commuting $(n-2)$-tuples in each twisted fixed division ring $E_a=\{c\in D:σ(c)a=ac\}$ for $0\ne a\in D$.

title: Nonradial threshold scattering for the planar cubic--quintic NLS
abstract:
We study the planar cubic--quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[
  i\partial_tu+Δu=-|u|^2u+|u|^4u,
  \qquad (t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2, \] with initial data $u_0\in H^1_x(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove scattering in both time directions when the mass of \(u_0\) equals the mass of the ground state for the focusing cubic equation. This resolves the nonradial threshold scattering problem posed by Murphy [\emph{Comm.\ Partial Differential Equations} \textbf{46} (2021), 2213--2234]. Together with the known subthreshold scattering theory and the existence of standing waves at every larger mass, this identifies the sharp mass range in which every $H^1$ solution scatters. The proof combines localized interaction Morawetz estimates with propagation estimates on moving halfspaces to control exterior kinetic energy.

title: Projection-Based and Modulus-Based Equivalent Reformulations of the Linear Complementarity Problem and Corresponding Iterative Methods: A Review
abstract:
The Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) is a fundamental
  mathematical model arising in optimization, equilibrium
  theory, and various scientific and engineering applications.
  Its complementarity structure admits several equivalent
  mathematical representations, which provide a foundation
  for developing a wide range of iterative solution methods.
  This review presents a systematic and critical analysis
  of the principal reformulations of the LCP, with particular
  emphasis on minimum-function, projection-based,
  positive-negative part, and modulus-based formulations.
  The mathematical equivalence of these representations
  to the standard LCP is examined, highlighting their
  underlying relationships and the preservation of the
  complementarity conditions.
  Building upon these formulations, the review surveys
  the corresponding iterative methods developed in the
  existing literature, focusing on their mathematical
  foundations, algorithmic structures, and convergence
  requirements.
  A comparative perspective is developed to discuss the
  relative advantages and limitations of the different
  approaches, emphasizing that the suitability of an
  iterative method depends on the structural properties
  of the underlying LCP and the specific algorithm employed.
  In addition, relevant performance measures, including
  iteration count, CPU time, complementarity residual,
  memory requirements, and parameter sensitivity, are
  discussed as criteria for numerical evaluation. Finally,
  the review identifies important challenges and potential
  research directions, particularly in adaptive parameter
  selection, effective matrix-splitting strategies, scalable
  implementations, and reproducible numerical benchmarking,
  with the aim of supporting the development of reliable
  and computationally efficient methods for solving LCPs

title: Hurwitz equivalence in quandles of order at most four
abstract: Let $X$ be a quandle and let $m\geq 2$ be an integer. The $m$-braid group acts on the $m$-fold Cartesian power $X^m$ by the Hurwitz action. For an $m$-tuple $\boldsymbol{x}\in X^m$, we introduce two invariants of the Hurwitz action: the product $Π(\boldsymbol{x})$ of its entries in the associated group $\operatorname{As}(X)$ and the orbit multiplicities $μ_w(\boldsymbol{x})$ $(w\in X)$. We prove that these two invariants completely classify Hurwitz equivalence classes for all quandles of order at most four. We also establish a complete classification of Hurwitz equivalence classes for a class of amalgamated sums of trivial quandles and a reduction theorem for disjoint sums with trivial quandles. Finally, we study the corresponding action of the virtual braid group. For this action, the orbit multiplicities alone give a complete classification for every quandle of order at most four.

title: Some Results on the Complex Oscillation of Second-Order Linear Differential Equations
abstract: We study the zeros of solutions of $f''+A(z)f=0$ with an entire coefficient $A$. We answer two questions of Gundersen affirmatively. We prove that if $A$ has finite order and the exponent of convergence of its distinct zeros is smaller than its order, then the zeros of the product of any two linearly independent solutions have infinite exponent of convergence. We also prove that if $A$ has finite order and the exponent of convergence of its zeros, counted with multiplicity, is smaller than its order, then the zeros of every non-trivial solution have infinite exponent of convergence.

title: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
abstract: We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations. The resolutions motivate us to introduce the notion of locally analytic representations of compact presentation, which generalizes the notion of finitely presented representations. These representations are related to prim objects on the classifying stack in the sense of $6$-functor formalism and their extension groups to admissible locally analytic representations are finite-dimensional. As an application, we establish Serre duality for extension groups of locally analytic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ attached to non-trianguline de Rham Galois representations under the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

title: The Fujita equation with time-integrable forcing: effective mass, mass annihilation and sharp lifespan
abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $\partial_t u-Δu=|u|^p+ζ(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, $p>1$, with sign-changing data and a forcing whose temporal profile $ζ$ is integrable on $(0,\infty)$, the model case being $ζ(t)=t^σe^{-t}$, $σ>-1$. For power-type profiles $ζ(t)=t^σ$ the forcing is known to raise the critical exponent above the Fujita exponent $p_F=1+2/N$ or to destroy global existence. We show that an integrable forcing leaves $p_F$ unchanged and acts only through the effective mass $M_{\rm eff}=\int u_0+(\int_0^\inftyζ)(\int w)$. Our central result is an exact mass-annihilation identity: if $1<p\le p_F$, every global weak solution lies in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty))$ and satisfies $\iint|u|^p=-M_{\rm eff}$. Hence, for $p\le p_F$, no global solution exists when $M_{\rm eff}\ge0$ and the data are nontrivial, and every global mild solution vanishes in $L^1$ as $t\to\infty$; examples show that $M_{\rm eff}<0$ neither excludes nor implies global existence. For $p>p_F$, every solution is dominated by a multiple of the linear forced flow under a single integral condition; this gives small-data global existence without sign restrictions and, if $ζ$ decays mildly, convergence to $m_\infty G_t$ with asymptotic mass $m_\infty=M_{\rm eff}+\iint|u|^p$. We also give a localized necessary condition valid for all $p>1$, showing that large or slowly decaying data blow up regardless of the forcing and that non-integrable forcings shift the threshold, and sharp lifespan estimates for small data with positive effective mass: $T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-2(p-1)/(2-N(p-1))}$ for $p<p_F$ and $\log T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for $p=p_F$.

title: On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families
abstract:
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$.
  We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $χ\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $π_{χ,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $π_χ=\operatorname{ind}_P^Gχ$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $χ$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $π_{χ,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $χ$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

title: Critical spectral weights on triangulated disk
abstract: We solve the common-positive-weight support problem at the local spectral threshold 1/2 for relative triangulated disks with interior degrees at most five and an empty or connected degree-five core. We characterize feasibility by a finite decomposition into three elementary pieces and a condition on the original boundary marking. The proof passes from spectral equality to a positive conjugate rectangle, then uses geometric reductions to obtain a serial presentation. The empty-face inequality holds for some common positive weights exactly when such a presentation has only old join endpoints. Whenever this condition holds, our construction yields weights with a positive definite empty-face matrix. Positive Schur responses establish sufficiency, and a uniform face-counting obstruction proves necessity. This gives a finite combinatorial criterion for critical spectral feasibility together with a constructive choice of common weights.

title: Rough vector fields with vanishing Lie brackets
abstract: We consider two vector fields $X, Y \in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\mathbb R^d) \cap \mathbf L^\infty$ with bounded divergence. If $p \geq 2$, this paper shows that $DX \,Y - DY \, X = 0$ almost everywhere if and only if their Regular Lagrangian Flows commute. If instead $1 \leq p < 2$, we present an example of two divergence free locally Sobolev vector fields in $\mathbb R^2$ with vanishing Lie brackets whose flows do not commute. In the regime $2 \leq p < \infty$ this paper also yields a quantitative commutation result not depending on the Lipschitz constant for vector fields with $[X, Y] \neq 0$, which is new even in the smooth setting.

title: A Characterization of Rings Where a Linear Transformation and Its Inverse and Transpose Have the Same Information Exchange
abstract: Linear transformations are considered over finite commutative rings. It is shown that the information exchange of an invertible linear transformation and that of its inverse are equal for any ring. It is also shown that the information exchange of any linear transformation and that of its transpose are equal if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications are presented to the Discrete Fourier Transform, to the analysis of Vandermonde transformations, and to area-time complexity.

title: Turán number of the odd-ballooning of odd prisms
abstract: The Turán problem for odd-balloonings has been studied for various classes of skeleton graphs, including stars, paths, cycles, trees, bipartite graphs, and certain 3-chromatic graphs. The Turán numbers and extremal graphs for odd prisms have also been determined. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the Turán problem for prescribed odd-balloonings of odd prisms. Let $k\geq1$ be fixed, and let $F^o$ be a prescribed odd-ballooning of the odd prism $C_{2k+1}\square K_2$, in which each edge is replaced by a cycle of prescribed odd length at least five. For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that $${\rm ex}(n,F^o)=\Big\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\Big\rfloor+(k+1)n-3(k+1)^2.$$ Furthermore, the unique extremal graph is $K_{\,2k+2,\,\lfloor(n-2k-2)/2\rfloor,\,\lceil(n-2k-2)/2\rceil}$. The proof combines the decomposition-family method and Simonovits' structural theorem with local embedding arguments to establish the extremal structure and its uniqueness.

title: Optimal local gradient estimate for gravity water waves and its application to the Stokes conjecture
abstract:
In 1880, G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol. I] studied a two-dimensional gravity water wave and conjectured that the wave crest forms a symmetric corner of angle 2pi/3 at the stagnation point.
