After anisotropic rescaling, the intensity converges globally in $L^1$ to a transverse Gaussian times a longitudinal quartic exponential. Moyal's identity gives the corresponding total STFT-energy law, but does not imply a local phase-space concentration theorem. We compare these global statements with the earlier quartic critical-window analysis of Berry and Shukla for periodic superoscillations. Supporting results include quantitative fixed-Gaussian STFT expansions, entire-growth convergence with a critical-step obstruction, and conditional Gabor-frame and dual-window expansions. Weighted STFT estimates for polynomial electric-field evolution are obtained as applications. No claim of priority is made for quartic criticality, qualitative STFT supershift preservation, or polynomial electric-field persistence as such.

title: Global stability and nonlinear asymptotics for the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity
abstract: We study the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity, a positive coefficient $λ+μ>0$ in the divergence term, and full heat conduction. Horizontal viscosity does not dissipate vertical shear derivatives, while thermal diffusion is coupled to the compressible variables. For small $H^2$ perturbations of a constant equilibrium, we construct global strong solutions. Additional spatial localization yields anisotropic decay through second order, convergence of the full $H^2$ norm, and horizontal Gaussian profiles determined by an effective velocity datum. The third-order behavior contains nonlinear contributions: horizontal viscous heating generates a differentiated Newton potential in temperature, while compressible transport slows the decay of the potential velocity. We prove the corresponding bounds with exponents $17/8$ and $2$; for each exponent, we construct a fixed datum in the corresponding class for which every larger exponent fails. For each fixed initial datum, however, the corresponding time-weighted norms tend to zero as $t\to\infty$. Smallness of the first vertical derivative of the initial velocity in the horizontal mixed norm improves the vertical decay estimates and restores the linear third-order temperature rate. Both the existence and decay results require only $H^2$ Sobolev regularity of the initial data.

title: Homeomorphic Sobolev Extensions to Jordan Domains and the inner distance
abstract: Given a Jordan domain $Ω$, we characterize the situation where a given parametrization (or all parametrizations) $\varphi:\partial\mathbb D\to\partialΩ$ has (have) a homeomorphic $W^{1,1}$-extension $f_{\varphi}:\overline{\mathbb D}\to\overlineΩ$.

title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
abstract: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of interaction topology and latent network states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian. We develop TopoScore-FAF, a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, while a frozen diffusion emulator represents the centered transition residual, avoiding the structural ambiguity of unrestricted generative models. First, we establish a score--topology duality that expresses edge-wise transition likelihood gradients as projections of the residual diffusion score. This enables topology learning without evaluating transition densities or differentiating through the generative sampler. Second, we develop diffusion-score-based topology identification with guarantees of identifiability under intermittent observations and invariance of the population minimizer across diffusion noise levels. Sufficient smoothing yields global strong convexity for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. As smoothing vanishes, the asymptotic covariance of the state-pair estimator decreases toward the Cramér--Rao bound, with a strict advantage over Gaussian quasi-likelihood under an edge-relevant non-Gaussianity condition. Third, we construct a topology-conditioned generative particle filter that combines guided residual sampling with score-driven graph updates. We establish mean-square closed-loop error bounds under a step-size-independent small-gain condition. The resulting framework uses the graph to structure state propagation and the estimated states to refine the graph. Synthetic and real-data experiments demonstrate its benefits under non-Gaussian forcing.

title: A complete classification of isometries of quasihyperbolic domains
abstract: We classify all surjective quasihyperbolic isometries between arbitrary proper planar domains. Apart from Euclidean similarities, the orientation-preserving isometries are reciprocal maps on sectors or punctured planes and explicit complex-power maps on logarithmic spiral sectors. In particular, orientation-preserving planar quasihyperbolic isometries need not be Möbius. As consequences, we obtain similarity rigidity when either domain has finite inradius, for multiply connected domains other than punctured planes, and for $C^1$ domains other than half-planes. The $C^1$ conclusion strengthens Hästö's corresponding result for planar $C^3$ domains. Our planar classification, together with Richard's classification in dimensions $n\geq3$, completely solves the quasihyperbolic isometry problem between proper subdomains of $\mathbb R^n$ in every dimension $n\geq2$. As an application, we extend to dimension two the characterization of pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence of quasihyperbolic domains obtained by Herron, Richard, and Snipes.

title: A Batched Discrepancy Principle for Stochastic Landweber-Kaczmarz Iteration and its Application to EIT
abstract: We consider an inverse problem given as ill-posed system of possibly nonlinear operator equations between Hilbert spaces. To solve the problem we use a stochastic mini-batch Landweber-Kaczmarz method, drawing uniformly a subset of equations in each step. As an a posteriori stopping rule, we introduce a batched version of the discrepancy principle, in which only the residual of the selected batches is monitored. Under the tangential cone condition, we establish the convergence of the iterates for exact data, the convergence of the regularized iterates for noisy data under an a priori choice of the stopping index, and the convergence of the method when it is terminated by the proposed batched discrepancy principle. Numerical experiments for the electrical impedance tomography problem illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the performance of the method for different batch sizes.

title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
abstract: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).

title: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
abstract: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\neΛ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(Λ)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $Λ\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.

title: Boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to diffusion operators in Lebesgue spaces
abstract: We revisit boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to a diffusion operator both in fixed and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. We obtain optimal asymptotics in the former setting and we provide new tools to establish boundedness in the latter.

title: The number of $k$-factors of a random regular graph
abstract: Let $Z_k(G)$ be the number of $k$-factors ($k$-regular spanning subgraphs) of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph $G\sim G(n,d)$, where $d\ge 3$ and $1\le k\le d-1$ are fixed integers such that $dn$ and $kn$ are even. We determine the asymptotic second moment of $Z_k(G)$ and show that $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G)$ converges in distribution to an explicit random variable $W$ that depends on the short-cycle counts of $G$ but not on $k$. Moreover, for any $1\le k,\ell\le d-1$, the normalised counts on the same graph satisfy $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G) - Z_\ell(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_\ell(G) \to 0$ in probability, and, since $W>0$ almost surely, their ratio converges to $1$ in probability. This extends results of Bollobás--McKay and Janson for $k=1$ and Robalewska for $k=2$ to all $1\le k\le d-1$. In the pairing model, the second moment reduces to a one-dimensional lattice sum over the overlap of two $k$-factors. We evaluate this sum using the Poisson-binomial representation of the hypergeometric distribution, exponential tilting, and a uniform local limit theorem.

title: Cwikel and Kato-Seiler-Simon estimates for commutators
abstract:
We prove that the commutator $[a(X),b(-\mathrm{i}
abla)]$ belongs to the weak Schatten class $\mathcal{S}^p_{m weak}$ provided $
abla a\in L^p$ and $
abla b\in L^p_{m weak}$ for $\max\{1,2d/(d+2)\}<p<\infty$. This is an analogue of Cwikel's estimate, with a larger range of exponents. We also prove analogues of the Kato-Seiler-Simon and Birman-Solomyak-Simon estimates. Counterexamples show the necessity of the lower thresholds and the failure of the Lipschitz endpoint estimate.

title: A Trajectory-Based Mathematical Framework for Wildfire Front Propagation in Heterogeneous Landscapes
abstract: We present a mathematical formulation based on trajectories for modeling the propagation of wildfire fronts in heterogeneous landscapes and apply it to the Brazilian Pantanal. The formulation is made up of a direction-dependent propagation law and Finsler orthogonality along a moving boundary. This results in a nonlinear local system for outward fire front trajectories. We provide a strictly convex translated ellipse representation at each point of the evolving boundary which guaranties uniqueness and existence of the chosen outward velocity. The effective propagation coefficients that are dependent on space and the hourly wind forcing permit the perimeter to evolve irregularly without imposing a fixed global front geometry. Computed trajectories were georeferenced and isotropically spatially registered with VIIRS active-fire observations. ERA5 wind and ERA5-Land vegetation data were used to describe the environmental forcing and landscape heterogeneity. The full-run Dice coefficients for the observation-guided spatial comparisons for the exploratory experiments for September 3-5, 2020 are 0.578, 0.571, and 0.467 respectively. One-at-a-time sensitivity perturbations of the spatial propagation coefficient, wind speed magnitude and rate-law exponents quantify the governing influence of the environmental forcing and parameter variations on the spatial extent of the calculated fire advance. These observed patterns also guided calibration and, in the absence of exact timestamps of satellite acquisition, the results show within-event spatial agreement rather than independent predictive validation. The framework provides a mathematically rigorous basis for subsequent uncertainty quantification, independent validation over multiple events and prospective sector-wise assessments of simulated fire spread.

title: Restoring Power Fairly: Equitable Resource Allocation in Post-Disaster Grid Recovery
abstract: Post-disaster power restoration requires allocating limited repair and power resources across affected communities, creating a fundamental tension between restoring service efficiently and providing equitable access to electricity. We develop an optimization framework incorporating horizontal fairness, which promotes comparable service across affected communities, and vertical fairness, which accounts for differences in community vulnerability. The framework integrates repair-crew scheduling with an approximation of power-system operations, including distributed generation and solar-plus-storage resources. It supports vulnerability-aware prioritization while protecting specified fractions of bus-level service under a horizontal-fairness reference plan and limiting the increase in restoration cost. Structural results characterize when the two fairness benchmarks can be attained simultaneously in an aggregate allocation model and provide a sufficient condition under which improving vertical fairness requires changing discrete decisions in the full restoration model. Using the IEEE 33-bus test system, we show that equitable restoration operates through two interconnected mechanisms: reconnecting isolated areas and allocating limited power within connected areas. In the tested setting, selected vulnerability-aware solutions attain both fairness benchmarks at a lower cost than their horizontal-fairness reference plan. The results also show that stronger emphasis on horizontal fairness can yield lower efficiency losses than intermediate fairness settings, with an identical-demand comparison illustrating the role of demand heterogeneity. The framework helps decision makers identify the operational sources of service disparities and evaluate how repair priorities, power allocation, and allowable cost increases affect the opportunities to reduce them.

title: Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem
abstract: We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology class, then the sum of all correction terms strictly increases along its surgeries with coefficients -1/j relative to the rational longitude, so no nontrivial surgery yields the original oriented manifold. We also show that every purely cosmetic band surgery on a knot with an L-space branched double cover is weakly nugatory, which answers a question of Rogers for these knots.

title: Nine-Colored Partition Components Modulo 19
abstract: Let $p_{m}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ into parts of $m$ colors, and let $y=q^{19}$. Starting from Winquist's identity, as Hirschhorn did for the modulus $11$, we express each of the nineteen components of $(q;q)_{\infty}^{10}$ modulo $19$ as a sum of two quartic products of the theta functions $(y^{a};y^{19})_{\infty}(y^{19-a};y^{19})_{\infty}$, and deduce all nineteen generating functions $\sum_{n} p_{9}(19n+r)y^{n}$ modulo $19$ in closed form. The vanishing class $p_{9}(19n+17)$ is the one known previously. For seventeen colors, the residue class singled out by Kiming and Olsson carries no congruence, and we show that its generating function is $y f(y^{19})^{2}/f(y)$ modulo $19$. Along the way, we recall, with proofs, such exact relationships known for all these congruences. O'Brien's cubic relation is a Weierstrass equation for $X_{0}(19)$ in Kolberg's coordinates; we prove the existence of a doubling automorphism of the theta functions, fixing the cubic, which acts on both dissections by explicit scalars. All proofs are by hand.

title: Katona's Shadow Equality Persists under Bounded VC-Dimension
abstract: Katona's intersecting-shadow theorem states that every $t$-intersecting $r$-uniform family has size at most that of its $(r-t)$-shadow, with equality precisely for complete $r$-uniform families on $2r-t$ points. We prove that both the shadow inequality and its equality classification remain valid under the substantially weaker assumption that the VC-dimension is at most $r-t$. By contrast, bounded VC-dimension and $t$-intersection do not, in general, yield the same extremal bounds in the corresponding cardinality problem.

title: Shape-Derivative Moment Approximation for a Reduced Time-Harmonic Biot Poroelastic System with Random Interfaces
abstract: We develop first- and second-moment approximations for a reduced time-harmonic Biot poroelastic interface system with random material interfaces. The model retains mixture inertia, quasi-static Darcy discharge, and explicit storage and coupling coefficients. The interface separates two media, each with constant Lamé parameters and hydraulic mobility. We use shape calculus to analyze random perturbations normal to the interface. We derive the first shape derivative in a total-traction and normal-flux formulation, establish a Taylor expansion on a fixed function space under a non-resonance assumption, and prove error bounds on fixed observation regions. The mean approximation is second-order accurate, and the covariance and variance approximations are third-order accurate. We estimate the variance error directly. Applying pivoted Cholesky compression to the covariance matrix of the coefficients in a fixed basis of smooth interface modes reduces the computation of the leading covariance to deterministic sensitivity solves. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions examine perturbation rates, low-rank truncation, coupled statistics, and computational cost.

title: Convergence of replicator-mutator particle systems via bounded Wasserstein distance
abstract: Interacting particle systems with selection and mutation mechanisms arise in biological modeling, evolutionary optimization, and particle filtering methods. In this work we will consider the paradigmatic replicator-mutator PDE, which combines a diffusive component with a source term that depends on an external potential. We derive quantitative error estimates for the distance between the empirical measure of an unweighted particle system and the solution of the PDE. The proof uses a Wasserstein-1 distance with a bounded ground cost, which allows us to treat unbounded potentials on an unbounded state space. The key tools are the optimal coupling of newly resampled particles and, for the time-continuous limit, the use of a discrete-time killing resampling.

title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

title: Tropical Geometry of $G_2$
abstract: We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard. These form hexagons in incidence geometry. We classify all toric degenerations and their Newton-Okounkov polytopes. Mukai theory leads us to tropical canonical curves of genus 10. This article serves as a blueprint for studies of reductive groups in tropical geometry.

title: Dyson's Tenfold Way, Revisited
abstract:
In this work, we study semilinear representations of groups acting on degree two Galois extensions. Our results include a classification of irreducible semilinear representations, which generalises Dyson's Tenfold Way. Using this, we completely describe the semilinear representation theory of certain groups, such as symmetric groups, and of finite groups over cyclotomic fields.
  We also prove many results concerning semilinear representations over $\mathbb{C}$, which includes an induction theorem which simultaneously generalises Brauer's Induction Theorem and Serre's Induction Theorem. We are also interested in applications of our classification theorem to crystallography, and include a detailed study of the semilinear representation theory of magnetic wallpaper groups.

title: Optimal Stability for Bivariate Weighted Fourth-Order Inequalities
abstract: In this paper, we prove sharp stability estimates for a two-component radial weighted fourth-order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality in the two radial regimes for which the scalar optimizers are explicitly known and the corresponding spectral non-degeneracy holds. These regimes are \(4-N<α<2,\ \ell=-α\), and \(2<α<N,\ \ell=4(α-2)(N-2)/(N-α)-α\). Let $N\ge 3$, $p=2(N+\ell)/(N-4+α)>2$, \(μ_1,μ_2\geq0\), \(κ>0\), and $r,s>1$ satisfy $r+s=p$. For radial pairs $(u,v)\in X_{\mathrm{rad}}\times X_{\mathrm{rad}}$, we determine the sharp constant $S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ}$ in the coupled inequality \[ S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ} \left(\int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^\ell\big(μ_1|u|^p+μ_2|v|^p+pκ|u|^r|v|^s\big)dx\right)^{2/p} \le \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^α\big(|Δu|^2+|Δv|^2\big)dx . \] The sharp constant is expressed through the scalar sharp constant and the minimum of an explicit one-dimensional ratio function. We also characterize all extremals and prove sharp quantitative stability estimates. The stability exponent is determined by the degeneracy of the ratio minimizers: it is quadratic in the non-degenerate case and becomes square-root type in the degenerate case.

title: An additive-square-free word over an alphabet of size 6
abstract: An additive square over $\mathbb{N}$ is two consecutive nonempty blocks of the same length and same sum. For example, 1423 is an additive square, since 14 and 23 both have length 2 and sum 5. Solving a problem that has been open for more than 50 years, we give an example of an infinite word over a 6-letter subset of N that avoids additive squares.

title: Worst-case bias of the independence assumption for functions of two ordinal variables
abstract: Let ordinal grades $X$ and $Y$ be obtained by cutting a pair of random variables with copula $C$ at arbitrary thresholds, and let $g$ be a function of the grades. We study the largest error $S_C(g)$, over all thresholds, that is, over all marginal laws, made when the mean of $g(X,Y)$ is computed as if the grades were independent. This is the counterpart of the classical dependence-uncertainty problem: the copula is fixed and the discretisation is free. The error is caused entirely by the interaction of the inputs, measured by an index $ρ(g)$, the largest absolute $g$-volume of a rectangle of grades, which vanishes if and only if $g$ is additive. For every copula, $S_C(g)$ lies between $ρ(g)$ times the largest deviation of $C$ from the independence copula and $ρ(g)$ times half the total variation of their difference, and the factor one half cannot be improved. For the Gaussian copula with correlation $λ$ we prove that $S_C(g)$ equals $|λ|ρ(g)/(2π)$ to first order, with a sharp constant and an explicit remainder. The same first-order law holds for copula families whose first-order departure from independence is a product of unimodal factors, including the Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern, Ali-Mikhail-Haq, Frank, Clayton and Plackett families, and we characterise the Archimedean families with this property. An application to the TNM staging of colon cancer, with data from a clinical trial, compares the bounds with the actual error of the independence computation.

title: Multiplicity criteria for the absolutely continuous spectrum of finite hopping Hermitian operators
abstract: We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.

title: Global nonsolvability of the leafwise $\dbar$-equation on foliations with Stein leaves
abstract: Motivated by our previous work on $q$-convexity and global solvability for Levi flat structures, we study the complex foliation associated with the non-tame family of Stein structures constructed by Forstneri\v c and Sigurðardóttir. Although every leaf is closed and biholomorphic to $\C^2$ and the foliation admits a complete bundle-like Riemannian metric, there exists a smooth leafwise $\dbar$-closed $(0,1)$-form for which the leafwise $\dbar$-equation admits no global $L^r_{\loc}$ solution for any $0<r\le\infty$. This result also suggests a modification of Questions~2.10.4--2.10.6 in \emph{Foliations: Dynamics, Geometry and Topology}.

title: Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
abstract: Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_α(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $ν(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $α\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_α(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.

title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

title: Sharp Sobolev thresholds and rapid rotation for Navier--Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation
abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with fractional horizontal dissipation $νΛ_h^{2α}$, $0<α\le1$, and a Coriolis force. There is no vertical dissipation. The scaling-critical Sobolev index is $s_c=5/2-2α$. For $0<α<1$, we prove local Hadamard well-posedness in $H^s$ for $s\ge s_c$; for $α=1$, the range is $s>1/2$. At every prescribed finite rotation rate, norm inflation holds in all remaining positive-order Sobolev spaces for classical solutions with smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, starting from arbitrarily small $H^s$ data in arbitrarily short time. Thus $H^{s_c}$ is a well-posedness space for $0<α<1$, whereas $H^{1/2}$ exhibits norm inflation for $α=1$. These results give sharp Sobolev thresholds for each finite rotation rate. Throughout the well-posedness range, small data yield global solutions with a rotation-independent smallness threshold, and every fixed datum yields a global solution for sufficiently rapid rotation. The nonlinear solution converges to the linear Stokes--Coriolis evolution uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ and in the global dissipation norm as $|Ω|\to\infty$. For spectrally localized data separated from the vertical frequency axis, the convergence rate is $O(|Ω|^{-γ})$ for every $0<γ<1/2$. For $0<α<1$, the energy estimates close at $s=s_c$ without loss of derivatives in isotropic Sobolev spaces, using Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Sobolev trace inequalities, and localized horizontal product estimates. Below $s_c$, norm inflation follows from an approximation by a fixed smooth Euler solution after rescaling. At $(α,s)=(1,1/2)$, viscosity remains fixed under critical rescaling; the construction instead uses a localized scalar shear and conormal analytic stability estimates uniform in the vertical concentration parameters.

title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
abstract:
We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures.
  Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number

title: Parameter estimation for discretely observed rough fractional interacting particle systems
abstract: We study parametric inference for interacting particle systems driven by independent fractional Brownian motions, based on discrete observations of all particles over a fixed time horizon. Our goal is to estimate an unknown drift parameter in the joint limit as the number of particles increases and the observation mesh vanishes. For $H>\frac 12$, we construct contrast based estimators by extending the discrete time least squares approach of Neuenkirch and Tindel to the interacting setting. For the rough regime $H\in(\frac 14,\frac 12)$, we introduce a modified contrast and use the stochastic sewing lemma to handle the first order approximations available from discrete observations. Our analysis combines the propagation of chaos for the associated fractional McKean Vlasov equation with estimates controlling the temporal discretization error. When the Hurst parameter and the diffusion coefficient are known, we establish strong consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators. The asymptotic results reveal an interplay between the number of particles and the temporal discretization: the convergence rate with respect to the observation mesh changes at $H=\frac 34$, while the asymptotic normality holds in both regimes considered. We further develop a joint estimation procedure for the drift parameter, the Hurst parameter, and the diffusion coefficient, extending quadratic-variation methods for fractional Brownian motion to the interacting particle framework. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators.

title: Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
abstract:
We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field.
  Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors using the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent. In this work, we complement this approach with the asymptotic analysis of the double contour integral. The integrals are moved to the double cover of the Harnack curve. We analyze the effect of the first two transformations of the Deift-Zhou method, and deform the contours to the relevant saddle points. We visualize our asymptotic analysis on the amoeba of the Harnack curve, in the spirit of the work of Berggren and Borodin on the doubly periodic Aztec diamond.

title: A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
abstract: The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons. The main step towards deriving the semialgebraic description is the observation that we need to consider only finitely many ellipses that go through some of the vertices of the inner polygon and are tangent to some of the edges of the outer polygon. Although the description is not completely quantifier-free, for a general matrix, the quantified variables satisfy a system of polynomial equations that has at most four solutions corresponding to reduced conics.

title: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
abstract: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $ψ$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $ψ$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $ψ$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013).

title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. Bérczi and Fehér conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

title: Hull variation of algebraic geometry codes under divisor twists
abstract:
The hull $\mathrm{Hull}(\mathcal{C})=\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{C}^{\perp}$ of a linear code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ interpolates between linear complementary dual (LCD) codes, with trivial hull, and self-dual codes. Its dimension is preserved by coordinate permutations but not by scalings $\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathbf{x}\cdot\mathcal{C}$, $\mathbf{x}\in(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^n$. This governs the complexity of Sendrier's support-splitting algorithm and decides whether an equivalence class contains LCD codes. We study this hull-variation problem, formalised by Chen, for algebraic geometry codes $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ over a function field $\mathcal{F}/\mathbb{F}_q$ of genus $g>0$, where scalings are twists of $G$ by principal divisors; as a natural relaxation, we allow twists $G\mapsto G+L$ by arbitrary divisors.
  Writing $\mathcal{C}(D,G)^{\perp}=\mathcal{C}(D,H)$, with $H=D-G+W$, $W$ canonical, a twist acts by $(G,H)\mapsto(G+L,H-L)$. Whenever $\gcd(G+L,H-L)$ is non-special, the hull dimensions of $\mathcal{C}(D,G+L)$ and $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ differ by exactly $\frac12(\mathrm{deg}|G-H|-\mathrm{deg}|G-H+2L|)$. For a genuine scaling, $L=-(z)$, this variation is bounded by $2[\mathcal{F}:\mathbb{F}_q(z)]$. Under the same hypothesis, we obtain an upper bound on the hull dimension depending only on $D$ and $W$, and characterise exactly when it is attained by a scaling of it. These bounds shed new light on Chen's maximal hull dimension; explicit scalings on Kummer extensions show that the first is sharp. We construct explicit twists that raise, respectively lower, the hull dimension by prescribed amounts, one unit at a time, and apply them to two classical families. Starting from known LCD codes, we reach every hull dimension in an explicit range; starting from a self-dual code ($q$ even) or a code of maximal hull dimension ($q$ odd), we descend to $0$, yielding LCD codes of various dimensions.

title: A counterexample to Molchan's orthant persistence conjecture
abstract: We refute Molchan's conjecture that the persistence probability of the isotropic fractional Brownian field on $[0,R]^d$ satisfies $p_{d,H}(R)=R^{-d(1-H)+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$. We prove $$ \limsup_{d\to\infty}\limsup_{R\to\infty} \frac{-\log p_{d,H}(R)}{d\log R} \le 1-\frac{49}{48}H+o(H), \qquad H\downarrow 0. $$ Thus the conjecture fails for every sufficiently small fixed Hurst parameter in all sufficiently large dimensions. A finite-step Gaussian interpolation inequality on the exact positive sphere is proved in an appendix.

title: Conditional Mean-Field Type Linear Quadratic Optimal Control Problem for Regime-Switching Diffusions with Indefinite Coefficients
abstract: We study a conditional mean-field type linear quadratic optimal control problem for regime-switching diffusions with indefinite weights. The dynamics and cost depend on conditional expectations of the state and control given the history of the Markov chain. Under standard definiteness conditions, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the optimal control and derive its feedback representation and optimal cost through two sets of coupled Riccati equations and a linear backward stochastic differential equation driven by the Markov chain. To treat the case of indefinite weights, we extend the equivalent cost functional approach to this setting using regime-dependent quadratic adjustments for the conditional mean of the state and its deviation from that mean. When the transformed weights in the equivalent cost functional satisfy standard definiteness conditions, this construction yields unique solvability of the original Hamiltonian system and a feedback representation of the unique optimal control. The proposed results also provide an effective method for establishing the solvability of fully coupled linear conditional mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations that do not satisfy certain existing monotonicity conditions. We further apply the results to conditional mean-variance portfolio selection with exogenous liability in an incomplete regime-switching market and derive the optimal investment strategy.

title: (Non-)existence of complex structures on $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras
abstract: In this paper we determine which $8$-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent real Lie algebras admit (integrable) complex structures. We construct explicit examples on $40$ out of the $43$ isomorphism classes, and show that there are obstructions to the existence of complex structures on the remaining three isomorphism classes. These obstructions are related to the set of elements of rank $2$ in the pencil defining the Lie algebra structure. We also show that for any even-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$, the direct sum $\mathfrak{g}:=\mathbb{R}^2\oplus \mathfrak{h}$ (and also some other, more general, extensions of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by $\mathfrak{h}$) admits a complex structure if and only if $\mathfrak{h}$ admits a complex structure. In particular, this allows us to construct the first examples of $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras in every even dimension $2n\geq8$ which do not admit complex structures. Finally, we show that every even-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebra with $2$-dimensional center admits a complex structure.

title: Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical
abstract:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule. If the canonical map $H_0\to H/J(H)$ is surjective, then $H$ is generated by $H_0$ if and only if $H=H_0^3+J(H)^2$, where $H_0^3$ is the span of products of three elements of $H_0$.
  For finite locally free Hopf algebras of constant rank over a $k$-scheme in characteristic zero, including duals of liftings of a given Nichols algebra, the locus where this property holds is Zariski open and compatible with arbitrary base change.
  For a finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $K$ with abelian coradical over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the largest Hopf ideal contained in $J(K)$ is determined. $K^*$ is generated by its coradical if and only if $J(K)$ contains no nonzero skew-primitive elements. For liftings of quantum linear spaces and standard liftings of finite Cartan type, this condition is expressed in terms of the deformation parameters of $K$.

title: Failure of the $L^p$ Neumann problem in bi-Lipschitz images of a ball
abstract: For every $n\geq 2$ we construct a bounded domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}$, which is the image of the unit ball under a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, and a bounded Neumann datum $g$ with zero mean such that the variational solution $u$ of the Neumann problem with datum $g$ satisfies $\mathcal N(\nabla u)\notin L^1(\partialΩ)$. In particular, the $L^p$ Neumann problem is not solvable in $Ω$ for any $1<p<\infty$, although $Ω$ is a two-sided chord-arc domain whose boundary supports a weak $(1,1)$-Poincaré inequality, and although in this class of domains the Dirichlet and the regularity problems are solvable for some exponents. This answers in the negative a question of C. Kenig, and it also shows that, unlike the solvability of the Dirichlet problem, the solvability of the $L^p$ Neumann problem for some $p\in (1,\infty)$ is not invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.

title: Recent developments in stochastic systems with singular dynamics -- a brief survey --
abstract: Diffusions with singular drifts appear naturally in the study of certain classes of interesting particle systems. Due to the singularities involved in the equations describing them, studying their dynamics is both interesting and challenging as they fall outside of the usual regularity assumptions on the vector fields in the literature. One needs to introduce and study them with different methods, with the use of symmetric polynomials being a particularly promising approach. In this expository work, we give an overview of some models and methods, and we further explore their interactions with the areas of Multiple Loewner chains (in particular, multiple Schramm-Loewner Evolutions), the new links with Random Matrices, and the novel area of Machine Learning for Singular Dynamics.

title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Residual-based methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), physics-informed Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, and some physics-informed neural operator architectures, approximate PDE solutions by minimizing a discrete least-squares loss formed from the PDE and boundary residuals over a prescribed trial class. This structure is shared by classical least-squares Kansa collocation, whose kernel trial spaces admit an established convergence theory. For neural trial classes, approximation power alone does not ensure that discrete residuals control the continuous solution error. For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, we extend the kernel-based collocation framework to neural trial classes through elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency. Elliptic regularity supplies the PDE estimate relating solution error to continuous residuals. Discrete stability identifies admissible trial subclasses in which continuous residuals are controlled by a computable discrete loss. This step also quantifies the required number of collocation points. Furthermore, the stability analysis naturally demands a scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weight. For the constrained problem, consistency requires accurate comparison functions within the same admissible subclass, a requirement not supplied by neural approximation estimates alone. Specializing to multilayer perceptrons with tanh activations (tanh-MLPs), we construct admissible comparison networks and establish convergence for the constrained residual minimization problem. We further obtain conditional convergence of unconstrained physics-balanced PINNs based on tanh-MLPs under joint network and sampling refinement.

title: Mixed-integer programming formulations for the quadratic bin packing problem: linearization, hybridization, and enhancements
abstract: The quadratic bin packing problem (QBPP) extends the classical bin packing problem by incorporating pairwise dissimilarity values between items assigned to the same bin. The objective is to minimize the total cost, composed of the cost associated with the number of bins used and the sum of pairwise dissimilarity values for items assigned to the same bin, subject to the bin-capacity constraints. We study the quadratic programming formulation together with a broad family of equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for the QBPP based on classical linearization techniques. We analyze the relationships among the linear programming relaxations of the MILP formulations and strengthen several of these relaxations by exploiting the structure of the QBPP. We further introduce the first hybrid exact formulation for the QBPP that combines elements of two distinct modeling approaches. In particular, we show that the combination of explicit bin patterns and assignment-based representation performs particularly well. For the hybrid formulation, we investigate the effect of item selection, and for both the hybrid and non-hybrid formulations, we study the impact of item ordering on formulation size, relaxation strength and computational performance. Although a recently introduced tailored branch-and-price algorithm remains the state-of-the-art for the QBPP, we show that the proposed ordering-based non-hybrid and hybrid formulations substantially improve computational performance over the best MILP formulation known to the literature, in addition of solving 33 new benchmark instances to optimality.

title: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Exact Bounds and Extremizers
abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy $D(P\|Q)$ in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences $χ^2(P\|Q)$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)$. For any $A,B>0$, the constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)\leq A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)\leq B$ yield upper bounds on $D(P\|Q)$ and $D(Q\|P)$. Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions each attain both bounds simultaneously. As a consequence, for sequences of probability mass functions $\{P_n\}$ and $\{Q_n\}$ on a common finite or countably infinite alphabet, both $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ and $D(Q_n\|P_n)$ tend to zero whenever one of the two ordered chi-squared divergences tends to zero and the other remains uniformly bounded. Without this boundedness assumption, $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ can fail to converge to zero even when $χ^2(Q_n\|P_n)\to 0$. Finally, in contrast to the attainable upper bounds, on any finite or countably infinite alphabet containing at least three elements, the infimum of $D(P\|Q)$ under the exact constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)=A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)=B$ is zero and is not attained.

title: Asymptotics for generalized integer partitions
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of weighted partition functions $p_f(n)$, defined by the generating function $\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^{n})^{-f(n)}$ with non-negative real weights $f(n)$. We assume that the associated Dirichlet series $D(s) = \sum_{n \geq 1} f(n) n^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to a half-plane $\Re(s) \geq -\varepsilon$, with finitely many real poles of arbitrary orders, the largest of which is a positive pole $α$ of order $k$, and a possibly infinite collection of complex poles lying strictly to the left of $α$, with some additional conditions. We extend the saddle-point method of Debruyne and Tenenbaum, and show that the pole $α$ dominates the contribution of all other poles. As a result, we give an explicit asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$ described via generalized Lambert functions. Furthermore, we show that for $k \geq 2$ no finite combination of powers of $n$, $\log n$, $\log \log n, \ldots$ approximates the saddle point well enough to give an asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$. We also discuss a number of applications related to algebra, number theory, and combinatorics.

title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya--Szegö
abstract: We prove the polygonal Saint--Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya and Szegö: for every $n\geq 3$, among (possibly non--convex) polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity. The proof is purely analytic and stems from the local version of the result given in our previous paper: it combines an area--angle proportional partition of a polygon, inspired by Solynin and Zalgaller, with a sharp comparison for the mixed torsional rigidity of the partition cells, and with an angular concavity property of this functional on the class of isosceles triangles.

title: Treewidth 3 in the Product Structure Theorem for Bounded Degree Graphs in Minor-Closed Classes
abstract: We show that, for all positive integers $t$ and $Δ$, there exists an integer $c$ such that, for every $K_t$-minor-free graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $Δ$, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $3$ and a path $P$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the strong product $H\boxtimes P\boxtimes K_c$. This improves on a previous result of Dujumović, Esperet, Micek, Walczak, and Wood (2022) by bounding the treewidth of $H$ independently of $t$ and $Δ$. As an immediate consequence we obtain a bound of $O(r^4)$ on the $r$-weak colouring number of bounded-degree graphs from any proper minor-closed graph class.

title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
abstract: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose pattern can be unknotted in the solid torus by a single rational tangle replacement.

title: Asymptotic Error of the Euler--Maruyama Scheme for McKean--Vlasov SDEs Driven by $α$-Stable Processes
abstract: We study the continuous-time Euler--Maruyama error for McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by symmetric $α$-stable noise, $1<α<2$. We assume globally Lipschitz coefficients, a bounded jump coefficient, and bounded Lipschitz state derivatives and law-derivative kernels. The error normalized by $(n/\log n)^{1/α}$ converges jointly with the original driver in the multivariate Skorokhod $J_1$ topology, and hence stably relative to the driver's path. The limit solves a linear SDE driven by the original noise and an independent symmetric $α$-stable process. Conditional centering removes both law-derivative terms from the limiting equation. For $1\leqslant p<α$, the Euler schemes based on the numerical and exact marginal laws differ by $o((\log n/n)^{1/α})$ in the $L^p$ norm of the path supremum. Their normalized errors have the same limiting $p$th moment of the path supremum, which is positive if $σ(x_0,δ_{x_0})\partial_xσ(x_0,δ_{x_0})\ne 0$. For test functions in $C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$, the fixed-time weak error is $o((\log n/n)^{1/α})$.

title: Asymptotics of linear normal lambda terms: WKB structure, Airy turning point and a positive recurrence
abstract: Let a n be the number of closed linear $λ$-terms in $β$-normal form with n variable occurrences. We prove  is the large-order constant of the Riccati-Airy sequence K m attached to the turning point of the WKB expansion. We show that the K m are exactly rescaled coefficients of the formal logarithmic derivative of the Airy asymptotic series, and deduce $κ$ $\infty$ = 1/(2$π$) from the explicit Airy coefficients. Hence  The proof combines four further ingredients: (i) the WKB coefficients are polynomials with nonnegative coefficients in v = (1 -4w) -1/2 and satisfy an explicit positive recurrence; (ii) the linearisation of the WKB equation has a combinatorial meaning ($λ$-chain terms) and is a translation in the action coordinate s, whose singularity sits at the instanton action A 0 = ln 2 -1 2\,; (iii) an exact identity shows that, after conjugation by the transported WKB prefactor $μ$ = r/(1+r) 2 , the remaining non-linear terms are either negative or of relative size O(m -2 ); (iv) under the conjugated linear dynamics the depth profile is dominated by its top coefficient. A finite bound on an explicit ratio sequence is obtained by exact computer arithmetic (the program is given in an appendix); it also yields a n $\le$ 1.14736 f '' n (1) for all n, with f '' n (1) $\sim$ 5 144 (n -1)!$λ$ n .

title: Global well-posedness and decay estimates of strong solutions to a non-conservative compressible two-fluid model in $L^p$ critical framework
abstract: We investigate the global existence and long-time behavior of solutions to a general multidimensional non-conservative compressible two-fluid model satisfying the algebraic capillary pressure relation \(P^{+}(ρ^+)-P^{-}(ρ^-)=f(α^{-}ρ^{-})\) in the $L^p$ critical framework. Our main contributions are twofold. First, under the sharp stability condition \(-\frac{s_{-}^{2}(1,1)}{α^{-}(1,1)}<f^{\prime}(1)<0,\) we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions for small perturbations around a linearly stable constant equilibrium. In particular, our result removes the additional negativity assumption required in Evje--Wang--Wen [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 221:1285--1316, 2016]. Second, assuming in addition that the low-frequency of the initial perturbation is small in a lower-regularity Besov space, we derive optimal decay rates for the solution.

title: Induced matching treewidth in classes with a forbidden structure
abstract:
Induced matching treewidth is a tree-decomposition based parameter where we bound the size of an induced matching whose every edge intersects a single bag of the decomposition.
  It is known that many computational problems can be solved efficiently in graphs of bounded induced matching treewidth.
  In this paper we are interested in understanding what classes of graphs have bounded induced matching treewidth.
  We provide dichotomy theorems for all classes defined by excluding a single graph with respect to six basic containment relations: (induced) subgraph, (induced) topological minor, and (induced) minor.
  Furthermore, we study the case where the input graph has minimum degree at least 2, as well as the more restrictive case where it is 2-connected.
  This can be assumed without loss of generality for many computational problems.
  It turns out that for classes excluding some graph as an induced minor, this restrictions yield some new cases of bounded induced matching treewidth.
  As a consequence, our results imply new algorithmic results, as well as the existence of balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices in the considered classes. This confirms some special cases of two conjectures of Gartland and Lokshtanov.

title: Universal operators on Banach spaces
abstract: The paper studies universal operators and $n$-tuples of operators on Banach spaces. In the Hilbert-space setting, sufficient criteria for universality, concrete examples, and spectral properties are well established. We investigate extensions of these results to Banach spaces. In particular, we discuss the link between universality and the invariant subspace problem: this leads us to define a stronger notion of universality which is the notion of hereditarily universal operators. We give sufficient conditions for an operator to be hereditarily universal and provide some examples. We also study $n$-tuples of operators by generalizing Vladimir Müller's results to the Banach setting. Finally, we obtain a result on the essential spectrum of a universal $n$-tuple of operators on $\ell_p$.

title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
abstract:
We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio.
  For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined $(n+1)$-plane. To our knowledge, this is the first such convergence theorem for spherical free boundary MCF in arbitrary codimension. The closed theorem requires additional quadratic pinching for $5\leq n\leq7$, and the free boundary theorem for $4\leq n\leq7$. For $n\geq8$, the necessary quadratic bound follows from quadratic convexity.
  We also establish preservation of ordinary quadratic pinching $|A|^2\leq c|H|^2$ under spherical free boundary flow for $n\ge2$ and $\frac{9}{8n}\leq c\leq\frac{4}{3n}$, including both endpoints.

title: Quasimonomial Monge--Ampère equations for big classes
abstract: Let X be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We describe an alternative approach to a differentiability result of volumes of norms defined by finitely many quasimonomial valuations. As a consequence, we prove the non-Archimedean Calabi--Yau theorem for quasimonomial measures on $X$ with respect to big classes, in the trivially valued case. We also obtain continuity of solutions as numerical classes vary in the big cone. This extends previous results of Boucksom--Jonsson and Dervan--Reboulet, and gives the first uniqueness results in the big case. Our approach relies on convex geometry and Okounkov bodies, without involving non-Archimedean pluripotential theory or test configurations.

title: Trickle groups on a complete graph are linear
abstract: Trickle groups were recently introduced by Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris, as generalizations of both cactus groups and right-angled Coxeter and Artin groups. We construct a representation of any trickle group $\mathrm{Tr}(Γ)$ with complete graph $Γ$ on a space having a basis in bijection with the vertex set $V(Γ)$, and show that it is faithful. This in particular shows that trickle Garside groups are linear. It also allows one to realize every finite trickle group as a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_{|V(Γ)|}(\mathbb{C})$. We do not use the results of Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris; instead we rather show that several properties of trickle groups that they obtained (and also some new ones) can easily be proven in the particular case of a complete graph using our representation. This includes the normal forms, the embedding of the trickle monoid inside the group in the case where $μ(x)=\infty$ for all $x\in V(Γ)$, and the absence of torsion of the latter. In this last case we give a second proof of faithfulness in the spirit of Krammer-Hée, which explains how to read Garside-theoretic information from the representation.

title: The number of cycles in a random 2-factor of a random regular graph
abstract: We study the number of cycles $X$ in a uniformly random 2-factor $F$ of a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices (in the pairing model) for any fixed $d\ge 3$. When the pairing $P$ and the 2-factor $F\subseteq P$ are chosen uniformly at random together, the probability generating function of $X$ is $Γ(n+\tfrac u2)Γ(\tfrac12)/\bigl(Γ(n+\tfrac12)Γ(\tfrac u2)\bigr)$, which does not depend on $d$. Consequently, $X$ has mean $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$ and variance $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$, satisfies a central limit theorem, and equals $1$ (so that $F$ is a Hamilton cycle) with probability $Θ(n^{-1/2})$. Using an exact formula for the second moment of the cycle generating polynomial together with small subgraph conditioning, we transfer these results to a uniformly random 2-factor of a fixed random regular graph.

title: An asymptotic ball algebra with countably determined spectra and a nonseparable character space
abstract: Let $X=\partial\mathbb B_2\subset\mathbb C^2$ and let $\mathcal R$ be the restrictions to $X$ of functions in the ball algebra $A(\overline{\mathbb B_2})$. The unital uniform Banach algebra \[ \mathcal A=\{(f_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X)):\mathrm{dist}_{C(X)}(f_n,\mathcal R)\longrightarrow0\} \] is inverse-closed in $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X))$. Consequently one countable family of evaluation characters generates the spectrum of every element of $\mathcal A$. Nevertheless $Δ(\mathcal A)$ contains continuum many pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets and is therefore nonseparable. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Ohrysko, Wojciechowski and Graham.

title: Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one
abstract: We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $χ=χ(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance. We prove that its nonvanishing condition holds whenever $\sum_i n_i\le2χ+4$, where $I_{n_i}$ are the reducible fibers; hence every such surface is a Mori dream surface. Independently of this condition, we exclude ample generator degrees throughout the stated cone range. We also determine the section--fiber subring and give minimal complete-intersection presentations when all $s$ reducible fibers have type $I_2$ and $s\le2χ+1$, including the endpoint beyond that cone range.

title: Taming the Tails of Stochastic Gradient Descent in the Interpolation Regime
abstract: In this paper, we study stochastic gradient descent in the smooth interpolation regime, where the population objective shares a common minimizer with the sample losses. In contrast to prior work, which has largely focused on in-expectation analysis, we obtain high-probability convergence guarantees under the same assumptions. In the convex case, we prove a fast rate of order $\log(β^{-1}) \cdot n^{-1}$ after $n$ iterations, with failure probability at most $β$. In the strongly convex case, we derive a family of moment-based bounds of order $β^{-p} \cdot \exp(-\mathcal{O}(p \cdot n))$ for $p \in (0,1]$, and complement them with a matching lower bound showing that the corresponding deterioration in the exponential rate is essentially unavoidable. In both settings, our theoretical results are unified across a broad class of step-size schedules. Building on this analysis, we extend our results to a low-noise regime and to nonconvex objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.

title: A Cohen--Macaulay Analogue of the Brodmann--Rotthaus Theorem
abstract: We prove a Cohen--Macaulay analogue of the theorem of Brodmann and Rotthaus on the lifting of quasi-excellence. More precisely, let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I$ be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. We show that if $A/I$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-Q0 and $A$ is a $\mathsf{CM}$\textnormal{-G-}ring, then $A$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-quasi-excellent. Our proof follows the strategy of Kurano and Shimomoto and makes essential use of Česnavičius' Macaulayfication theorem.

title: An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs
abstract: Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate. We also give an explicit descent from Nielsen transitivity to transitivity under the Vieta involutions alone.

title: Energy decay and asymptotic profile for a system of damped wave equations
abstract: We consider a system of two wave or Klein-Gordon equations on the Euclidean space. One is damped, while the second is only indirectly damped via a coupling term. We are interested in the large time behavior of the solutions. More precisely, we prove energy decay for both components and, when possible, we give their asymptotic profiles. Our proofs are based on spectral analysis. We will see that in our setting the contribution of high frequencies always decays exponentially, so the results depend on the contribution of low frequencies. We observe a diffusive phenomenon as for a single wave equation, but the coupling between the two components gives completely different behaviors, depending on the nature of the equations and the strengths of the damping and coupling.

title: Sharp integral condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals
abstract: We show that the necessary and sufficient condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals with nonnegative i.i.d. vertex weights in every dimension $q\ge2$ is the same criterion for linear growth of directed last-passage times. We also obtain two-sided finite-size estimates, up to dimension-dependent constants, for the mean maximal weights of directed paths, lattice animals, valid for every nonnegative weights. These estimates determine the order of mean growth even when growth is superlinear. Since every up-right path from the origin is a lattice animal, the lower bound follows from the corresponding last-passage bound. For the upper bound, we couple the lattice weights to a Poisson process and represent each animal by a polygonal route of length proportional to its size.

title: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=λ(1+t)^{-μ}$ with $0<μ<1$, $λ>0$, or $μ=1$, $λ>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the spatially dependent damping coefficient, even though its contribution persists for all time. We also obtain decay estimates of order $\varepsilon(1+t)^{-μ}$ for the derivatives $u_t$, $v_t$, and $v_x$, together with a pointwise estimate for $u_x$ involving the spatial coefficient $a(x)$. The main ingredient is a time-uniform $L^\infty$ estimate for an inhomogeneous coupled transport system with a non-small spatial coefficient. Combined with suitable transformations of the Riemann-invariant derivatives, this estimate allows us to control the nonlinear terms and establish global $C^1$ bounds.

title: The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
abstract: We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam.

title: Finding four vertices of a square of area $n$ in a grid by geometric construction
abstract: In this study, we consider geometric construction in an infinite square grid. Our purpose is to find efficient methods for constructing a square of area $n\in\mathbb{N}$ based on arithmetic properties of the sum of squares. As a consequence, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we derive the optimal number of construction steps required to determine the four vertices of the square. Furthermore, we classify all positive integers into three classes according to these optimal numbers.

title: The n-th Zbáganu constant
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Banach spaces and investigate its basic properties. We establish some inequalities which give the relationship between the $n$-th Zbáganu constant and two other constants, namely the $n$-th Von Neumann-Jordan constant and the $n$-th James constant. In addition, we determine the values of the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Lebesgue spaces, Morrey spaces, and discrete Morrey spaces.

title: Two results on rich-neighbour $5$-colouring of subcubic graphs
abstract: A rich-neighbour edge-colouring is a proper edge-colouring in which every non-isolated edge has an adjacent edge whose neighbours have pairwise distinct colours. Petruševski and Škrekovski conjectured that every connected subcubic loopless multigraph distinct from $K_4$ admits such a colouring with five colours. We prove the conjecture for two classes: claw-free subcubic loopless multigraphs and $2$-connected subcubic outerplanar loopless multigraphs. The bound is sharp in both classes, as witnessed by the diamond $K_4-e$.

title: Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops
abstract: We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.

title: Rational v. Radical: Trajectory Properties of Iterated Bayesian Updates
abstract: Iterating Jeffrey's update on fixed evidence gives a maximum-likelihood estimate under suitable support conditions. What is less clear would be how the trajectories are organized, and what happens when we trace them in reverse. For a fixed strictly positive, invertible classical channel and full-support evidence, reverse iteration corresponds to repeated prior hacking. Almost every interior prior then approaches certainty in one possibility while each nontrivial step worsens agreement with the evidence. We call this limiting behavior radicalization. Priors that approach the same pure state form a Bayes phase. In the phase diagrams, the separating trajectories instead approach facet fixed points determined by M-projections. We also ask whether one can choose evidence that brings every interior prior to the same conclusion. For a strictly positive, invertible channel this is always possible, although one cannot always prescribe which conclusion it will be

title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$
abstract: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.

title: Quaternionic Torus Actions on Manifolds
abstract: We study smooth actions of quaternionic tori $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$ on closed, connected smooth manifolds, establishing sharp bounds for $r$ in terms of the dimension of the manifold when the action is either effective, effective almost-free, or almost-effective. In particular, we prove that an almost-effective $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$-action on an $n$-dimensional manifold satisfies $r\leq \lfloor2n/3\rfloor$, and we classify up to diffeomorphism all simply connected manifolds attaining the maximal possible rank. This gives a quaternionic counterpart of the maximal symmetry rank conjecture without any curvature assumption. We also establish the bounds $r\leq n/3$ for effective and effective almost-free quaternionic torus actions, and we compute the exact value for spheres, quoric manifolds, or manifolds of the form $(S^3)^a\times (S^1)^b$.

title: Power projections, Gram structures, and finite-field lifting of Butson Hadamard matrices
abstract: In this paper we investigate the algebraic properties of Hadamard powers of Butson Hadamard matrices $H\in \mathrm{BH}(n,3p)$, and show that for certain parameter values the cube root projection matrix $H^{\circ p}$ has the same structure as the adjacency matrix of a strongly regular graph. Then, by using a simple eigenvalue analysis we show, among other results, the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(17,15)$ matrices. For other parameter values, a more in-depth study and in particular, a complete classification of all possible projection matrices is necessary. We carry out this task for the case of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices, and using finite field techniques we show that none of these projections can be lifted up to form a Butson matrix. In particular, we show the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices for the first time.

title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
abstract:
$A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics.
  By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie.
  We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is unusual in that rather than defining them by localization, we construct our $\infty$-categories completely explicitly as simplicial sets.
  Our $\infty$-categories are intended for applications to Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry. Given a suitable symplectic manifold $(X,ω)$, one should construct its Fukaya category ${\mathscr F}(X,ω)$, a (filtered) $A_\infty$-category, and its derived Fukaya category $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,ω)$, a triangulated category (or better, a stable $\infty$-category). Typically ${\mathscr F}(X,ω)$ depends on many arbitrary choices. Our $\infty$-categories give a clean way to explain in what sense ${\mathscr F}(X,ω)$ and $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,ω)$ are independent of these choices.

title: A stratified version of geometric realizations
abstract: Given a simplicial set $X$, let $\operatorname{B}({X})$ denote its poset of nondegenerate simplices. We define a natural stratification $\left\vert{X}\right\vert\rightarrow\operatorname{B}({X})$. When $X$ is locally finite, we prove that this stratification is conical. Moreover, if $X$ is finite, we prove that the exit path category $\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ satisfies the geometric realization formula $\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\limits_{σ:Δ[p]\rightarrow X} \operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({p})}(Δ^p)\simeq\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ where the colimit is indexed by the category of simplices of $X$.

title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square torus
abstract: For each $1<s<2$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$.
