The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a periodic one-dimensional solution of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier.

title: A Geometric Calderón Problem for Differential Forms
abstract: We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

title: Divisibility of Character Values of Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group whose character table is integer-valued, and let $K$ be any fixed positive integer. We prove that almost every entry of the character table of the wreath product $G\wr S_N$ is divisible by $K$ as $N\to\infty$.

title: Uniqueness of coexistence states in diffusive predator-prey models, at the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the first publication of V. Volterra on the predator-prey system
abstract: This paper analyzes the existence and uniqueness of coexistence states for a generalized class of diffusive Lotka--Volterra predator-prey models involving spatial heterogeneities and mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type. Its main findings are the following: (a) after characterizing the existence of coexistence states, the uniqueness of the coexistence state is established, in a multidimensional context, near the curves of change of stability of the semi-trivial positive solutions of the model, (b) the one-dimensional uniqueness theorem of López-Gómez and Pardo [65,67] is sharpened up to cover the case of mixed boundary conditions of nonclassical type, (c) the multidimensional uniqueness theorem of [66] is substantially generalized up to deal with variable coefficients, and it is complemented with the global attractivity of the unique coexistence state, which excludes any Hopf bifurcation, (d) assuming Neumann boundary conditions and constant coefficients, we can sharpen, very substantially, the pioneering results of Leung [46] establishing the the constant coexistence state is the unique coexistence state of the model. In this setting, we can also prove that the constant coexistence state is a global attractor with respect to the positive solutions of the associated parabolic problem, and that it is non-degenerate, even for general differential operators, not necessarily self-adjoint. \par As this paper is a personal homage to Volterra [92] at the centenary of the publication of his foundational paper on the predator-prey model, based on the field data of D'Ancona [4], this paper begins with a review of the first scientific works in population dynamics of Vito Volterra and Umberto D'Ancona.

title: On the Vertex Growth Rate of Integer Partition Polytopes and Their Non-Vertex Structure
abstract:
The Hardy-Ramanujan formula states that the asymptotic growth of the number of integer partitions of $n$ is $\exp(Θ(\sqrt{n}\,))$. We prove that the number of vertices of the integer partition polytope is bounded by $\exp\left(\mathcal{O}(\ln^2 n)\right)$. This implies that all partitions of $n$ can be generated from a negligible subset of vertex partitions using convex combinations.
  We also present new computational data on the structure of non-vertex partitions, which cause the huge gap between the number of vertices and the total number of partitions.

title: On least energy solutions for a critical nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the competitive case
abstract: We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger system with Sobolev critical nonlinearities and repulsive interaction involving all the components at the same time. Under the scalar Brezis-Nirenberg assumptions on the linear coefficients, we prove existence of least energy fully non-trivial solutions on smooth bounded domains for every negative coupling in dimensions \(N=5,6\). For \(N=3,4\), due to the lack of $L^2$-integrability of the Aubin-Talenti bubbles, the same conclusion holds under additional sufficient assumptions, and in particular we provide an explicit condition on the domain and coefficients. We also investigate the strong competition limit, and characterize fully non-trivial limiting profiles as minimizers of a partially segregated variational problem. A preliminary study of independent interest concerns the whole-space problem. For general admissible \(K\), we determine the component-wise Nehari infimum and prove that it is not attained, even in the radial class. Finally, when the linear coefficients coincide, we establish a sharp criterion for the existence of positive synchronized solutions in terms of the strength of the competition.

title: Whitehead doubles and the failure of the AJ conjecture
abstract: For marked Whitehead doubles of torus knots with coprime parameters $2\le r<s$, the AJ conjecture fails for both clasp signs, both companion chiralities, and every integer twist. The zero-framed signed unreduced colored Jones sequence has a nonzero rationally saturated annihilator. Every nonzero primitive representative specializes nontrivially at $t=-1$ with the meridian variable $M$ independent. With $L$ the longitude variable, the specialization contains the irreducible quadratic $E=L^2-(M^4-4M^2+1)L+M^4$ for the negative clasp and $M^4E(M^{-1},L)$ for the positive clasp. The corresponding quadratic is coprime to the full classical $A$-polynomial, including $L-1$, over $\mathbb{Q}(M)[L^{\pm1}]$, so the discrepancy persists when each irreducible factor is counted once. The curve $E=0$ comes from the marked Whitehead link exterior with its axis cusp complete. For the displayed monic polynomial, $πm(E)$ is the unsigned volume of that two-cusped exterior. We use the actual Jones sequence to select a right divisor of the satellite transfer operator. Rational factor tests show that the quadratic survives in this divisor, and the two marked companion fillings exclude it as a component of the satellite boundary curve.

title: On the $L^p$-Neumann problem for divergence form elliptic equations in the upper half-space
abstract:
A central question has been whether the $L^p$-Neumann problem is solvable for some $p\in(1,\infty)$ in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+:=\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty)$, $n\geq2$, for second-order uniformly elliptic equations in divergence form whose coefficients are either independent of the transverse variable or satisfy the Dahlberg--Kenig--Pipher (DKP) condition. We answer this question in the negative for both classes, even for matrices whose symmetric part is the identity. The two examples have the same nonzero Neumann datum $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ of mean zero. Although $g$ is bounded and belongs to the real Hardy space $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, neither equation admits a weak solution with this datum whose gradient has a non-tangential maximal function in $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ for any $1\leq p<\infty$. For the variational solution $u$ associated with either matrix $A$, the non-tangential maximal functions of $\nabla_x u$, $\partial_tu$ and $(A\nabla u)_{n+1}$ each have infinite $L^p$ norm for every $1\leq p\leq\infty$.
  In the example with coefficients independent of the transverse variable, the equation in the interior is the Laplace equation. The matrix in the DKP example has finite $L^2$-type Carleson discrepancy from the identity. This shows that solvability of the $L^p$-Neumann problem is not stable under arbitrary Carleson perturbations of the identity. For a suitable choice of the coefficients in the lower half-space, the $L^2$ non-tangential maximal and uniform slice estimates fail for both the tangential gradient and the transverse derivative of the associated single layer potential. The $L^2$ estimate for the tangential gradient of its boundary trace also fails. We explain the role of the coefficients below the boundary and prove the $L^2$ layer potential estimates for the reflected extension when the DKP norm is sufficiently small.

title: Behind the equivalent descriptions of the Loewner energy
abstract: This expository paper retells the story behind the paper "Equivalent descriptions of the Loewner energy," which uncovered the link between random fractal SLE curves and the Kähler geometry of universal Teichmüller space via the Loewner energy. It is written for the Proceedings of ICBS as the summary paper for the 2026 Frontiers of Science award.

title: Quadratic splitting for a weighted Monge--Ampère equation on $(0,\infty)^l\times\R^m$
abstract: We study a Monge--Ampère equation arising from the existence problem for complete Kähler--Einstein metrics with zero Ricci curvature on divisor complements. We prove a splitting theorem for nonnegative smooth strictly convex solutions on a product of positive half lines and a Euclidean space. The potential and its first derivatives extend continuously to the boundary. The directional derivative in the equation is positive in the interior and vanishes on the boundary. After an affine change of variables, the solution is the sum of a function on the product of half lines and a positive definite quadratic form in the Euclidean variables. No growth condition or homogeneity is assumed.

title: On automorphisms of symplectic varieties acting trivially on the second cohomology group
abstract: We prove that the group of automorphisms acting trivially on the torsion-free part of the integral second cohomology on a primitive symplectic variety is a locally trivial deformation invariant. We exhibit some examples of this invariant.

title: Flexibility for the Monge-Ampere system implies flexibility for isometric immersions into Riemannian manifolds
abstract: We prove that any flexibility result for the Monge-Ampère system implies the corresponding flexibility result for the isometric immersion system, with the same Hölder regularity. We treat the general isometric immersion system, in which both the source and the ambient metrics are arbitrary Hölder regular, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. Combining this implication with existing results for the Monge-Ampère system, we obtain new ${C}^{1,α}$ flexibility statement for isometric immersions with arbitrary source and ambient metrics. To our knowledge, these are the first such results for non-Euclidean ambient metrics.

title: Sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation and non-uniqueness in passive scalar transport
abstract: We prove that for any concave, non-Osgood modulus of continuity $ω$, there exists a divergence-free velocity field $u\in L^\infty([0,1];C^ω(\mathbb T^2))$ and an initial data $f_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^2)$ such that the solutions of the associated advection-diffusion equation exhibit anomalous dissipation. This establishes the sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation. It follows as a corollary of our main result that the Osgood condition is also sharp for the uniqueness of bounded solutions to the transport equation.

title: Sixth and twelfth moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions in prime power moduli
abstract: For a fixed odd prime $p$ and $q=p^n$, we establish power-saving bounds for the sixth and twelfth moments of central values of primitive Dirichlet $L$-functions, with exponents $5/4-3/332$ and $2-51/261961$, respectively. More generally, our methods yield a power saving over the classical interpolation bound for every moment of order $4<j\le12$. Our approach begins with short second moments over character cosets and preserves the dependence on the character parameter. An exact linearization of the $p$-adic stationary phases reduces the critical large-value range to exponential sums with perturbed square-root phases over prime-power rings. We establish a large-value estimate for these sums by combining congruence-spacing bounds, higher congruence energies, and an average of quadratic Gauss sums over the dual frequency. For the remaining high-value range, we develop an incomplete-correlation estimate using $p$-adic exponent pairs.

title: Smooth structures on polyhedral products of disks and spheres
abstract: We prove that every polyhedral product of disks and their boundary spheres that is a topological manifold admits a stably parallelizable smooth structure. We also show that if a moment-angle complex or a real moment-angle complex admits a smooth structure for which the coordinate action is smooth, then the link of every face of the underlying simplicial complex is a simplicial sphere, and every such smooth structure is stably parallelizable.

title: The Holomorphic Reduction of Pseudoconvex Homogeneous Manifolds
abstract: Suppose $G$ is a connected complex Lie group and $H$ is a closed complex subgroup. Then there exists a closed complex subgroup $J$ of $G$ containing $H$ such that the fibration $π:G/H \to G/J$ is the holomorphic reduction of $G/H$, i.e., $G/J$ is holomorphically separable and ${\mathcal O}(G/H) \cong π^*{\mathcal O}(G/J)$. In this paper we prove that if $G/H$ is pseudoconvex, i.e., if $G/H$ admits a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion function, then $G/J$ is Stein and $J/H$ has no non-constant holomorphic functions.

title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
abstract: For $κ\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_κ$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circψ^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

title: Inversion of Set-Valued Wiener Models
abstract: A Wiener system consists of a linear system followed by a nonlinear system. This paper addresses the problem of recovering a vector in a Hilbert space from the outputs of multiple Wiener systems. While prior literature on provably convergent methods has studied this problem under the assumption that the nonlinear operators are single-valued and firmly nonexpansive, we investigate the broader setting in which the nonlinear operators are set-valued and maximally cohypomonotone. We design a splitting algorithm for this extended framework and establish its convergence. Our framework remains novel even in the special case of maximally monotone operators. Numerical applications to signal and image recovery are presented.

title: Einstein Constants and Smooth Topology, Revisited
abstract: In 1997, Catanese and the first author showed that, for every $m\geq 2$, there exists a smooth closed $4m$-manifold that admits both a $λ> 0$ Einstein metric and a $λ< 0$ Einstein metric; thus, the sign of the Einstein constant $λ$ is not always determined by the differential topology of the host compact manifold. This result was later improved by Răsdeaconu and Şuvaina (2009), who showed that there are in fact at least $\binom{m + 3}{3}$ topologically distinct such examples in each dimension $4m$, $m\geq 2$. In this note, we further improve these earlier results by showing that infinitely many topologically distinct examples of this phenomenon actually occur in dimension $4m$, for each $m\geq 2$.

title: Sharp Partial Regularity of Weakly Pseudoholomorphic Maps Into Projective Algebraic Varieties
abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that a weakly pseudoholomorphic $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ map from a real-analytic almost complex $2m$-manifold into a projective algebraic variety has a countably $(2m-4)$-rectifiable singular set. When $m=2$, the singular set is shown to be locally finite. We first establish both conclusions on smooth almost complex domains under the additional assumption that the pullback of the Fubini--Study form is distributionally closed. We then show that this conservation law follows from the Cauchy--Riemann equation alone on real-analytic domains.

title: On cyclic codes generated by cyclotomic polynomials
abstract: Let $n$ be a composite positive integer coprime to $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and let $t = \operatorname{lpf}(n)$ be the least prime factor of $n$. In this paper we study the cyclic codes $\mathcal{C}_{n,t} = \langle Q_n(X)Q_t(X)\rangle$ and $\mathcal{C}_{n,t,1} = \langle Q_n(X)Q_t(X)Q_1(X)\rangle$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $Q_d(X)$ denotes the $d$-th cyclotomic polynomial. These codes extend the families $\mathcal{C}_n = \langle Q_n(X)\rangle$ and $\mathcal{C}_{n,1} = \langle Q_n(X)Q_1(X)\rangle$ recently studied by Bhagat and Sarma. We determine the exact minimum distances of $\mathcal{C}_{n,t}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{n,t,1}$, showing that $d(\mathcal{C}_{n,t,1}) = 2t$ and that $d(\mathcal{C}_{n,t})$ equals $t$ if $t^2 \nmid n$, and $2t$ if $t^2 \mid n$. For the dual codes, we establish $d(\mathcal{C}_{n,t}^\perp) = 2^{ω(n)}$, handling the case $ω(n) \le 2$ via the Hartmann--Tzeng bound, and the case $ω(n) \ge 3$ via a direct-sum decomposition $\mathcal{C}_{n,t}^\perp = \mathcal{C}_n^\perp \oplus \mathcal{V}_t$ and the tensor-product structure of $\mathcal{C}_n^\perp$ over its prime-power components. As applications, we show that all four code families are linear complementary dual (LCD) and locally recoverable (LRC), and we determine their locality parameters, identifying several infinite families that are $r$-optimal or $d$-optimal with respect to the Singleton-type bound for LRC codes.

title: A Lions lift framework for gradient and Newtonian evolutions in Wasserstein spaces
abstract: To analyze evolutions driven by functionals over the space of probability measures, one can opt for the extrinsic Lions lift approach or the intrinsic Wasserstein viewpoint with its abstract metric structure. While the latter has been a successful playground for the study of first-order gradient flows, it classically relies on $λ$-convexity, and has eluded attempts of extensions to second-order Newtonian-like dynamics. Motivated by these obstructions, we show that the extrinsic Lions lift has the full capabilities to carry out the first-order gradient-flow program, which is classically done intrinsically in the Wasserstein space. As illustrated in an example, this paves the way for a framework of gradient evolutions beyond the $λ$-convex case, which is classically demanded for energies in the Wasserstein space. Furthermore, our interpretation of the Lions lift enables the formulation of a notion of second-order Newtonian curves in the Wasserstein phase space. Such curves can be constructed through a second-order JKO-like scheme and, when applied to linear and interacting energies, naturally lead to Vlasov kinetic equations and existence of solutions thereof.

title: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
abstract: Given a quadratic number field $K$ we show that the $abc$ conjecture over $K$ implies that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$ and, hence, a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$. More generally, the same conclusions hold for an arbitrary number field $K$ provided that the $abc$ conjecture holds over $K$ and that there is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rank is positive and does not increase over $K$.

title: An Upper Bound on the Proportional Choice Number of a Graph
abstract: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. A recently proposed conjecture states that for any graph $G$ with at least one edge, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G) + \text{col}(G) - 1$, where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$ and $\text{col}(G)$ is its coloring number. In this paper, we prove this conjecture using a generalization of Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem due to Aharoni and Berger, in which one of the matroids is replaced with an abstract simplicial complex. As a consequence, we can completely determine the proportional choice number of every path: $χ_{pc}(P_1)=1$, $χ_{pc}(P_n)=2$ for $2 \leq n \leq 5$, and $χ_{pc}(P_n)=3$ for $n \geq 6$. This resolves a question about paths that has remained open since the introduction of proportional choosability.

title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdős conjecture
abstract: El-Zahar and Erdős asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors are joined by an edge.

title: On a Secretary Problem with Two Equal-Sized Pools of Candidates
abstract: This paper presents the solution of a secretary type problem where the decision maker observes a sequence of offers of two types. There are N objects of both types and these objects appear to the decision maker in random order. Objects can only be compared when they are of the same type. The objects of a given type that have already appeared can be ranked according to a complete order. Objects of different types are not comparable. On the appearance of an object, the decision maker must decide whether to accept that object (and thus stop searching) or irrevocably reject it (and thus continue searching). The goal of the decision maker is to accept an object that is the best of its type. The authors present the general form of the optimal policy and the asymptotical solution. The authors give a strong result describing whether an object of relative rank one should be accepted when the same number of objects of both types have been seen.

title: Low-dimensional optimal stopping with rank-dependent loss
abstract: Sequential selection problems with independent observable scores and rank-dependent objectives are not reducible, in general, to dynamic optimisation over a state space of fixed dimension. We consider optimal stopping problems with truncated loss structures through the lens of the planar Poisson process, where self-similarity removes the time variable and the state is reduced to the $m$ lowest scores observed so far, rescaled to the initial time. For $m=1$ the optimal rule stops at the first record below a hyperbola, which is found by a sliding-window argument. For $m=2$ we derive the equations for the boundaries of the stopping sets of $1$-records and $2$-records, solve them explicitly on a part of the state space, and express the optimal values by quadratures. The value function and the optimal strategy are characterised by a static integro-differential equation. The optimal strategies are compared with simple low-parameter rules, which are close to optimality.

title: Efficient orders for reciprocal matrices with block structure
abstract: We consider block partitioned reciprocal matrices. For these matrices, we characterize the efficient vectors whose subvectors, corresponding to principal blocks, are positive multiples of given efficient vectors for those blocks. This generalizes a prior, scalar oriented, extension theorem. Conditions are presented that guarantee the existence of efficient vectors that preserve ordinal relations associated with cross-block comparisons. The notion of order transitivity is also generalized to block reciprocal matrices. For such matrices, it is then shown that efficient vectors, with no rank reversals in positions corresponding to off-diagonal blocks, exist. The notion of uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices (all efficent vectors exhibit the same order) is also generalized in the block reciprocal setting. This class is characterized via known matrix bounds for the consistent matrices associated with efficient vectors. We also provide a graph-theoretic characterization of the existence of a positive vector that is efficient for all completions of a given partial reciprocal matrix. Based on this, we apply some of our results on ordering to such matrices.

title: A simplicial model for manifold calculus through the configuration category
abstract:
Let $M$ be a closed $d$-dimensional smooth manifold and $X:Δ^{op}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$ a finite simplicial set whose geometric realization is homeomorphic to $M$. Given the $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ of disks embedded in $M$ and the path components functor $π_0:\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$, we construct a cofinal functor $Γ_X:Δ^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ such that $X=π_0\circΓ_X$.
  This result provides an alternative construction of a simplicial model developed by Boavida de Brito, Lambrechts, Pryor and Songhafouo Tsopméné to compute the space-valued presheaf $\operatorname{Emb}(-,M):\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}$. We also extend the result to manifolds with a $G$-structure and discuss applications to manifold calculus, factorization homology, and a possible generalization to manifolds with boundary.

title: Multiplicity of positive solutions for degenerate nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problems without monotonicity of the normalized reaction
abstract: We study degenerate nonlocal Dirichlet problems driven by the $p$-Laplacian, with diffusion depending on weighted sums of integral powers of the solution. Under explicit sign, spectral and size conditions, we obtain two positive solutions for each bounded positivity interval of the diffusion coefficient with zero endpoint values. Neither monotonicity of the normalized reaction $f(x,t)/t^{p-1}$ nor uniqueness of the frozen problem is required. The proof combines Schauder's theorem on a product space of a scalar parameter and a function with subsolution bounds and an energy estimate. The multiplicity result also persists under uniformly small continuous perturbations of the nonlocal functional, including perturbations that do not preserve order.

title: Half-Line Hardy-Szegő Point Processes: Fisher-Hartwig Asymptotics and Sparse Conditioning
abstract: A horizontal window extending from a fixed positive height to infinity has infinite area but a finite expected number of Hardy-Szegő zeros. We study its zero count as the horizontal length $L$ grows. Unlike for fixed bounded-height windows, the logarithmic moment generating function has a new $θ^2\log L/(2π^2)$ term; we also identify its holomorphic order-one correction. The logarithmic term has two equal contributions: a Fisher-Hartwig jump in a canonical Wiener-Hopf model and an endpoint effect in the original Fourier-Laplace operator. This yields precise point and tail probabilities at positive count densities. We also determine the transition when a moving upper height is comparable to $L$. For sparse exact counts $n_L\to\infty$ with $n_L=o(L)$, we obtain logarithmic probability asymptotics relative to the exact void probability. We determine the void exponent and sharp asymptotics relative to the void probability for counts up to order $\log L$. Under sparse exact-count conditioning, the empirical distribution of rescaled horizontal positions and logarithmic heights converges to the uniform law on the unit square. Near distinct interior horizontal locations, the rescaled configurations converge to independent Poisson processes with uniform logarithmic-height marks.

title: Capacity-Aware Redistribution Control for Mitigation of Cascading Failures in Networks
abstract: This paper studies the control of irreversible cascading failures in networks with finite node capacities. Each node carries a nonnegative divisible quantity, referred to as load, and fails irreversibly when its load exceeds its capacity. The network dynamics are represented by topology-dependent row-stochastic matrices. When nodes fail, these matrices must be updated. However, directly deleting rows and columns corresponding to failed nodes can reduce the total load in the network. We therefore introduce a topology update that preserves unit row sums and quantifies any unserved load explicitly. We derive the resulting load-balance relation and a necessary and sufficient condition for lossless redistribution after simultaneous failures. Based on these results, we formulate a two-stage optimization problem: the first stage minimizes unserved load, and the second stage minimizes the highest capacity utilization among the surviving nodes. Simulations on grid and Barabasi-Albert networks show that, unlike the standard equal and residual-capacity redistribution approaches, the proposed method prevents secondary failures in all tested cases, with a tradeoff against served load on scale-free networks.

title: Moment approximations in optimal transport: geometric estimates and a semiclassical limit
abstract: We study finite moment approximations of linear optimization problems over measures. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the existence of discrete minimizers with a controlled number of support points, duality and $Γ$-convergence as the moment approximation is refined. This framework accommodates several transport problems, in which marginal constraints are replaced by finitely many moment constraints. For moment functions localized at scale $r_n$, we prove an estimate controlling $W_\infty$ by $W_p$ up to an additive error of order $r_n$, which also applies to discrete measures. For repulsive costs, we show that minimizers remain separated from the diagonal, uniformly in the number of moments, and we derive consequences for dual potentials. Finally, under a moment-correction assumption, we prove that the fermionic minimum energies converge in the semiclassical limit to the moment-constrained Coulomb transport value for a fixed family of moment functions.

title: Regularity and stabilization of integral closures of powers of homogeneous ideals
abstract: In this paper, we establish explicit polynomial bounds for the regularity defect and the stabilization index of integral closures of powers of arbitrary homogeneous ideals over fields of any characteristic. Specifically, let $I \subseteq K[x_{1}, \dots, x_{n}]$ be a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal generated in degrees at most $d$. We prove that $\reg \overline{I^{s}} \le ρ(I)s + d^{(n-1)2^{n}}$ for every $s \ge 1$, where $ρ(I) \le d$ denotes the eventual slope of $\reg \overline{I^{s}}$. Furthermore, the stabilization bound is polynomial in $d$ for a fixed number of variables $n$. In characteristic zero, an upper bound for the first Hilbert coefficient yields a significantly sharper exponent. Our approach relies on exact equigenerated reductions, free lattice constructions within normalized Rees algebras, monic Frobenius presentations, and Tor-module regularity controls, complemented by generic source hyperplanes that reduce the stabilization behavior to the eventual nonvanishing of graded components.

title: Unbounded traces, Connes' index theorem for measured foliations, and the Godbillon-Vey invariant in KK-theory
abstract: We prove that unbounded positive traces define KK-elements with real coefficients. Such traces naturally arise from invariant transverse measures on foliations (Connes, 1979) and, more generally, on Lie groupoids (Crainic--Mestre, 2019). As an application, we build a canonical KK-element with real coefficients whose associated map of K-groups is the Godbillon-Vey invariant as constructed by Connes. In the process, we show how Connes' index theorem for measured foliations can be deduced from the Connes-Skandalis longitudinal index theorem, using cyclic cohomology.

title: Real Frøyshov invariants and lattice homology
abstract: For a class of almost rational plumbing 4-manifolds equipped with smooth involutions, we give a description of the Real Frøyshov invariants of their boundaries in terms of lattice homology. Our approach uses the $S^1$-stable equivalence between Seiberg-Witten Floer spectra and lattice spectra constructed by Dai-Sasahira-Stoffregen, and the $\operatorname{O}(2)$-equivariant versions of these spectra developed by Kang-Park-Taniguchi. As applications, we derive a formula for these invariants for every $\operatorname{spin}^c$ structure on the double branched covers of even torus knots $T_{2p,q}$, and determine the smooth nonorientable $4$-genus of an infinite family of torus knots $T_{4,q}$.

title: Structure-Preserving PHS RBF-FD Methods for Schrodinger Equations
abstract: We develop and analyze a structure-preserving polyharmonic-spline radial-basis-function finite-difference (PHS RBF-FD) method for the two-dimensional Schrödinger equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The method combines a 29-point complete-shell stencil with odd boundary reflection to construct a symmetric discrete Laplacian. Unlike conventional nearest-neighbor RBF-FD discretizations, whose independently selected stencils do not generally preserve global symmetry, the proposed construction admits an exact discrete sine eigenbasis. We derive a Fourier-symbol representation and establish a sufficient criterion for strict negative definiteness, verified for the \(r^7+\mathbb P_4\) and \(r^{11}+\mathbb P_5\) formulations using validated coefficient calculations. The resulting symmetric spatial operator preserves discrete mass and energy under exact semidiscrete evolution, while fully discrete conservation depends on the time integrator. Numerical experiments examine kernel selection, dispersion, convergence, symmetry defects, and computational cost. Comparisons with conventional RBF-FD and fourth-order finite differences include exact Fourier modes and a variable-potential Schrödinger problem with an independently refined spectral reference. The \(r^{11}+\mathbb P_5\) formulation provides favorable accuracy in the tested problems while maintaining the desired spatial structure. The analysis establishes a connection between boundary treatment, global operator symmetry, and structure preservation in localized PHS discretizations.

title: Low Moments, Small Balls and Star Discrepancy
abstract: Let $D_P$ be the discrepancy function of a configuration $P$ of $N$ points in the $d$-dimensional unit cube, and let $\|D_P\|_q$ be its $L^q$ discrepancy. We prove that for all fixed $d\ge2$ and $0<q\le1$ the $L^q$ discrepancy of every configuration of $N\ge2$ points is at least $c_{d,q}(\log N)^{(d-1)/2}$ with a constant $c_{d,q}>0$. This bound is sharp; together with the classical results for $q>1$, it determines the minimal order of the $L^q$ discrepancy for every $0<q<\infty$ in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for $q=1$ it answers Chen's problem on the sharp lower bound for the $L^1$ discrepancy in dimension $d\ge3$. We prove the small ball inequality for Haar functions in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and for arbitrary real coefficients with the conjectured power of $n$, up to a polylogarithmic factor; here $2^{-n}$ is the smallest volume of the dyadic boxes involved. The method also extends to a class of piecewise polynomial mother functions. For the $L^\infty$ discrepancy $\|D_P\|_\infty=ND^*(P)$, where $D^*(P)$ is the star discrepancy, we prove the conjectured lower bound $c(\log N)^{3/2}$ in dimension three, and the lower bound $(\log N)^{d/2}$ up to a power of $\log\log N$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge4$. Finally, we construct $N$-point sets whose $L^\infty$ discrepancy is $O_d((\log N)^{d-1-1/16})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$; this disproves the conjectured optimality of the order $(\log N)^{d-1}$ of the classical constructions.

title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category
abstract: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.

title: The limits of inertia bounds on graph powers
abstract: We investigate the tightness of inertia and inertia-type bounds related to graph powers. This class of graphs appears in several contexts, such as the theory of distance-regular graphs, quantum information theory and coding theory. They are a priori not covered by previous separation constructions involving locally sparse graphs, see Kwan and Wigderson (2024), or Alon's pseudorandom graphs, see Elphick, Tang and Zhang (2025). Instead, we apply the latter's lower bound for complements of pseudorandom graphs to random graphs and random Cayley graph constructions, whose graph-power structure is ensured by additive combinatorial arguments. From this we are able to conclude that also for graph powers there can be a large gap between inertia bounds and the actual independence number. For the inertia-type bound, which is based on polynomials, we achieve even larger separation by considering sequences of graphs whose spectrum converges to a continuous distribution. Our methods draw from several areas of mathematics, ranging from additive combinatorics and probabilistic methods, to character sums over finite fields and arithmetic geometry.

title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvořák, Masařík, Musílek and Pangrác and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvořák, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $ε$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

title: Systole and kissing number of closed hyperbolic surfaces
abstract: In this article, we prove that if the genus of a closed hyperbolic surface $S$ is sufficiently large, then\[ \operatorname{sys}(S)\leq\frac{4}{3}\log(\operatorname{area}(S)). \] This proves a conjecture by Schmutz for large genus. The proof is based on quantitative counting estimates for closed geodesics derived from the Selberg trace formula. As a consequence, we also prove that for such surfaces, the kissing number of $S$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{Kiss}(S) \leq C\frac{\operatorname{area}(S)^{\frac{5}{3}}}{\log(\operatorname{area}(S))}, \] where $C>0$ is a constant.

title: The commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface has finitely generated abelianization
abstract: We prove that the commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface with at most one boundary component has finitely generated abelianization. The proof combines Gaifullin's finite-generation sufficient condition with the explicit generating set for the Torelli commutator subgroup due to Brendle, Margalit, and Putman.

title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
abstract: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by showing that $D(C_6^r)>5r+1$ for every $r\ge23$.

title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(τ_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.

title: The Lyapunov and uniform spectra
abstract: The \textit{Lyapunov spectrum} of a linear cocycle (or vector bundle) is the set of Lyapunov vectors with respect to all ergodic probability measures for the base topological dynamical system. This spectrum disregards trajectories that are atypical from the measure-theoretic viewpoint, and so it is in general insufficient to determine important properties of the cocycle, such as existence of dominated splittings. We resolve this deficiency by introducing a larger set which we call the \textit{uniform spectrum} of the cocycle. This definition is akin to Misiurewicz and Ziemian's rotation set. We prove several properties of the Lyapunov and uniform spectra, including relations between them. Motivated by a theorem of DeWitt and Gogolev, we consider Hölder-continuous cocycles over hyperbolic homeomorphisms and then provide bounds for the uniform spectrum in terms of the Lyapunov spectrum. We exhibit additional connections to the literature.

title: The Asymptotic Capacity of the Grabbag Channel With and Without Feedback
abstract: The grabbag channel models communication through a randomly mixed store. At each use, an input ball of one of $K$ colors is inserted into a bag containing $M$ balls, and one of the resulting $M+1$ balls is selected uniformly, observed, and removed. We show that, when $2\leq K\leq M+1$, both the capacity without feedback and the capacity with noiseless strictly causal output feedback are at most $9.77(K/(M+1))^{2/3}$, and that, when moreover $M+1\geq2^{22}$, both are at least an absolute constant times $(K/(M+1))^{2/3}$. Hence, both capacities are of order $(K/M)^{2/3}$, and of order $M^{-2/3}$ for every fixed $K$. The converse is a single bound on the information that a feedback code conveys in $n$ uses, valid for every initial state. For each initial state, it bounds the information in each output by the change of a potential of the posterior law of the state given the earlier outputs, defined through noisy cube roots of the color counts. A budget on the true state bounds the total cost of the uses in which the inserted color is rare. The lower bound uses a statistic of two output histograms whose expectation does not depend on the unknown initial composition, an outer code, and words with prescribed compositions. We also show that the channel is indecomposable and relate its capacities to the finite-state-channel information formulas.

title: Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
abstract: Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $1<p<2$. These estimates hold for every integer $k\ge2$ and every $0<β<1$ such that $k+β<s(p)$, where $s(p)$ is the optimal regularity order identified by Iwaniec and Manfredi. As consequences, we obtain decay estimates at critical points, a Liouville theorem with optimal growth exponent, and uniform higher-order estimates for the flux of planar $q$-harmonic functions with $q>2$.

title: Unique determination of ellipsoids by their intrinsic volumes
abstract: We prove that ellipsoids in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 2$, are uniquely determined by their intrinsic volumes up to congruence, resolving the conjecture posed by Gusakova and Zaporozhets in 2017.

title: Shadowing Property for Linear Operators on Banach Spaces
abstract: This note is dedicated to the study of the shadowing property for (bounded linear) operators on Banach spaces. We combine the spectral characterization of the shadowing property, recently established by Dragičević and Pituk, with tools from local spectral theory, to obtain new results and simpler proofs of known results on shadowing for operators. We also prove that the shadowing property always implies the average shadowing property and the asymptotic average shadowing property for invertible operators on Banach spaces. Furthermore, we investigate the shadowing property for some specific classes of operators, such as weighted composition operators and adjoints of multiplication operators on certain spaces of holomorphic functions.

title: Gauss--Bonnet theorem for o-minimal surfaces with isolated singularities
abstract: We study the relationship between topology and curvature of surfaces definable in an o-minimal structure. Our main result is a Gauss--Bonnet-type formula for closed (not necessarily compact) definable surfaces with finitely many singular points, expressing the Euler characteristic in terms of the total Gaussian curvature, the local densities at the singular points, and the density at infinity. As consequences, we obtain an inequality for definable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities and, for complex algebraic curves, a formula and an inequality relating the Euler characteristic, the total curvature, the multiplicities at the singular points and the degree.

title: Pair Siegel-Veech constants for branched covers of tori and Veech surfaces
abstract: For a locus $\mathcal{E}$ of branched covers of tori satisfying a monodromy assumption, we show there exists an explicit constant $c_A(\mathcal{E})$ so that the number of pairs of saddle connections on surfaces in $\mathcal{E}$ of length at most $R$ and cross product at most $A$ grows like $c_A(\mathcal{E})R^2$ for every Diophantine surface in $\mathcal{E}$; this constant is moreover piecewise linear in $A$. In particular, this covers the case of billiards on rectangles with a barrier. Similar pointwise results are shown for Veech surfaces. The proof uses work of Margulis-Mohammadi on the quantitative inhomogeneous Oppenheim conjecture.

title: Non-intrusive modal decomposition of transport-dominated data
abstract: We derive a non-intrusive modal decomposition method for positive transport-dominated datasets. We derive our method by generalizing an optimization-centric formulation of the Proper Orthogonal Decomposition. We propose two principles as a basis for this generalization. The first is that the Wasserstein distance is a more effective measure of the approximation error for transport-dominated problems, and the second is that the smoothness of the low-dimensional trajectories must be taken into account during the reconstruction. The framework is sufficiently flexible that domain-expert knowledge, in the form of inequality constraints, can be easily included. These features are demonstrated on synthetic problems and on data from a wildland fire simulation. Our method is based on the Shifted POD, which models the data as the sum of modes undergoing different coordinate transformations, but unlike the bulk of Shifted POD literature we do not assume that the correct transformation parameters are known. For a fixed number of modes, we observe a reduction of the reconstruction error of up to $43\%$ with respect to the Shifted POD baseline, despite the fact that the baseline assumes a-priori knowledge of the coordinate transformation parameters and the proposed method does not.

title: Invariant solitons of the inverse mean curvature flow in the sphere and in hyperbolic space
abstract: We study hypersurfaces of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ and of hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, $n\ge 3$, that move under the inverse mean curvature flow by a one-parameter group of isometries. No closed hypersurface has this property, and a soliton with constant mean curvature is an open subset of a horosphere. For the rotation hypersurfaces of do Carmo and Dajczer, of spherical, hyperbolic and parabolic type, the soliton equation reduces to a single ordinary differential equation, which we analyse in every dimension. In $\mathbb{H}^n$ the horosphere appears at the critical speed $λ=1$ and separates entire bowls from solitons that end at a singular $(n-2)$-sphere; each class has exactly one horospherical end, and it is the threshold between ends asymptotic to totally geodesic hypersurfaces and ends at a singular orbit. At an axis of codimension two we obtain a complete trichotomy, which changes at the speed $λ=2(n-1)$ from logarithmic spirals to cuspidal edges. In $\mathbb{S}^n$ no rotational soliton through the axis is complete, and the radius of its singular sphere satisfies $\fracπ{2}-r_+=\frac{K_n}λ\left(1-2(n-1)^2λ^{-2}\logλ\right)+O(λ^{-3})$, with $K_n=\sqrtπ\,Γ(\frac{n+1}{2})/Γ(\frac{n}{2})$. For $n=3$, the commuting pairs of Killing fields give two further classes, helicoidal and Hopf-invariant surfaces; the latter are the rotators of the inverse curve shortening flow on the round two-sphere.

title: Two almost sure upper bounds for sums of random multiplicative functions
abstract:
Let $f,g$ be a squarefree and extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions, respectively. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely
  $$\big|\sum_{n \le x}\frac{f(n)}{\sqrt{n}}\big| \ll (\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}, \qquad \big|\sum_{n\le x}g(n)\big|\ll\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}.$$
  We also show that almost surely, there exist arbitrarily large values of $x$ such that $\sum_{n \le x}\frac{f(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \gg (\log\log x)^{1/4+o(1)}$. We follow Caich and Durkan and Pearce-Crump by using a version of the Azuma--Hoeffding inequality for martingale difference sequences.

title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
abstract: We prove that, for every inclusion $M\subset P$ of countably decomposable von Neumann algebras with a normal faithful conditional expectation, $M\subset c(P)$ has the weak Dixmier property, where $c(P)$ is the continuous core of $P$. By Haagerup's characterization, we have a completely new proof of Connes' bicentralizer conjecture, independent of the recent proof of Houdayer--Marrakchi. By Marrakchi's characterization, we also prove his relative bicentralizer conjecture. We also give a new solution to Kadison's problem after Popa and Marrakchi: further assuming that $M$ and $P$ have separable preduals and $M'\cap P=\mathcal Z(M)$, then there is a maximal abelian subalgebra of $M$ that is also maximal abelian in $P$. The proofs are based on a Poisson boundary theory for general von Neumann algebras, developed here as an extension of the theory of Das--Peterson for finite von Neumann algebras. Once this theory is established, the proofs for Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem are short (around 7 pages each) and self-contained, relying only on results established by 1990. In both proofs, no separate treatment is needed for the type $\mathrm{III}_1$ case.

title: Exponential boundary stabilization of the KdV--KdV system with time-varying delay: the nonlinear case
abstract: We consider a Boussinesq system of KdV--KdV type on a bounded interval, with a boundary feedback that includes a damping term with a time-varying delayed term. Although the exponential stability of the linearized system was established in [1] by a Lyapunov approach, global existence and stabilization for the nonlinear problem remained open. Here, we prove that, for sufficiently small initial data and under a suitable restriction on the interval length, the nonlinear system admits a unique global solution whose energy decays exponentially. In particular, we provide an explicit decay rate and a quantitative smallness condition on the initial energy. Our approach combines a Lyapunov argument with well-posedness estimates that are uniform under time translations of the delay, allowing the solutions to be continued globally.

title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
abstract:
Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincaré polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$.
  Let $n\geq4$ and $W=S_n$ or $W(B_n)$. For $w\in W$ whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ satisfies $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=2$, we prove the sharp bound $[q^k]D_w(q)\leq[q^{k-1}]P_{w_0}(q)$ for $1\leq k<\ell(w)/2$.
  For every $n\geq3$ and $1\leq h\leq2n-4$, we construct an element $b=b_h^n\in W(B_n)$ with $P_{\mathrm{id},b}(q)=1+q^h$, and determine the asymmetry polynomial $D_b(q)$ and all Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,b}(q)$ for $x\leq b$.

title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
abstract: For a crystallographic root system $Φ$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}Φ$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $ρ+ λ$, where $ρ$ is the Weyl vector and $λ$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $ρ$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

title: Slope stability for normal varieties
abstract: In this expository paper, we review the theory of slope stability of torsion-free sheaves with respect to nef curve classes and extend it to normal varieties.

title: Large deviation principles for component counts in the dense regime
abstract: This paper develops large deviation principles for component counts in dense random geometric graphs. We consider a homogeneous Poisson point process on the flat \(d\)-dimensional torus and study the number of isolated components of fixed order \(k\) at connection radii above the connectivity scale. Two types of large deviation behaviour are investigated. First, we prove a Donsker--Varadhan large deviation principle in the regime where the expected number of such components tends to infinity. Second, we study the opposite extreme regime, where this expectation tends to zero, and establish fixed order tail measure limits for the associated \(k\)-component isolation-volume point process. As a consequence, we obtain functional large deviations for the moving threshold component count process.

title: Balanced Simplicial Complexes for the $γ$-Vectors of Zig-Zag Eulerian Polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we construct a simplicial complex whose $f$-vector equals the $γ$-vector of the descent polynomial of an arbitrary canonically labeled rank-one poset. As an application, we prove Petersen and Zhuang's conjecture that the $γ$-vector of the normalized zig-zag Eulerian polynomial is the $f$-vector of a balanced simplicial complex.

title: Endpoint behaviour of vertical and horizontal Riesz transforms for the flow Laplacian on homogeneous trees
abstract: We study endpoint estimates of Riesz transforms on a homogeneous tree equipped with its canonical flow measure $μ$. We prove that the known boundedness from $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ to $L^1(μ)$ of the vertical Riesz transform can not be strengthened to boundedness on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ itself. We also prove that the adjoint vertical Riesz transform is not of weak type $(1,1)$. For the scalar horizontal transforms defined by nonzero bounded coefficients with zero sum on each child set, we establish $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)\to L^1(μ)$ boundedness and show that failure to preserve cancellation on atoms prevents boundedness on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$. We then introduce a horizontal derivative based on deviations from sibling averages. Its associated Riesz transform retains the $L^p(μ)$ bounds for $1<p<\infty$ and the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate, and is bounded on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ itself. These mapping properties parallel those of horizontal Riesz transforms in the continuous setting, supporting our construction as a natural discrete analogue. These results distinguish vertical and horizontal behaviour at the endpoint and identify cancellation on sibling sets as a mechanism for Hardy-space boundedness.

title: Dual Gauss-Thakur sums for Drinfeld modules
abstract: We define dual Gauss-Thakur sums for Drinfeld modules, building on constructions of Gauss-Thakur sums due to Thakur, in the case of the Carlitz module, and Gazda and Maurischat, for general Anderson $t$-modules. Using results of Ferraro, we demonstrate that these sums can be obtained by evaluations of dual special functions at elements of finite fields. Our main results are matrix identities assembled from Gauss-Thakur sums and dual Gauss-Thakur sums in terms of multiplication coefficients for the Drinfeld module and its adjoint. We further prove determinant identities and explore connections with special Goss $L$-values and Drinfeld modular forms.

title: Infinite-dimensional invariant tori for the perturbed modified KdV equation
abstract: In this paper, we consider the perturbed modified KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6u^2u_x+\partial_x(u^5)$ on the circle, without external parameters. We prove that it admits plenty of almost periodic solutions.

title: Broximal Gradient Descent in General Norms: Convergence without Fejér Monotonicity
abstract: We study Broximal Gradient Descent in a general norm for smooth optimization over a closed convex set. Each update minimizes the linear model over the intersection of the feasible set and a norm ball. Unlike the Euclidean case with suitably restricted radii, the distance to a solution can increase, even when the squared norm is strongly convex. We instead use a comparator inequality and an observable stationarity certificate. For convex objectives, prescribed radii yield value convergence, including escape when the infimum is unattained, and a last-iterate $O(K^{-1/3})$ bound without a distance-bound assumption. A level-set distance bound gives an all-iteration $O(1/K)$ rate with calibrated radii and an asymptotic $O(\log K/K)$ rate with radii using no problem constant. Strong convexity and power growth give explicit faster envelopes and convergence of the iterates. Without convexity, a constrained Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality gives linear convergence with prescribed radii. An observable radius-halving rule needs a valid smoothness constant but neither the PL modulus nor an initial gap bound; warm starting gives logarithmic total oracle complexity in inverse accuracy. The analysis separates established local-oracle ingredients from the control of level sets, radius calibration, and accuracy-based oracle counts.

title: On the Principle of Localization on Quasi-Orbits in Crossed Products
abstract: Quasi-regular $C^*$-dynamical systems with locally closed quasi-orbits are considered. For the corresponding crossed products, a localization principle on quasi-orbits is proven. This principle reduces the study of the primitive spectrum of the original crossed product to the study of the primitive spectra of crossed products, each corresponding to its own $C^*$-dynamical system with a single quasi-orbit. Assuming that the group action on the primitive spectrum of the $C^*$-algebra in the crossed product is free, except for some fixed subset, a characterization of the spectrum of the crossed product is provided, which allows for a description of the Jacobson topology on it.

title: Variation bounds for averages over nondegenerate curves
abstract: In this article, we prove sharp variational estimates for averaging operators over non-degenerate curves in $\R^3.$ The sufficiency follows from dyadic localisation, Sobolev embedding, and local smoothing estimates, and the primary novelty of this article lies in obtaining sharp necessary conditions for variational estimates.

title: A variational approach to an anisotropic nonlocal porous medium equation with drift
abstract: We study nonlocal porous-medium equations driven by anisotropic Riesz-type repulsive interactions and an external confining potential. The pressure is determined by convolution with an interaction potential of the form $$ W(x)=|x|^{-s}Ω\left(\frac{x}{|x|}\right), \qquad d-2<s<d, $$ where $Ω$ is a smooth, even, and strictly positive angular profile. For quadratic confinement and $s\in(d-2,d)\cap(0,5]$, under suitable positivity assumptions on the anisotropic kernels, we prove that the unique energy minimizer is the only steady state among bounded continuous probability densities. We then establish the long-time convergence of global weak solutions to this equilibrium, both locally and globally in Hölder norms. To obtain these results, we derive uniform $L^p$, $L^\infty$, and Hölder estimates, adapting the regularity theory for fractional porous-medium equations to the anisotropic setting. We also construct global weak solutions through a minimizing-movement scheme in Wasserstein space, establish the corresponding energy-dissipation inequality, and prove a Talagrand-type transport inequality.

title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
abstract: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $δ>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^δ(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^δ(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{δ\to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^δ(K)) |}{δ^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $δ$ instead of $δ^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

title: On the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture
abstract: We extend our results on Zhao's conjectural basis to finite multiple zeta values modulo arbitrary prime powers and to the corresponding completed algebra. As a consequence, the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture, which gives a precise description of relations modulo arbitrary prime powers in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values, follows from the dimension and direct-sum conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values. We also prove Rosen's lifting conjecture under the dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values. The proofs use confluence relations and $p$-adic associators and do not use motivic theory.

title: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
abstract: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

title: Topological Properties of Cones with Small Entropy
abstract: We show that regular hypercones in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with small entropy have simple topology. As a result, the link of the given cone is topologically an $(n-1)-$sphere. Moreover, the space of all links whose associated cones have entropy close to 1 can be retracted onto the space of equatorial spheres, which is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^n$.

title: Global $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
abstract: In this paper, we prove that for $3\leq k\leq n-1$, continuous $k$-convex solutions of the $σ_{k}$ equation on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{3}$ domains $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $C^{3}$ boundary values and positive continuous density on $\overlineΩ$ belong to $W^{2,p}(Ω)$ for every $1<p<\infty$. If, in addition, the density is $C^α$ on $\overlineΩ$, $0<α<1$, the solutions belong to $C^{2,α}(\overlineΩ)$.

title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.

title: On the Beauville Dimension of Finite Abelian Groups
abstract: Unmixed Beauville manifolds of general type are rigid quotients of products of compact complex curves of higher genus by free diagonal actions of finite groups. Their biholomorphism classes are encoded by equivalence classes of group-theoretic data. For a finite abelian group $G$, we characterize when these data exist and determine the unmixed Beauville dimension $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)$, the minimum dimension of such a manifold arising from a diagonal action of $G$. We prove that $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)<\infty$ if and only if $\exp(G)$ is odd and greater than $3$, and the largest invariant factor of $G$ occurs at least twice. In that case, \[ \mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=\max\{\mathrm{rk}(G),\mathrm{rk}_3(G)+2\}. \] Specializing to $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=2$ recovers the classical result of Bauer, Catanese and Grunewald: the finite abelian Beauville surface groups are precisely $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$ with $n>1$ and $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Although the Beauville dimension has a geometric origin, our proof is entirely group-theoretic and combinatorial.

title: Electric combined-field-only P1 Galerkin BEM for PEC scattering with scalar Helmholtz operators
abstract: We develop a Galerkin boundary element method for the indirect electric field-only combined-field integral equation (ECFOIE) for perfectly electrically conducting obstacles with smooth surfaces. The method is free of low-frequency breakdown and of spurious resonances. It applies scalar Helmholtz operators componentwise, so that fast scalar solvers can be reused, with less memory than a Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretization. The iteration count of the Calderón-regularized ECFOIE (R-ECFOIE) is constant under mesh refinement and, with a complex-wavenumber Calderón regularizer, grows only mildly with frequency. The discretization uses continuous, nodal piecewise-linear basis functions on flat triangular meshes, with essentially as many unknowns as an RWG discretization, and tangential and normal projections and the mean curvature of the obstacle's surface carry the vector structure. On flat meshes the curvature is concentrated on the edges, and we average the edge measure obtained from the first variation of area over vertex patches, which gives sparse curvature matrices. At low frequency, four Lagrange-multiplier constraints on the induced charge and on the longitudinal dipole moments of the far field keep the R-ECFOIE accurate in the quasi-static regime, tested on scatterers eight orders of magnitude smaller than the wavelength. Under mesh refinement, the errors decrease at about second order. A Helmholtz resonator, a rounded Fichera cube, and a smoothed Stanford bunny are compared with electric field integral equation (EFIE) solutions, and the first two also with electrostatic references at extreme low frequency.

title: Singularities of ideals with minimal tangent space dimension in the Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold
abstract: We classify all singular monomial ideals in the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points on $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose tangent spaces have the minimal dimension $3d+6$. There are two families called the opera houses and rotating staircases, and we give their combinatorial and algebraic descriptions. All the opera houses are in one linkage class, and their singularities are smoothly equivalent to the vertex of a cone over the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,6) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{14}$ in its Plücker embedding. The rotating staircases split into many linkage classes and we give some examples.

title: Combinatorial Bloch-Gieseker inequalities on toric surfaces
abstract: We give a combinatorial proof of the Bloch-Gieseker inequalities in the special case of ample toric vector bundles on toric surfaces via a new rearrangement inequality for planar curves. Using this we establish the Hodge package for combinatorial analogues of cohomology rings of ample projective bundles over toric surfaces which don't appear to arise from matroidal constructions.

title: Uniformly positive entropy and mixing in minimal systems
abstract:
Every minimal system with uniformly positive entropy of order two is
  topologically mixing. In a minimal system, mixing along an infinite
  set $A\subset\N_0$ is equivalent to $\dist(T^nU,T^nV)\to0$ along $A$
  for all nonempty open $U,V$, and to unbounded complexity of each
  standard binary open cover along every infinite subset of $A$.
  For $A=\N_0$ it is also equivalent to $Δ^*$-transitivity.
  A local distance condition characterizes finite cyclic decompositions
  with mixing return maps. Such a decomposition exists precisely when,
  for each infinite $S\subset\N_0$, the closure of some proximal cell
  along $S$ has positive measure for some invariant probability.
  In a minimal weakly mixing system, for fixed infinite $S$, these cells
  are either all dense or all have closures of measure zero for every
  invariant probability. We also give proximal-cell criteria for
  Furstenberg families and mild mixing.

title: Comparing Lower and Upper Spectral Gaps of Nonnegative Symmetric Matrices
abstract:
We establish sharp estimates comparing the lower and upper spectral gaps of nonnegative symmetric matrices. Combining these comparisons with a multiplicity argument in the spirit of Li and Liu, we improve and extend earlier spectral gap comparison bounds of Saha and Li and Liu, which provide quantitative refinements of an observation of Breuillard, Green, Guralnick and Tao relating combinatorial expansion to two-sided spectral expansion. Our graph estimates hold for nonbipartite even-walk-regular graphs, which covers the classes of graphs, including vertex-transitive graphs, (twisted) Cayley graphs, and (twisted) Cayley sum graphs, investigated in previous work.
  Under an additional eigenmap assumption, we also establish quantitative two-sided comparisons between the lower and upper spectral gaps. In particular, these comparisons apply to walk-regular graphs.
